view.rationale: Despite solid restaurant-level margin expansion and improving labor costs, KRUS cut full-year revenue guidance and lowered restaurant-level operating margin outlook, citing construction/fire-inspection delays and macro pressure—clear downside to the growth narrative. Net income/EPS fell on the quarter.

Without a pre-release note or explicit consensus numbers, the setup is driven mainly by directionality: organic ASV growth re-accelerated and management reaffirmed full-year guidance, but adjusted operating margin fell ~300 bps Y/Y with compensation/investment and FX headwinds. With no clear evidence of guide upside, expected reaction is modestly positive.

Q3 results beat expectations on both sales growth and a large adjusted EPS/margin step-up, with clear productivity-driven improvement (incremental margin strong). Q4 guides sales and margin down sequentially/near-term, but this is attributed to known lapping effects; overall outlook still supports mid-teens margin path and improved cash conversion.

No pre-release note or consensus figures are provided, so beats/misses vs expectations can’t be scored quantitatively. Qualitatively, results show improving gross profit and a narrowed net loss, but guidance is described as moderate with limited forward visibility amid tariff/macro uncertainty—likely a neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so surprise timing can’t be quantified. Operationally, margins improved sequentially and backlog/orders looked solid, but fiscal 2026 delivery activity is shifting into fiscal 2027, and North American delivery forecasts remain depressed for 2026, limiting upside to a roughly median-to-slightly positive reaction.

FC lowered FY26 revenue guidance while gross margin declined year-over-year, offset by a maintained adjusted EBITDA outlook and improved deferred revenue/services booking pace toward FY27. With no pre-release note/consensus provided, the reaction skews mildly negative on the revenue cut despite cost discipline and better profitability.

With no pre-release note, expectations aren’t observable. On the facts, Q3 shows revenue down 5% YoY and operating margin contracting to 11.5% from 14% due to irrigation fixed-cost deleverage, plus continued unit-volume weakness (North America -11%, Brazil/International pressured by rates/credit). While buybacks and Infrastructure growth are positives, the underlying mix and irrigation demand appear to deteriorate, biasing reaction negative-to-neutral.

While full-year gross margin guidance was raised on mix, the near-term revenue outlook is weak: Q2 ex-Alcon sales are down ~20% YoY with continued competitive trialing expected to persist through year-end, and LDD placements were far below prior expectation (~11 vs ~25). Net: underlying demand/placement deceleration outweighs the margin upside, implying a negative-to-mildly negative reaction.

No pre-release note or reported quarter financials (revenue/EPS) were provided, so surprise vs consensus can’t be quantified. However, management’s commentary flags a pressured consumer environment with NAR categories roughly flat in dollars and Pet timing/inventory headwinds into fiscal ’27, offset by incremental positives (North America Retail base volume turning up and specific brand momentum like Love Made Fresh). Net effect is likely modestly neutral with a slightly positive bias given the early hedges/coverage and some volume stabilization.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but management lowered full-year organic growth guidance to 1%-2% and flagged continued Middle East-related headwinds into Q4. Q3 EPS was boosted by a tariff-recovery benefit, and underlying margins were pressured by mix/service dilution, offset somewhat by solid product growth and ongoing Cortland momentum.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so the beat/miss cannot be quantified. Operationally, results show mixed demand (wholesale down, retail and web up) with expanding gross margin but lower operating income as expense/income pressures offset; management’s retail margin expansion is delayed to Q4, which tempers optimism.

Despite a record Q3 and a FY26 outlook raise, the release flags worsening profitability (gross margin down sharply YoY with Q4 margin pressure) and a weaker advanced computing backdrop (Q4 and full-year hyperscale weakness with segment guidance for decline). The net effect should be mixed-to-negative given growth but decelerating/less attractive margins into Q4.

No pre-release note/consensus provided. Management reaffirmed full-year EPS but guided to the low end of the range (low-end organic sales; stronger profit improvement weighted to Q4), while PBNA margins fell ~90 bps and Q2 North America underperformed on affordability pressures; tariff refunds may support EPS but risk underlying margin pressure. Overall implies limited upside and some skepticism on near-term trajectory.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so beats/misses vs expectations can’t be quantified. However, management reported strong membership renewal (all-time high), accelerating membership monetization (Platinum mix), continued comp growth into early Q4, and expanding gross margin—suggesting a mildly positive reaction despite uncertainty on how much was already priced in.

No pre-release note or consensus is provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, demand for industrial water appears strong, but the Phase 2E lot count is materially smaller than a typical phase and the SFR program was scaled back due to regulatory uncertainty—together suggesting potential timing/volume risk that should cap upside reaction despite generally supportive commentary and guidance finishing at/above forecast.

Management guided that fiscal 2026 is not a revenue growth year and recovery is delayed to the Q4 holiday season; at the same time, Q2 revenue declined ~42% (below their own expectations) with sharp drops in conversion and AOV. Despite a strong adjusted gross margin (~62%), underlying profitability deteriorated with a swing to net loss and negative adjusted EBITDA, which should drive a negative reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so surprise scoring is limited. The quarter shows top-line growth, but margins compressed sharply (polyethylene price shock) and there’s evidence of competitive price concessions and project/invoicing timing effects; guidance is for improved sequential margins in Q4, which caps downside.

Pre-release research/consensus was not provided, so beats vs expectations are not measurable. Management did cite Q4 headwinds (input cost drag) and margin pressure from reclassifications, partially offset by strong Y/Y sales/EPS growth and operating leverage.

No pre-release consensus/option-directional expectations are provided, but the release includes meaningful negative developments: gross margin deterioration, large non-cash goodwill impairment, Atkins penetration loss tied to distribution/marketing issues, and FY26/FY27 volume headwinds from pricing elasticity. Management did not meaningfully reverse the downtrend via an outlook raise, keeping the reaction sub-median.

Adjusted EPS beat guidance and full-year organic revenue/EPS outlook was raised again, alongside 70bp margin expansion and stronger-than-expected free cash flow. Q3 guide is cautious but still growth-positive, with no explicit deterioration in demand/margins.

No pre-release consensus note was provided, so beats vs expectations can’t be quantified. However, management affirmed full-year EPS and delivered Q2 results above its initial guidance despite record fuel costs, with margin at 8.8% and Q3 operating margin guided 11-13%, which is likely supportive for a neutral-to-positive reaction.

AZZ delivered a solid, margin-expanding Q1 and raised FY2027 guidance (sales/EBITDA/EPS) alongside strong container end-market momentum and improving cash flow. However, parts of demand (Transportation and HVAC/appliances) were still down and the guidance raise magnitude is modest versus what the market likely expects given record results and low leverage, keeping the reaction to mildly positive.

No pre-release consensus or option-directional expectations were provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Reported results show margin expansion (despite tariff drag) and continued Med Tech growth with a modest FY27 revenue increase, suggesting a neutral-to-positive reaction rather than a clear upside surprise.

Without a pre-release note or consensus, expected reaction is driven by directionality: Q1 revenue fell ~32% YoY and net loss widened, with gross margin still pressured by discounting/promotions. While brand partner adds improved sequentially after the recruiting promo and expense/inventory actions helped cash, the underlying fundamentals (sales decline, margin not yet recovering) skew negative.

With no pre-release note or consensus numbers provided, the score leans on directional signals from the call: demand is strong (accelerating sales, rising contract count) and incremental margin points to eventual recovery, but near-term profitability is pressured (gross margin down, price/cost still a headwind; digital penetration guidance trimmed). Net: modestly positive/near-median reaction.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, but the call highlights constructive operating trends (8% PPNR growth, NIM 3.95% with loan yields intact, lower deposit costs, improved efficiency and strong capital). Credit costs rose due to growth and specific reserves, which tempers conviction, leading to a neutral-to-slightly positive expected reaction.

With no pre-release note, the clearest actionable items are a small NII ex-markets raise alongside a bigger expense increase (partly already booked), and better card credit (lower net charge-offs). Offsetting negatives include equities strength likely not repeating and a modest CET1 decline, which keeps the reaction closer to neutral-to-positive.

No pre-release expectations were provided, but the call flagged worsening unit/revenue trends, material gross margin compression, rising credit losses/delinquencies, and an unresolved liquidity constraint with a going-concern disclosure—more consistent with negative surprise than relief. The only clear offset was improved net leverage (lower net debt-to-receivables), but it likely doesn’t offset the deterioration in underlying performance and liquidity risk.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but management delivered strong operating leverage (efficiency ratio improved, >450 bp in 1H) and raised full-year operating leverage and NII growth guidance to the top end of the range, alongside standout IB/equities and record GWIM results—generally supportive for a positive next-day reaction.

Headline results were strong (best revenue in a decade, operating leverage, RoTCE held), but management explicitly signaled a materially weaker second half via retained full-year RoTCE target and warned markets revenues typically decline ~20% from H1 to H2—offsetting upside and likely capping the reaction. No pre-release consensus was provided, so the beat/miss vs expectations cannot be quantified.

No consensus/research note was provided, but the release contained broad-based upside drivers (record net revenues/EPS, sharply lower efficiency ratio, strong IB backlog/financing and strong AWM net inflows) plus a guidance raise for full-year fundraising; option markets were only moderately pricing a ~3% absolute move, implying room for a positive but not extreme reaction.

Management reported broad-based, record results with operating margin expansion and stronger buyback/shareholder return plans (buyback guidance raised). With no pre-release consensus provided, directionally strong fundamentals and a raised capital-return outlook point to a modestly positive reaction, though the exact magnitude is uncertain.

No pre-release consensus provided, but the release shows broad-based improvement (efficiency ratio, asset quality, record EPS, improving CRE) alongside steady NIM and a relatively constructive full-year outlook with lower net charge-offs guidance. Overall implies a modestly positive next-day reaction, though confidence is limited by missing consensus/positioning info.

The quarter improved sharply (EPS turnaround, bookings and record backlog) and the fiscal 2027 guide implies very large growth plus near-term non-GAAP pretax profitability. Offsetting negatives are full-year 2026 revenue decline and a clear gross margin compression, which likely limits upside despite strong demand signals; without a pre-release note, the size of the beat/raise vs Street is uncertain.

No pre-release note and no explicit consensus numbers provided for revenue/EPS, so surprise is hard to quantify. However, management guided to similar modest NII compression in Q3 (and flagged stabilization in Q4), and NII margin pressure was a likely key driver of a negative reaction—partially offset by ROTCE improvement toward the 17–18% target, stronger loan/deposit growth, and maintained full-year NII/noninterest expense guidance.

Raised full-year 2026 adjusted EPS floor to at least $27 (and reiterated 12%+ 2027 growth from that baseline), with Q2 EPS beating due to operating outperformance in MA/ACA. However, underlying Medicaid profitability outlook remains roughly at the trough with margins still ~-1.75% and a DC market exit adds execution risk; net reaction expected modestly positive.

No pre-release consensus or guidance targets were provided, but management reported broad-based strength across Wealth net new assets, Institutional equities performance, and upbeat NII/loan growth. Strong demand tone and capital return measures likely support a modest-to-positive reaction absent evidence of a decelerating outlook.

No consensus figures for revenue/EPS were provided, but the call emphasizes continued volume declines (6th straight year), margin compression (10–10.5% vs ~16% historically), and inflation exceeding productivity with only mid-Q2 pricing benefit—offset slightly by strong FCF conversion and a dividend cut used to fund strategy.

No pre-release note or reported revenue/EPS/explicit guidance levels were provided, so surprises are scored only on directional items from the call. The LOI scale, additional financing/downs payments, and clear overhead/liquidity runway modestly improve perceived de-risking, but the timeline into operations (2028–2030) limits how much near-term risk is removed.

No pre-release note/consensus is available to size beats vs expectations. The release shows strong loan production and efficiency, but also rising nonperforming assets and a margin guide that stays constrained as accretion burns off—likely a roughly median-to-slightly-positive reaction.

CTAS delivered strong profit and margin momentum (gross margin at/near record; incremental margins up) alongside a growth runway and a fiscal 2027 guide that implies continued margin expansion. The main offset is segment mix softness (Uniform Direct Sales down) plus a noted SAP-related gross margin headwind in Fire, which tempers upside conviction.

Raised full-year 2026 guidance with implied margin improvement, and multiple oncology launches/brands showed strong growth; however, MedTech growth decelerated (cardio/electrophysiology/Abiomed) and STELARA declined sharply, limiting the quality of the growth mix. Without consensus numbers, the reaction is judged mainly off the magnitude/direction of guidance and margin outlook.

No pre-release research note/consensus provided, so direction is judged from fundamentals only. Reported loan growth and PPNR growth are positives, but NIM compressed and fixed income revenues are expected weaker in 2H 2026; guidance was reiterated, suggesting limited upside surprise but some concern on mix/margin. Net reaction expected near median to modestly positive.

Without a pre-release note or consensus, the directional read is based on management commentary: volume growth hit a record and Dedicated reaffirmed truck guidance, but intermodal revenue per load ex-fuel was only marginally positive while Dedicated margins still face fuel and ongoing YOY pressure. Net is mildly positive/neutral-to-positive for the next day.

No pre-release expectations or consensus figures were provided, so surprises can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, the print included a record funded backlog and strong bookings, but also sharp Q4 revenue decline and an Elcom restructuring hit (including inventory write-down and foregone revenue), which likely tempers the reaction. New 3-year targets focus on gross/operating margins, but near-term revenue contraction still dominates.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, the report shows steady-to-improving credit, stable-to-positive capital return/capital position, and guidance reaffirmation for NIM/ROTCE and full-year growth, offset by softer Q3 fee/capital markets outlook. Overall expected reaction is mildly positive/neutral given reaffirmed guidance and generally constructive underlying trends, with only the known Q3 fee dip acting as a partial counterweight.

With no pre-release note or consensus provided, the key measurable delta is management raising full-year EPS guidance and operating earnings targets, alongside better-than-initial Medicare cost/mix signals (though management stressed no true inflection). The offset is mounting commercial cost trend pressure/IDR adding basis points and the persistence of Medicaid margin pressure, keeping reaction moderately positive rather than strongly bullish.

GE Aerospace delivered a broad full-year guidance raise (EPS and free cash flow) alongside strong Commercial Services growth and improving engine-shop visibility, offset by margin pressure from installed engine growth and peaking GE9X losses plus sequential spare-parts delinquency increases. With no pre-release note/consensus, the reaction is judged as modestly positive driven by the guidance/visibility improvements, but capped by underwhelming margin trajectory in the quarter.

EPS cleared the guidance midpoint ($0.99 vs $0.96) and management maintained 6% organic days-adjusted revenue growth with an improved/steady EBITA margin profile into Q3. However, underlying reported EPS includes notable disposition-related one-time benefit, and no pre-release consensus was available to quantify magnitude vs market expectations.

The quarter beat consensus and guidance with clear margin expansion (100 bps to 58%), plus Abbott raised full-year EPS guidance. Stock reaction likely moderated somewhat because the company guided persistent mid/high single-digit growth and the setup (healthy CGM and diagnostics momentum) was partly expected, but the upside EPS/raise still drives a positive next-day move.

With no pre-release note provided, the primary quantifiable incremental item is the raised full-year revenue growth outlook plus clear operating leverage (improving efficiency ratio) and expanding NIM toward a 3% 2027 path; however, the acquisition-related reserve build tied to the Amazon portfolio purchase and only modest buybacks cap upside.

Headline EPS/net earnings missed and gross margin contracted sharply (narrowing spreads + higher freight/manufacturing costs). Q4 gross margins guided to remain near current levels (only modest improvement contingent on further price realization) and shipments grew just 1.7% with wet-weather/data-center project delays—overall consistent with weak demand/earnings momentum.

No pre-release note was provided, and the call largely focused on generally maintained guidance (full-year loan growth) plus stabilization in deposit costs and NIM. The main potentially supportive item was the oil-and-gas asset sale recovery, while elevated Q2 expenses were framed as one-time noise; without consensus revenue/EPS, the expected reaction is modestly positive but low-conviction.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, but management guided to modest NII/fee growth with improving credit quality and continued operating leverage. The outlook doesn’t show a clear deceleration catalyst, supporting a mildly positive expected reaction.

Quarter results look solid with resilient margins despite a large fuel headwind and management expects material fuel recovery; however, the new Q3 EPS guide still embeds a meaningful fuel increase and full-year tightening is partly contingent on fuel normalization. With no pre-release consensus provided and the fuel-driven setup already central to the story, the net reaction is likely modest/neutral-to-positive rather than a sharp upside.

No pre-release note was provided, so surprises are scored from the call: the big positive was a favorable legacy loan trajectory versus expectation and acquisition economics (earnings/cost savings). Offsetting this, guidance/positioning suggests reduced loan-growth visibility and a more normalized noninterest income run-rate, limiting upside surprise.

No pre-release research/consensus is provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Operationally, NIM improved but loan/deposit balances declined and buybacks were explicitly less compelling at higher prices; partially offsetting expense savings and core run-rate guidance look more like cost stabilization than a clear growth re-acceleration.

Without the pre-release note/consensus, the score is driven by qualitative signals: procedures and margins were strong, but U.S. da Vinci growth moderated and management guided full-year toward the midpoint, with China still weak. The reported strength is partially offset by decelerating growth and uncertainty around I&A impact.

No pre-release consensus or bear case is provided, but the company posted record revenue/operating leverage and meaningfully raised full-year outlook for both fee revenue and NII. Despite a potential 2H moderation in markets revenue, the combination of strong organic AUM flows and a higher guidance midpoint supports a modestly positive, above-median reaction.

No consensus/estimate figures were provided, but guidance appears steady-to-supportive: Q3 growth guide (12% reported / 11% FX-neutral) and reaffirmed full-year 2026 growth (13%-14%). Management also highlighted improving season-2 falloff vs prior concerns and ongoing subscriber/viewership scale, which should temper downside risk; however, underlying reported vs expected revenue/EPS cannot be scored.

Headline quarter and Aluminum segment results were strong/record, but Alcoa lowered full-year alumina production and shipment guidance due to operational disruptions (Pinjarra instability, cyclone gas curtailment). With the lack of a pre-release note or consensus figures, reaction is modeled as modestly positive-to-neutral despite the guidance cut.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so directional scoring relies on the mix of results: strong earnings/ROTCE and fee strength were offset by guidance trims to net interest income/revenue and a continued NIM decline. Overall setup looks close to neutral with modest upside tilt, but confidence is limited by missing consensus expectations.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so surprises vs expectations are not quantifiable. Operationally, the quarter showed margin expansion and strong cash flow, but the company reiterated flat organic sales with a tougher light-vehicle production assumption and disclosed meaningful restructuring charges for Turkey, tempering the outlook despite profitability step-ups expected in Q4.

Headline revenue/EPS were strong, but management lowered full-year NII guidance and provision guidance ranges—both key drivers for bank earnings power. With NII slightly below guidance and CRE payoffs creating near-term yield headwinds, the net surprise vs what the market already expected is hard to pin down without consensus.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, but management reaffirmed full-year loan growth (mid-single digits) and described stable NIM, while deposits and margin outlook look supported by the BOH conversion and acquisition-related costs rolling off in Q3. Underlying credit provisions were modest, but organic growth remains limited and payoffs/elevated paydowns persist, keeping the reaction near-neutral.

No pre-release note and no consensus numbers provided for reported revenue/EPS, so the surprise assessment is limited to guidance tone. Management reaffirmed being at the top end of the 2026 net interest income growth range and signaled continued progress on positive operating leverage, which is modestly supportive. Offsetting negatives include one-to-four construction credit deterioration (a full migration to nonperforming status with specific reserve) and potential timing extension into next year for resolution, which likely caps upside.

Headline EPS benefited from merger/after-tax charges, but underlying performance appears supported by improving credit (net charge-off ratio) and a raised NII and noninterest income outlook alongside restored margin expansion. The key offsets are evidence of merger-related cost pressure and a tighter credit outlook narrative (second-half charge guidance reset).

No pre-release note/consensus was provided. The print highlighted strong core ROE (above long-term target), improving combined ratio, record profitability across segments, and a $1.5B capital return, but management also signaled some pricing softness (auto flat renewal, homeowners down) and maintained uncertainty reserves, limiting upside confidence.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, but the release shows clear operating leverage (revenue +5% while opex +3%) and strong net inflows/AUM growth, partially offset by weaker 1-year investment performance (41% outperforming). Guidance commentary is largely structural (tax rate/compensation/expense growth) rather than a clear beat-or-miss outlook driver.

No pre-release note or consensus metrics were provided, so surprise scoring vs expectations is largely unanchored. The call did, however, indicate broadly positive credit normalization (improving charge-offs and NPL metrics) alongside mixed macro/earnings drivers (NIM slightly down, income growth guided to low end), leading to a modestly positive but not strong reaction profile.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so surprises are inferred from qualitative themes only. Management reaffirmed Q4 2026 NIM guidance at likely low end and guided 2026 loan growth to be mixed (CRE/Construction flat-to-low-single-digit decline, C&I high mid-single-digit growth) while improving pipeline and maintaining low charge-offs; modestly positive but not strong given margin looks to be at the low end.

Headline results were reported as beating Wall Street with a very large adjusted EBITDA and margin expansion, alongside strong attendance growth. However, full-year cash-flow positivity is still not achieved and leverage only recently improved (still targeting ~3x), which limits upside in a market that likely already expected progress.

No pre-release note or explicit consensus figures were provided. Reported Q1 sales landed near the top end of prior guidance and gross margin expanded, but Q2 guidance included supply chain/international freight risk; net effect is modestly positive rather than a clear beat-and-raise surprise.

No pre-release note or consensus/guidance figures were provided, so beats/misses vs expectations can’t be quantified. Operationally, WRB reported record net investment income, improved combined ratio ex-cat, and management reiterated expense ratio durability (<=30%), supporting a modestly positive reaction absent evidence of deceleration in the underlying drivers.

No pre-release consensus to quantify beats/misses. Underlying adjusted EPS grew 10% with stable/strong NIM and low charge-offs, but the call also highlighted ongoing deposit competition (rising L/D ratio) and limited share repurchases, which tempers upside. With no clear guidance raise (operating leverage reaffirmed), reaction is likely near-median.

No pre-release note or consensus was provided, but the call highlighted broadly based loan growth with record pipeline, continued NIM expansion, and improving asset quality—partly offset by deposit growth still constrained and efficiency expected to be harder to sustain below 30%. Overall setup suggests a modestly positive reaction rather than a major repricing.

No consensus note was provided and EPS/revenue aren’t specified, but the key datapoint is the miss in U.S. same-store sales (+0.1%) driven by controllable premium/ticket weakness. Management maintained full-year guidance while trimming U.S. net store growth to ~175, signaling pipeline/macro and profitability strain persist—likely capping upside after a softer print.

No pre-release note or consensus provided for revenue/EPS, but management raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance (clear positive) and reported solid cash conversion. Offsetting factors include reported revenue timing delays in bioprocessing (partial timing miss) and full-year bioprocessing growth headwinds due to shipment shifts into 2027.

No pre-release consensus/option directional earnings expectation is provided, but the release guided to nearly 10% Q3 sequential growth and >$600M 2026 revenue plus raised long-term targets—offset by GAAP EPS uplift largely from a tax benefit and management’s admission that product gross margins declined (relocation costs) despite higher consolidated margin. Net: modestly positive but not a clear upside shock.

No pre-release note and no consensus/revenue/EPS expectations provided, so surprise scoring is limited. Management raised/narrowed full-year EPS to $9.25–$9.50, which is supportive, but the sequential NIM decline (-42 bps) and commentary about elevated payment rates and back-half provisions being more growth-driven add caution, keeping the reaction near-median.

Headline Q2 beat guidance with improving software/service gross margin and better expense leverage, while Q3 revenue guidance (4% at midpoint) and full-year revenue at the top of the growth range point to continued execution. Main offset is appliance gross margin deterioration from higher memory costs, though management frames it as bottoming in Q3 and gross-profit-neutral over time.

Headline margins were better (home sales gross margin above the top end of guidance), but the key negative is the full-year delivery guidance cut (~3%) tied to softer demand and a higher cancellation rate plus rising SG&A deleverage. Q4 guide still implies modest gross margin/pretax margin and demand qualification issues; overall skews negative versus expectations.

Q2 beat vs the April guidance midpoint (revenue +$5m; adj EPS +$0.05) alongside a 120 bps expansion in ex-FICO EBITDA margin, which supports an overall positive reaction. Partially offsetting: EWS government revenue -4% and mortgage-rate-driven weakening in U.S. mortgage origination assumptions (mortgage revenue guide just above 20%), plus a $40m legal settlement charge and slower buyback cadence to fund M&A; net effect looks modestly constructive rather than a major upside shock.

GM raised full-year 2026 guidance again with improving adjusted margins (NA back in target range) and record first-half EPS, plus better expected EV-loss and warranty-cost trajectories. Offsetting negatives include additional EV-related restructuring charges and a clearly weaker-than-normal Q4 vehicle outlook tied to launch costs/volume headwinds.

Headline Q2 sales and adjusted EPS were modestly positive, with clear margin expansion in the Motion/industrial segment. However, management reiterated full-year EPS guidance while flagging additional Iran-related headwinds and lowering the automotive outlook by ~0.5pp with ongoing separation-related costs—offsetting confidence that would otherwise support a strong positive repricing.

Reported revenue growth and Wizards-led demand strength supported a full-year Wizards outlook raise (low-double-digit CC growth) and higher margin/EBITDA targets, but adjusted EPS was held back by a large non-cash impairment and management guided to low single-digit Q4 Magic revenue decline. Cyber incident losses were less than the prior estimate and operations recovered early, providing partial relief, keeping the net reaction modestly positive.

No pre-release consensus figures were provided, but management raised full-year earning asset growth and tightened credit (NCO) range, while NIM guidance was held and originations are expected to moderate in the back half. Net: overall execution/supportive guidance but some growth deceleration risk limits upside reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus is available, so surprises are inferred from the call: NIM expanded and management guided NIM slightly higher (2.75% Q3, 2.80% Q4), supporting an upbeat near-term earnings power view. However, credit is mixed (nonaccruing improved but past due surged due to a single CRE office loan), limiting upside conviction; growth guidance remains mid-single-digit full-year, suggesting no major acceleration catalyst.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so comparisons are limited. Management guided tighter/toward the higher end on loan growth and strengthened outlook for NII/NIM while credit quality appears stable/improving; however, deposit-cost pressure and only modest improvement in core NIM temper the upside.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, but the company raised full-year revenue and net interest income guidance and upgraded loan-growth targets, alongside an expanding NIM guide. Offsetting factors include softer-than-expected investment banking/debt fees and rising nonperforming assets.

No pre-release note/consensus is provided, but the full-year adjusted EPS guide was raised (positive) while the Q3 guide implies sequential EPS decline and management flagged worsening H2 conflict costs plus a pressured Americas segment income outcome—offsetting the headline raise.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so relative beats/misses can’t be quantified. Directionally, results show continued NIM expansion and improving organic loan growth, while guided margin compression from Navitas reinvestment is largely expected and largely offset by underlying widening.

Q2 organic growth and margin expanded well ahead of expectations, and full-year organic growth and EPS guidance were raised broadly with improved growth-to-market and backlog/orders strength. No meaningful incremental negatives were flagged, supporting a strong positive reaction despite some acknowledged consumer weakness and tariff/input headwinds being known.

No pre-release consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Guidance indicates sequential revenue softness (Q3 C&P flat to down 2%, D&E down 3-5%) but margin improvement (125-175 bps / 25-75 bps) and intact international growth engines, which likely supports a modestly positive reaction absent a clear miss/bear-case risk.

Q2 shows broad-based improvement with operating margin expansion and strong North America Utility demand, and management raised full-year net sales/EPS guidance. However, Telecom weakness persists and infrastructure is facing ongoing cost pressure (steel/diesel) with agriculture internationally still hit by Middle East delays—limiting the upside reaction absent consensus benchmarks and given the mixed segment mix.

Even without consensus inputs, the release shows strong demand/backlog and a full-year guidance raise. However, EPS upside is heavily influenced by discrete tax/one-time investment gain items and margins are pressured by unfavorable EAC adjustments plus lowered Space margin guidance—muting the quality of the beat and likely limiting upside reaction.

No pre-release note was provided, so beats vs consensus are not measurable. However, management delivered clearly strong operating momentum (NIM expansion guided higher in H2, exceptionally low credit losses/NPAs, and strong commercial/treasury fee growth) alongside maintained full-year loan growth guidance, which should be modestly supportive for the stock absent valuation/positioning context.

Strong Q2 momentum in organic growth and record asset-based fee/ETF AUM inflows, but the next-two-quarter sustainability & climate net sales guide is roughly flat-to-negative, and the company is raising expense guidance (with acquisition-driven cost/d&a/interest effects). Net effect likely modestly positive versus market expectations given lack of pre-release consensus info.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but the release includes a clear NIM guidance raise for 2H26 (second consecutive increase) alongside improving capital and efficiency. Offsetting negatives include rising net charge-offs and noninterest expense pressure with meaningful nonrecurring operational charges, so the reaction is modestly positive rather than outsized.

EPS beat was partially offset by a disclosed strategic-securities sale loss, but underlying credit metrics (declining provision and improving net charge-offs) supported the result. Guidance is reiterated (no raise/cut provided), while criticized loans increased—limiting upside to a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

Credit remained strong and provision normalized lower, but NIM expansion looks transitional: management guided NIM down to ~3.45% in Q3 amid deposit cost pressure and higher brokered reliance for funding, offsetting growth quality for near-term sentiment.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. On-call commentary indicates continued margin improvement (pretax +80 bps, gross margin slightly higher) and liquidity/visibility remain solid, but gross margin was still described as at the low end of its range due to mix/slower absorption and growth/runway commentary highlights execution dependence (slower absorption; development cycle timing). Guidance was maintained.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so surprises are based on guidance/mix of disclosures. Operating results appear supported by reaffirmed guidance, credit metrics meeting targets, and continued progress on CVOW, but the CVOW schedule push-out (+6 months) and cost estimate increase are clear offsets that likely cap upside.

Reported Q2 performance and incremental margins were strong, and full-year 2026 guidance was raised with a substantial leverage improvement and very high book-to-bill. Without a pre-release consensus note, quantifyable beats vs expectations are unknown, but the combination of raise + strong demand points to a modestly positive reaction.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided for revenue/EPS or for the CapEx/production assumptions, but management delivered broadly positive operational updates (higher upstream volumes, record refinery throughput), aggressive deleveraging, early/structural cost-savings delivery, and an otherwise reaffirmed strategic outlook. Net: likely modestly positive reaction rather than a strong beat-and-raise given lack of benchmarked expectations and no clear guidance upshift.

Without a pre-release note or consensus figures, the directional call is driven by guidance/mix: Q3 adjusted EPS implies a meaningful sequential decline (even with tariff refunds), and management flagged a potentially larger-than-normal seasonal drop and step-up in inflation/costs. Despite margin expansion and strong Q2, the guide tone skews negative.

No pre-release research note or consensus figures were provided, limiting surprise scoring versus expectations. The release does show broadly expanding gross margins, record profitability for the quarter, and aggressive buybacks exceeding prior-year totals, which should be supportive absent evidence of decelerating demand or a cut/trim in outlook.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so surprise vs expectations cannot be quantified. Directionally, the print includes strong Engineered Solutions margin/cash generation, but guidance implicitly reflects ongoing Consumer & Specialties margin pressure from a price/cost lag and a reserve charge in the quarter, keeping the near-term outlook mixed and limiting upside reaction.

EPS was explicitly “in line with expectations,” and full-year 2026 guidance was reaffirmed with no incremental raise/cut. Demand commentary around industrial and data center growth is supportive, but there’s no quantified beat to drive a clear upside surprise.

No pre-release note/consensus provided. Reported GAAP and non-GAAP EPS were explicitly in line with guidance, with revenue effectively flat YoY during a known 3860-to-3870 transition. The key negatives are margin contraction tied to the 3870 ramp; the positives are strong 3870 backlog (bookings > shipments) and record MRI-compatible monitors sales, while management reaffirmed full-year guidance.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so beats/misses can’t be scored on reported revenue/EPS. The call did show credit pressure (reserve build, criticized/classified rising) alongside improving NIM and cost guidance downshift, which likely nets to a modestly positive, near-median reaction rather than a strong repricing.

No pre-release consensus numbers were provided, but the call highlighted strong underlying momentum (record AUM, solid net inflows, and continued margin expansion). The notable item for sentiment is guidance for diluted shares and interest income being lowered (capital reallocated to buybacks), which is more of a financial-structure/assumption change than demand deterioration; net reaction is roughly neutral-to-slightly positive.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so surprise is largely unobservable. Operationally, Q1 margins improved but guidance implies sequential margin compression in Q2 (normalized gross margin ~46% with one-time refunds and then lower guided margins), partially offset by strong demand and FCF/deleveraging; net reaction expected to be modestly positive.

Revenue and shipments were highlighted as record-setting and backlog/orders strengthened, but EPS/net income declined and gross margin contracted (COGS pressure and higher SG&A). Without consensus or guidance details, the likely reaction is mixed-to-neutral rather than a clear beat/raise setup.

With no pre-release note or consensus provided, the only directional read comes from fundamentals: underlying P&C profitability deteriorated materially (combined ratio 94.2%, loss ratio +2.6 pts) while retention softened (<80% again) and international rates remained down in a competitive market. Specialty new business growth is positive, but the underwriting trend and portfolio walk-away outweigh it, implying a below-median reaction.

TWST delivered a modest Q3 revenue beat and, more importantly versus the pre-release setup, raised FY26 revenue guidance (to $456–457M) and guided Q4 to ~25% YoY growth—addressing the note’s main bearish risk of flat/strained H2. Gross margin improved sequentially and AI/therapeutics and AI-enabled order growth confidence stayed intact, with no new negative demand signals disclosed.

KRYS delivered roughly in-line revenue and EPS versus the note’s anchored consensus ($119M / $1.70), while gross margin expanded to 95% and U.S. reimbursement approvals exceeded the penetration path. The main negative was Europe/Japan being held back by a reserve for German pricing negotiations (flat ex-Q/Q), which the market had flagged as the key swing factor; guidance was reaffirmed with no new upside to re-rate fundamentals.

With the note flagging that a ~15–19% revenue beat looked unlikely and that per-BTC accretion had likely decelerated, the reported ~8% revenue growth to ~$67M looks broadly in-family (headline EPS is unavailable/placeholder). The stock still showed improved BTC-per-share/reserve growth and record production, but gross margin compressed to ~49% as realized BTC price fell, leaving a mixed-but-not-worse setup for the next-day move.

Revenue and the key driver (global + U.S. BRIUMVI guidance) came in better than the pre-release yardstick, and management reiterated a confident growth path (U.S. exit >$250M quarterly; 1B annualized). EPS remains low but is consistent with the pre-noted EPS-definition issues, so the market should focus on the raised guidance and underlying operating setup (manufacturing charges largely excluded).

Q3 headlines missed on EPS (and revenue was slightly below consensus) while—more importantly—full-year adjusted operating income was cut to $2.1–$2.3B with a worse beef-loss outlook ($500–$650M), signaling margin pressure despite solid chicken gains. With the stock/quarter setup already not implying a high beat probability, the guidance reset drives a negative reaction.

The quarter beat on adjusted EPS at the top end of guidance, supported by expanding gross margin from the Fuel for Growth program, but demand was mixed (BSG comps down) and full-year guidance was essentially a modest tightening with comparable sales slightly less favorable than prior. Net: positive but not a major upside catalyst given the market’s expectation that SBH would largely execute at guidance.

Q2 EPS and fees beat the setup (EPS $3.19 vs $3.06 cons; fees $1.58B up 13% vs the note’s in-range cards/RevPAR mix). However, the release is offset by a still-unfavorable near-term demand/earnings path: Middle East remains a major headwind (RevPAR -43% in Q2) and net rooms growth shifts toward the low end due to construction delays, plus Q4 headwinds and the new incentive adds cost line pressure. Guidance was raised (FY RevPAR +3% to +3.5%; Q3 up 3.5% to 4%), but the market appears to have expected a decent World Cup/fee backdrop, keeping the reaction closer to neutral-to-mildly positive.

With no meaningful published consensus, the yardstick is mainly directional vs the prior quarter and the weak principal-transaction backdrop in the note. Underlying profitability improved materially (adjusted pretax more than doubled) alongside higher IB/new issue and trading, though equity-method losses widened—net suggests a modestly positive reaction rather than a runaway beat given the lack of consensus and small-cap noise.

Q2 results beat consensus on both revenue and EPS, with expanding adjusted EBITDA margin (up 150 bps) and record occupancy/yields despite higher fuel costs. More importantly, FY2026 revenue guidance is raised to $830–$860M and net yield growth is lifted, while adjusted EBITDA guidance is maintained—supportive for a stock already near highs.

Q2 operating metrics outperformed the flagged low-bar setup (EBITDA 314 vs ~295–305 guided range; gross adjusted EBITDA margin ~85% vs 75% target; volumes boosted by third-party inflows), but headline financial guidance was largely unchanged and the Q3 outlook is roughly flat while underlying free cash flow is expected to decline further on higher capex. Also, there were minor one-time credits driving some margin strength, and no buyback occurred in Q2 (debt paydown instead).

The note did not identify a clear EPS/revenue setup for this quarter, and the call delivered no concrete EPS/revenue figures versus consensus. However, management did reaffirm utility EPS guidance and flagged removal/pausing of the 500MW data-center plan (capital plan impact) and expects difficulty in the Washington settlement process—incrementally worse growth/visibility than implied by the earlier pipeline discussion—offset by contained wildfire financial exposure and cost-recovery petition intent.

AEIS delivered a clear underlying beat with record revenue/EPS, sharply higher gross margin, and raised full-year growth into the mid-30s plus stronger data-center growth; Q3 guide also supports continued records. The main offset is that 2026 cash/inventory/capex intensity (and the inventory build) leaves some near-term execution risk despite the strong operating leverage.

With no pre-release note, expectations are inferred from the mix of results: gross margin improved, but guidance for 2026 revenue was lowered and cost structure worsened (S&M and G&A up sharply), alongside continued heavy cash burn. The lowered outlook and margin/cost offset likely weigh more for near-term reaction.

Q2 results beat revenue and improved margins/EBITDA, plus management reported record awards ($1.8B) and a constructive data-center pipeline outlook. EPS landed exactly at consensus (non-GAAP $0.20) while the full-year non-GAAP EPS range was raised, but the main upside driver appears tied to the assumed tax benefit rate change and near-term financial impact is guided as limited for data centers, tempering the reaction.

No consensus/research note provided for revenue/EPS, but the call highlighted materially lower OpEx (down ~25–24% YoY in Q2/1H and targeting ~35% OpEx per barrel in 2026), strong Jubilee performance (J76 top-end; production up ~18% H1), and balance-sheet progress (net debt ~15% down). Activity pause from Winterfell #5 casing issues is a negative, but management says no material daily production impact. Overall, the news flow is more constructive than typical, implying a modestly positive reaction.

Headline results were solid versus a seasonally tricky setup, and FY guidance was raised. However, WTA margins declined (acquisition + timing/mix) and EPS guidance is shaped by a higher reliance on the Q3 shipment/margin normalization narrative, limiting upside surprise durability despite the guidance raise.

No pre-release note or consensus/option expectations were provided, so surprise scoring is limited. Reported results showed strong revenue and adjusted EBITDA growth with margin expansion and continued carrier ramp/Smart Campaign traction; however, Q3 revenue/EBITDA growth decelerates vs Q2, with incremental opex for AI-first products likely capping near-term upside.

Most of the upside/strength was already pre-announced in the 7/15 preliminary, and Q2 EPS largely lands within the pre-disclosed range. The key incremental catalyst is the raised full-year guidance plus a stronger-than-prior tone on Q3 Ocean operating income, which should be modestly supportive but not a major upside shock given positioning and prior disclosure.

No pre-release research/consensus provided. However, management cites revenue beating expectations and adjusted EBITDA materially above the guidance midpoint with an improving margin profile. The key offset is DTC revenue and ad/other revenue declines, plus Q3 guide implying only modest YoY growth at the midpoint with a sequential dip from deal-day timing.

Revenue/transactions came in slightly below Q2 guidance, but management highlighted substantial operational improvements (margin rebound, aged inventory largely cleared, faster sale velocity) and guided a narrower adjusted EBITDA loss with higher expected Q3 volume. Overall setup suggests a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction given the revenue/volume miss offset by improving trajectory.

Revenue was in guidance and unchanged on an underlying-volume decline (active coaches -48.7% YoY) with gross margin compressing. While EPS exceeded the guided range and the company reaffirmed a full-year return-to-profitability target by Q4, the lack of quantified Catalyst savings and ongoing margin pressure temper upside.

With no pre-release yardstick, the scoring relies on qualitative items. Procedure demand and physician growth were strong, and adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to ~5.1% (revenue outpacing opex). The guidance raise is modest (low end lifted) but offset by commentary on higher cash flow variability tied to capex/capacity and HQ buildout.

No financials/guidance were provided, so the read-through is mainly operational and clinical. Enrollment and retention in EMPEROR appear strong (162 enrolled in 10 months, zero discontinuations; 60 patients completed week 28 primary endpoint visit), and the company reiterates a rolling NDA starting Q1 2027 with potential early-2028 launch—overall a modestly positive outcome vs what the market typically expects for biotech program progress absent a pre-release yardstick.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so the reaction is anchored to qualitative factors. Results were described as beating revenue guidance and returning to profitability a quarter early, but the key structural driver (outpatient genome collection rate) remains weak (~32%) and management guided Q3 collections to stay flat with the largest improvement pushed to Q4/2027—limiting upside.

With no pre-release note and no explicit consensus figures provided, the best-supported call is the qualitative setup: Q2 growth was strong and management raised full-year guidance, but bookings/book-to-bill are currently weak on a quarterly basis (0.5x) even as the 12-month ratio remains healthy, and there is a sizable Kuwait/LOGCAP revenue headwind later in the year. Net: moderate positive reaction expected, tempered by the mixed demand/billings signals.

Q2 revenue landed essentially in-line and FY2026 guidance was reiterated (key watch item stayed stable). Underlying operating performance/diversification signals were positive (non-Pay-TV +54%, record new customers, 6 license deals, strong semiconductor trajectory), which should offset the market’s recent pattern of selling headline beats. No clear negative guidance or margin deterioration was indicated, implying a near-median reaction.

Results modestly beat on revenue and EPS was roughly in-line (non-GAAP slightly below the note’s non-GAAP consensus estimate). The key swing is guidance: FY2026 revenue was raised to $13.1–$13.2B versus expectations consistent with the note, but margin outlook/operating cost pressure (SG&A +45% YoY) and a negative guidance nuance for JOURNAVX gross-to-net normalization (pushed to 1H’27) temper the upside, keeping the net reaction near neutral. Underlying growth is supported by ALYFTREK and strong CASGEVY/JOURNAVX adoption, but pricing/coverage dynamics introduce a partial offset.

No revenue/EPS prints or explicit consensus levels were provided, so the main signal comes from the forward outlook: fiscal 2027 organic sales flat-to-up slightly with a slower Q1 and margin temporarily pressured to ~42% due to materially higher commodity/supply chain inflation. Given the modest demand tone and margin headwind (first-half concentrated), the reaction is expected to be slightly negative to near-median.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. The release shows a strong sequential revenue/EPS quarter and upward-looking Q3 guide (supporting a neutral-to-slightly positive reaction), but underlying profitability is still below the company’s 20% gross-margin target and cash flow turned negative on inventory build (capping upside).

Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS were essentially in line with consensus in the pre-release note, but management raised full-year EPS and free cash flow and lifted commercial revenue growth guidance. The key offset was a lowered government revenue growth outlook (high single digits vs low teens) alongside only modest sequential backlog and ongoing margin/cost watch, keeping the net reaction modestly positive rather than strong.

Strong profitability upside (EBITDA margin +1,200 bps to 30%) plus a meaningful full-year revenue and margin guide raise, supported by a very large CoreWeave contract and sharply increased RPO. The main offset is caution around near-term gross margin timing and higher 2026 CapEx/lease intensity, but the overall risk/reward improves versus what options typically price given the 18% revenue growth and visibility uplift.

Headline revenue/EPS and a sizable adjusted FCF beat versus consensus, plus a full-year net sales/EBITDA/FCF raise. However, the note already framed a likely defense-support backdrop and emphasized that commodity-driven margin compression could be a headwind; management also highlighted cost pressure (recoverable with lag), tempering the quality of the margin story and keeping the reaction near positive-but-not-stellar.

PAY delivered a clear beat on Q2 revenue and EPS and raised FY revenue/EBITDA above consensus. However, the company also guided Q3 to decelerating growth (15.2% and 18.5% EBITDA at the midpoint) and contribution margin ticked down with added enterprise billers—muting what would otherwise be a larger upside reaction given valuation/prior run-up risk.

With no pre-release note and reported Q2 being above guidance midpoints, the main observable upside is a strong Q3 gross margin step-up guide (to 40–42%) plus indications of accelerating AI data center demand (Other up 34% sequentially) and record FCF margin. High-priced-for-growth elements (utilization jump, utilization-driven margin expansion) keep the reaction from being extreme, but the guide supports a moderately positive move.

Q2 revenue and EPS were below the pre-release consensus, while the key message was continued (and quantified) reimbursement/coding/WISeR disruption ($40M in Q2; $120M–$130M full-year impact) plus restructuring charges. Although full-year revenue guidance was narrowed/raised vs the prior range in the quarter, the new outlook still implies negative growth and profitability tightening (adjusted op margin guide moved up only to 4-6% from the earlier ~2-4%, but restructuring and break-even Q3 messaging keep sentiment guarded).

Headline results/margins beat and full-year adj. EBITDA guidance was raised, but the key cloud growth outlook was cut (18% FY) alongside signs of sales-cycle elongation and sequential deceleration in scaled customer growth—muting upside despite the raise.

Revenue, U.S. commercial, TCV, and net retention beat the pre-release yardstick, and guidance was raised materially (largest ever raise). However, adjusted gross margin declined (government cloud hosting) and management flagged a notable Q3 expense ramp, which tempers the upside on an otherwise richly valued, narrative-driven stock.

Q2 revenue and profitability came in stronger than expectations (ad growth plus a much bigger other-revenue surge) and EBITDA exceeded the period’s implied level; the main incremental positives are operating leverage (58% gross margin, $250M adj. EBITDA) and a clearly stronger engagement backdrop (DAU/MAU). The biggest offset is the Q3 top-line guide still has tough comps and the company raised full-year infrastructure spend, which can limit upside to longer-term margins despite improved cash flow.

No pre-release consensus provided for revenue/EPS, but the company delivered clear underlying operating momentum (Q2 revenue +18%, adj. EBITDA margin +180 bps) and raised full-year 2026 guidance (midpoints +$75M revenue / +$25M EBITDA). Key offset: UFC Freedom 250 produced an anticipated margin drag and not all segments were immediately additive, keeping reaction moderately positive rather than strong.

Headline EPS beat was driven meaningfully by one-time tariff refunds and tax effects, but underlying margin strength (29.3% vs 27% assumption) and a raised FY organic growth guide (to 4–5%) support the key back-half story. Demand/portfolio color improved (strong instrument backlog; Diagnostics strong), partially offset by Life Sciences decline and Signals comp-driven weakness (software down ~20% in Q2).

EPS was essentially in-line vs the ~$1.65–$1.66 expectation, and the main guidance change was a tighter range (high-end lowered vs prior) plus higher tax rate—overall not a clean upside catalyst. However, Battery Materials expectations remained supportive and the stock has been positioned as a “meet-the-roadmap” setup, limiting the downside. Net: modestly negative/neutral reaction profile, not a strong beat-and-raise outcome.

Headline P&L was dominated by non-cash warrant remeasurement, but the underlying revenue came in below the very uncertain trough-quarter consensus. Offsetting positives included better-than-expected early Black Pearl rent commencement/capacity delivery and improved project financing terms/oversubscription; however, the call also flagged ERCOT batch timing uncertainty and continued lack of near-term HPC ramp revenue visibility, leaving the stock near the note’s base-case rather than a clean beat-and-raise.

Headline Q2 revenue far exceeded the preview’s $32.5M modeled Rigel-driven number, but the key equity bear case indicator worsened: ARV-102 U.S. hold effectively extended with Phase Ib now expected in 2027 vs 2026. Guidance/trajectory for the most valuable clinical catalyst slipped, which should dominate the muted-to-negative reaction despite the revenue upside. Underlying operating costs improved (R&D down) but the delay is a rerating risk.

Underlying Q2 beat is decent (adj EPS $1.88 vs $1.76 expected) and EBITDA/margin expanded, but the note flagged that the market primarily trades the FY guide—and consensus was already at the top end. Management did raise FY26 EPS to a midpoint of $7.24 (above the $7.14 consensus), which is supportive. However, water was still only low single digits with Middle East delays and full-year Water outlook was cut to low-to-mid single digits, offsetting part of the raise.

No pre-release expectations were provided, but the call signaled weaker underlying demand (volume softness, Light Duty deleverage) and a cut to full-year net sales growth guidance (3%-5% vs 7%-9%). Although headline EPS and operating margin benefited from a large IEEPA tariff refund, the comparable EPS and comparable operating margin deteriorated, likely weighing on the stock despite higher headline EPS guidance.

DOCN printed a modest revenue and large EPS beat versus a tape that was already positioned around the July pre-announcement, and—more importantly—raised FY26 revenue guidance to $1.17–$1.18B with a 35%+ Q4 exit and strong RPO quality (>$800M, 3.7-year average life). Profitability stayed strong (~40% adj. EBITDA), and the funding/capex narrative (equitized converts, ~0.7x net leverage) mitigated the main bear-case tail risk.

Headline cash/liquidity and burn guidance land broadly in-line with the note (funded through 2028 reiterated; FY26 cash consumption near the midpoint). Positives came from lower Q2 R&D and additional LOIs/backlog headroom, but the key negative was that full transition slipped from Q3 to Q4 (incremental schedule slippage beyond what was feared), which weighs on sentiment more than the loss/burn details help.

Q2 results beat consensus on both revenue and non-GAAP EPS, and management raised FY26 sales and EPS guidance. The main offset is a lower 2026 remeasurement-gains tailwind (down vs 2025) and softness in U.S. dental equipment demand (declining orders/comp pressures), keeping the read-through more balanced than a pure upside story.

Revenue landed near the pre-print consensus and margins improved, but the key transmission to the stock is guidance: FY adjusted EBITDA was cut to $133–136M (below the $133–140M framework and well aligned with the bear path of a CFO reset). The cut was explained by higher COGS from strong premium beef demand (not a demand collapse), yet management also lowered the longer-term unit-growth target and warned Q3 would be toughest/soft. That mix is likely viewed as deceleration/risk to the broken-multiple story despite the decent Q2 quarter.

Revenue was roughly in line with expectations, but EPS materially beat and—more importantly—full-year guidance was raised while contract value accelerated (ex-U.S. federal CV +3.3% and improved retention). With the stock positioned for a possible weak CV/revenue combo, the raised FY guide plus better demand indicators should drive a clearly positive next-day reaction, though the Fed-lap tailwind tempers the quality-of-beat.

Despite revenue decline, the company improved adjusted EBITDA margin and raised full-year revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance. However, full-year free cash flow is still a use of cash (~$75m), leverage remains elevated (11.3x), and the price-cost headwind worsened—likely limiting the upside reaction.

Q2 beat is directionally good but largely capped by the note’s view that the quarter itself was pre-signposted as “ugly.” The upside comes from guidance: revenue and EPS midpoint raised, and margins/FCF guided higher with strong cash generation and book-to-bill; these are incremental to what the note considered the base case, but the stock had already rebounded off the lows so the reaction is closer to modest than strong.

IMCIVREE net product sales beat the ~$67.3M expectation and US revenue reached $51M, supporting monetization off the HO bridge. RM-718 Part II efficacy was favorable with no generalized hyperpigmentation, and policy coverage advanced (25% Medicaid/35% commercial) without GLP-1 step edits. Offsets: international revenue declined on a France retrospective charge, and EPS net loss ($0.73) was roughly consistent with the noisy consensus. Net: modestly positive reaction, tempered by residual risk that ~$172M 2H26 still hinges on conversion/payer ramp despite better datapoints.

Headline results (revenue and adjusted EPS) beat the thin consensus, driven by Branded Products margin/EBITDA strength and SG&A leverage. However, guidance was reaffirmed (no upside) and Healthcare Apparel margin is expected to remain under pressure through 2026, which limits multiple expansion despite the beat.

Revenue and backlog beat the setup, but adjusted gross margin came in below the ~32–33% level the note flagged as crucial (30.6%), and Q3 EBITDA growth guide decelerates (8% midpoint), reinforcing the market’s margin-sensitivity. Net effect: modestly negative reaction despite solid top-line/orders.

Revenue and the margin bridge were weaker than implied by the pre-release setup (Q2 organic sales below expectations; NA shipments lag; additional full-year downside language). EPS/operating beat was driven largely by a Q2 tariff refund (one-off), while management explicitly lowered full-year outlook due to China disruption plus retailer/LA fire impacts, offset only in part by price and refund benefits—guidance is the dominant negative.

Despite a strong Q2 revenue/EBITDA beat and a clear FY26 guidance raise, the key margin test was not met: logistics gross margin fell to 18.4% vs the ~20% expectation and management points to partial headwinds (customer flying reduction) with only a gradual outlook. For a stock that had run up into the print, the mix/margin wobble likely limits upside.

Q2 delivered ahead of the already-tight setup: organic constant-currency +9% (vs +6–8% guide) and acquired BD growth re-accelerating, plus management raised FY organic growth to 7–9% and EPS to $14.45–$14.65. Only modest EPS outperformance vs $3.01 consensus and no mention of an FCF inflection limits upside versus the note’s bear risks (integration cash/FCF).

Q2 revenue and EBITDA were largely de-risked via the July 13 pre-announcement (so no meaningful incremental upside). EPS landed close to the already-marked estimate, while the key swing factor was Q3 revenue guidance: $305–$320M implies softness vs the note’s ~$285–$300M area, partially offset by raised FY adj. gross margin to ~38%. Net: mixed guidance signal with a modestly positive demand/cash flow backdrop, but no catalyst-level beat given how priced-in the quarter already was.

ADM materially raised FY26 adj. EPS guidance to $5.15-$5.60 (vs prior $4.15-$4.70 and above pre-release market expectation of ~$4.80). Q2 profitability was strong with sharply higher AS&O and a constructive biofuels backdrop, though results included ~$100M of positive MTM/timing. Net: a genuine upside guidance surprise should outperform a “beat-and-raise already priced” setup.

Quarter headline results missed (ongoing EPS -$0.21 vs $0.08 consensus; FCF deeply negative) and full-year EPS guidance was lowered (interest expense-driven) with tariffs still a headwind. While sequential EBIT margin improved and pricing/cost actions were reaffirmed, the underlying outlook still implies constrained recovery, leading to a modestly negative, but not catastrophic, reaction given the stock was already heavily positioned for weakness.

Results showed clear operational upside (orders up >12% sequentially, active customers +3%, adj. EBITDA margin 6.9%—best since 2021—plus strong FCF). Importantly, Q3 revenue growth was guided to high-single-digits (above the note’s mid-single-digit baseline) and margins were guided at the low end of the range without a step-down, reducing the key margin/GMV-risk that historically drives negative reactions for Wayfair. With the stock already run up and estimates revised up, the beat-and-raise is only moderately above expectation rather than a blowout.

Revenue and Q3 margin guidance largely fell within the pre-announced bands and were not a new shock; the main swing factors are gross margin (down to 40.7%) and the confirmation that the delayed customer orders won’t rebound in Q3—offset by still-strong optical and hyperscaler growth. With the stock setup already pricing timing/margin risk post pre-announcement, the net expected reaction is modestly negative-to-neutral.

Despite strong top-line growth, Q2 adjusted EBITDA margin compressed to 17.8% (vs ~19% expectations) and management cut FY26 adjusted EBITDA from $680–730M to $490–520M, far below the pre-release bull/base setup. Additional disclosed risks (West Coast underperformance, supplier price hike, stranded overhead) outweigh the positive new Humana OneHome capitated ramp.

Quarter-level EPS growth was solid and volume grew, but North & Central America operating earnings declined and management reaffirmed full-year guidance (no upgrade) while key capacity/ramp costs remain a 2H issue. Into a stock priced near its highs, this is more consistent with the note’s base-to-bear setup than a clear bull-case beat-and-raise.

Q2 beat on both revenue and EPS, plus an FY guidance raise—but the pre-release note framed the stock as already priced for a beat-and-raise at the top of guidance on record orders/backlog. The key incremental is the magnitude: sales grew 15% YoY and FY sales/organic guidance strengthened, while margins/FCF conversion also looked stronger. However, the raised guide is only modest vs the note’s base/bull path and Q3 implies deceleration, keeping the reaction near-median rather than strongly positive.

Adjusted EPS ($2.15) beat consensus ($1.41) largely driven by Renewables strength (record adjusted pretax $88M) with 45Z credits ($24M in quarter; $90–100M FY). Full-year run-rate EPS target to 2028 ($7) reaffirmed and credit expectation is broadly consistent with the note, so the reaction is positive but not extreme given the note’s expectation of strong 45Z/volume contributions.

Revenue growth and Premier/Dymatize outperformance came in better than expected, but the core story remains margin compression: gross margin collapsed and EBITDA margins/guides are weak (Q4 ~10% and FY2026 EBITDA down to ~$275–295M with freight/inventory headwinds). The FY revenue raise is offset by underwhelming profitability and leverage rising toward ~4x on a legal settlement, which should drive a modestly negative reaction despite the sales beat.

Headline adjusted EPS/ANI came in slightly below the $2.18/sh ANI beat line implied by consensus (after accounting for the pre-announced alt-income), but underlying fundamentals were strong: record ACS fees ($277M) and an improved net spread (reported 114 bps; 124 bps on normalized alts) with FRE margin expansion, while Q3 ADS redemption requests were ~half the prior run-rate. Guidance was reaffirmed on growth (20%+ FRE, 10% SRE) but the spread/earnings bridge and redemption commentary reduce the market’s key bear risk, yielding a modestly positive relief reaction rather than a large re-rating.

Without a pre-release note (consensus/what was priced), the best signal is underlying strength: revenue +13% YoY, gross margin improving (first YoY improvement in 4+ quarters), and a sharp adjusted EBITDA jump with operating leverage. Management kept full-year guidance but flagged H2 EBITDA decline YoY (Q3/Q4), which tempers the reaction versus the headline beat.

Despite a strong headline quarter (record revenue/backlog, margin expansion, raised FY sales outlook), the guidance and margin beat were meaningfully supported by tariff recoveries. Backlog also beat expectations, but the note flagged backlog/2027 narrative as the key asymmetry—management did quantify longer-dated Power & Energy orders (to 2030), which offsets concerns, leading to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Q2 revenue came in below the already-low consensus implied print while services remained soft (services decline + weak book-to-bill). Although FY revenue growth guidance was reaffirmed and adjusted EPS held flat, EBITDA/margin guidance was lowered (stranded costs) and continuing net loss widened—offset only partially by improving software bookings and Chemaxon-normalized bookings growth.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so beats/misses are not quantifiable. Narrative included strong printer unit momentum and a large multi-quarter industrial order, partially offset by gross-margin pressure from a printer-heavy 2H and a weaker Industrial/legacy services backdrop. Guidance is for a modest sequential revenue step-up with EBITDA still negative, implying limited upside near-term despite operational progress.

Underlying results were solid (FCF materially beat and margin expansion ahead of plan), but the forward outlook deteriorated: full-year adjusted revenue guidance was lowered and—most importantly for the multiple—Capital Markets growth guidance was cut sharply (to 3.0–3.5%) with additional attrition headwinds. Net: beat mainly in FCF/margins was offset by a quality of growth miss vs what the note flagged as the key swing factor.

No pre-release note was available, so surprise is judged mainly on the quality of the update: 2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance were raised and gross margin expanded for the second straight quarter with improving net leverage. The main offset is that adjusted EBITDA margin compressed year-over-year and net loss widened, limiting the upside to a moderate positive reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus provided. The raise to 2026 net sales/EBITDA is offset by margin pressure (tariff-related gross margin down 120 bps; adjusted EBITDA margin down 130 bps) and guidance that implies only low single-digit EBITDA growth amid higher leverage from the Cambridge deal.

Revenue was effectively pre-known and reiterated FY26 revenue guidance (no upside catalyst on top-line). However, underlying profitability is pressured: COGS rose to 24.2% from 19% due to Novitium royalties, which maps to the earnings-call “opex uncertainty” risk highlighted in the note; pipeline updates were positive but don’t offset the margin overhang for the next-day move.

Headline results are largely already underwritten by the same Beacon Point lease/financing narrative highlighted pre-release, and the call largely reinforces contracted backlog and financing rather than changing the key risks (timing/capex/financing gap). Revenue and operating profitability move in the expected direction, with GAAP dominated by digital-asset mark-to-market that the note framed as non-informative; G&A rise is mostly non-cash.

EPS beat versus expectations, but much of the quarter appears to align with the note’s “base/bull” setup (no big upside beyond what was modeled) while demand/visit indicators were not cleanly positive (U.S. visits still down; wellness weak). Despite the EPS/guidance raise, the new guidance is largely inline with the Street’s anchored midpoint, so the reaction is modestly positive rather than a repricing.

Core demand/mix concerns persist: global comps match the pre-note case, and U.S. momentum is flagged as slightly negative in July with an EDAP execution/traffic underperformance narrative. EPS looks roughly inline versus the already-pre-lowered bar, but the forex tailwind cut and the pushed-out restaurant target cap upside, limiting the reaction to neutral-to-slightly negative.

Quarter outcome looked better than feared (record Q4 closed sales and FY26 adj. EPS up to $9.60; Q4 equity position growth strong), and—critically—FY27 guidance and the FY27–28/visibility narrative improved versus what the note modeled (recurring growth range higher-end with margin expansion, plus larger buyback/dividend and embedded AI productivity). Only one structural risk remains (SEC e-delivery headwind over 2–3 years), which was already flagged as manageable.

Q2 beat both revenue and EPS versus the note’s $323M/$2.30 floor, and the company raised FY26 guidance again with EPS midpoint ($9.55) above the note’s $8.85–9.50 consensus positioning. However, AST already looked like the base-case bull setup and the stock was already up hard into the print, so the upside is moderated rather than “beat-and-runaway.”

Quarterly financials were largely a non-event (no meaningful revenue; EPS directionally inline vs non-cash-mark risk noted). The bigger surprise was operationally mixed: SELVA Phase 3 readout and continued 2H26 NDA submission/1H27 approval support the base case, but raising 2026 cash spend to $85–95M and losing BTD for cVM are negatives vs the note’s neutral/base framing, offsetting the positive trial/pipeline momentum.

Q2 results and, more importantly, guidance are better than the pre-release setup emphasized: GOV and adjusted EBITDA strengthened sequentially and management raised FY26 Marketplace GOV/EBITDA while cash increased and revolver was renewed. Upside is partially capped because the note already flagged World Cup as a key potential support, so the beat looks directionally constructive but not fully unanticipated.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, but the quarter delivered record adjusted EPS, revenue/organic growth, and gross margin expansion. The key offset is management explicitly tempering growth—Q2’s double-digit pace is not sustainable and 2026 guidance returns to the 6%-9% long-term range—limiting upside reaction.

Q3 delivered a beat (EPS $3.49 vs ~$3.37–$3.39 consensus) and margins expanded, with strong automation/data center demand. However, the key tension is guidance: FY26 adj. EPS midpoint is raised to $13.15 but still sits slightly below the pre-release $13.03–$13.06 consensus ‘top-of-guidance’ bar, while Lifecycle Services showed weakness (book-to-bill 0.97), keeping a deceleration/pricing-vs-cost risk in focus—consistent with a modestly negative-to-neutral tape reaction.

Q2 SaaS revenue and SaaS adj. EBITDA were in the expected ~$114–115M / $12–13M range, but FY26 guidance was cut (SaaS revenue and especially SaaS adj. EBITDA) and margins/demand quality look weaker versus the 2H hockey-stick requirement. Lowered back-half credibility after a strong pre-run should drive a negative tape reaction.

Q2 beat on adjusted EPS ($0.59 vs ~$0.56 published; ~+5% vs the note’s ~0.59–0.62 functional bar is at most modest) and delivered margin expansion (26.8% vs ~27% bar, but improved Y/Y). However, guidance was only affirmed (no FY margin raise), and Industrial margin slipped despite revenue growth plus capex guidance was raised to a higher-than-usual ~8.5% with higher H1 investment—limiting re-rating upside.

Q2 revenue and EPS came in well above the high end of outlook, and FY EPS/sales were raised. However, the call also guided to a Q3 deceleration and a step-down in EBITDA margin partly from the non-repeat removal of the tariff refund; the market likely focuses on that margin path, limiting upside reaction.
