Q2 delivered a clear upside on both revenue ($19.9M) and margins (61%+), plus a meaningful EBITDA improvement to near-breakeven. More importantly, FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $72–75M (midpoint above the pre-release expectations) and cash/EBITDA narrative improved versus the note’s key cash/credibility overhang—though some ASP strength includes aged-claims collections, partially muting the quality-of-growth beat.

ADUS beat consensus on both revenue (+~0.3%) and adjusted EPS (+~1.8%) and guided full-year adjusted EBITDA margin toward the higher end of its 12%-13% range, supported by strong personal care fill-rate improvement and hospice census growth. Offsetting items include hospice margin pressure from a Medicare cap accrual and tax-rate rise into the upper-20s; underlying EBITDA margin is still trending better despite the cap/tax headwinds.

Q2 revenue missed consensus and the Q3 revenue/EPS guide ($320–330M; $0.60–0.70) is below what the pre-release note framed as the likely “beat-and-raise” track for a stock priced for near-perfection. Positives (record Engineered Composites revenue and nearly doubled EC adjusted EBITDA) were not enough to offset the weaker Machine Clothing/delayed shipments and cash/working-capital pressure.

XMTR delivered strong beats on revenue ($229M vs ~$215M expected) and marketplace growth (45% YoY vs a guide/consensus centered around low/mid-30s), and—most importantly—raised FY26 revenue growth guidance to 33–34% (well above the 27–28% bearish base in the note). Underlying operating leverage improved (adj. EBITDA margin 6.2% vs 2.4%), with no meaningful offsetting deterioration.

EPS beat was supported by both underlying margin expansion and tariff refunds (non-recurring), while revenue was at the low end. Guidance was reiterated at the consensus-like level; however, Q3 organic is guided roughly flat with lower margins/EPS and Q3 revenue timing shifts into Q4, limiting upside at a stock priced for the semi-driven re-rating.

Record revenue and strong EBITDA growth, plus an EBITDA margin expansion and a full-year guidance raise, are likely supportive. However, GAAP improvement is heavily influenced by a favorable tax swing and SER/STEM timing items (and NOx-related cost pressure) keep the setup from being a clear upside blowout.

Q2 revenue ($883M) beat the $839.9M consensus and non-GAAP EPS ($0.93) beat $0.83; margins also improved to 47.6%. More importantly, management’s raised 2026 MSI growth forecast and the Q3 guide at roughly $905–935M vs the ~$871M pre-committed midpoint expectation supports upside to the Street, making reaction modestly positive despite the high bar set by the note.

No pre-release consensus or reported revenue/EPS figures were provided, so the valuation reaction must be inferred from qualitative guidance: management reiterated a maintenance CapEx run-rate (~$1.0–$1.1B/quarter) and targeted low single-digit organic growth into 2027, with near-term Waha price relief. However, guidance/trajectory is tempered by cost pressure (LOE ~$/bbl staying ~6 with inflation) and mixed EOR results, limiting upside and leading to a near-median reaction.

Headline revenue, EBITDA margin, and the pro-forma growth narrative came in better than the note’s base case (record $36.9M; adj. EBITDA margin 23.4%; oncology >$20M). However, Patient Services gross margin fell and guidance was only reaffirmed (no raise or quantified H2 improvement), which tempers upside for a stock already priced with elevated expectations.

Underlying profitability and full-year revenue guidance were improved with margin expansion, but the call also signaled second-half growth deceleration and a slightly trimmed net income outlook due to heavier investment spend—partially offsetting the positive. With no pre-release note/consensus provided, surprise vs expectations is unknown, leading to a roughly median reaction.

No pre-release consensus/guidance benchmark is available. Headline results were at the high end of guidance with FCF strong, but adjusted EBITDA margin slipped (20% vs 21%) and management cited higher conflict-related costs, partially offsetting the beat. Q3 guide implies modest sequential growth with acquisition/accounting tailwinds, but underlying margin remains a key watch item.

Q2 net sales slightly beat consensus (1% vs $1.81B expectation), but adjusted EPS is effectively inline while underlying profitability was pressured by Argo and Mexico, and guidance was maintained with FY adjusted EPS reaffirmed. With the market already braced for Argo drag and confidence concerns, the main positives (T&HS strength) partially offset the deteriorated Argo/LATAM demand and operating-income guide. Net reaction skewed neutral-to-slightly positive.

Quarter-level metrics broadly align with the pre-release base case (EBITDA in-range and outlook reaffirmed). The main incremental negative versus what was de-risked was that volumes/NICU days were weaker (volumes -2%, NICU -3%) versus the note’s base expectation of flat-to-mildly better conditions; guidance remained unchanged, so there’s limited upside catalyst.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations are largely not measurable. On fundamentals, results showed strong topline growth and a much larger order book, but guidance is only “slightly higher” and melt utilization missed plan due to power/execution issues, suggesting underlying margin headwinds and limiting the upside reaction.

Q2 revenue and (implied) EPS both fell below consensus, and adjusted EBITDA declined, indicating margin pressure rather than rebound. Management’s July commentary highlighted weather/air-quality headwinds (wildfires, heat, rain), and while share repurchases and record in-park per-capita spending were positives, the demand/attendance trend and underlying profitability were weaker than the note’s setup.

Quarterly adjusted EPS missed consensus (down to $1.49 vs ~$1.80) despite a 34% EBITDA rise, and management reaffirmed FY26 guidance while explicitly tracking below the midpoint on softer Texas load/power prices, Winter Storm Fern costs, and higher RGGI. The hyperscaler BYOP project alignment is a meaningful positive, but the guidance tone and extended net-debt/3x timeline dominate for near-term reaction.

Headline EPS missed mainly due to the already-expected Terns acquisition charge; ex-charge EPS and revenue were broadly in line to slightly better. The key debate is guidance/trajectory: revenue guide was raised slightly (2–4% growth) and pipeline de-risking looked faster, but management explicitly flagged moderation in U.S. Keytruda growth and lowered gross margin via higher inventory reserves—together implying a modestly positive-to-neutral reaction.

While underlying Q2 profitability and backlog momentum were very strong (EPS beat, EBITDA/margins up, backlog up sharply) and full-year guidance was raised well above the Street, the company also flagged Q3 order/backlog timing lumpiness and sequential backlog risk—capping the upside.

Revenue was broadly in line with the pre-release setup (Modern Oral growth continued, consolidated sales +23%). However, adjusted EBITDA dropped ~50% to $15M (11% margin) and the key market concern—profitability pressure from pouch investment/ZigZag softness—did not improve; only Modern Oral sales guidance was raised while full-year EBITDA stayed $70–90M. With the stock already up ~8% into the print, the net reaction skews slightly negative/flat.

No pre-release research note or revenue/EPS consensus was provided, but the company raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance at the midpoint and reiterated/raised long-term growth targets, with a solid 2Q EBITDA gain and on-time/in-budget Socrates Phase 1 milestone. Incremental leverage/capital capacity and deal narrative appear supportive, though without quantified consensus it’s harder to size the surprise.

Headline EPS grew but margins fell (gross margin down 120 bps) and both divisions reported book-to-bill below 1x with orders down, while guidance implies flattish/soft end markets and sequential declines from the Q2 peak. With no pre-release note/consensus provided, the setup points to a mild negative reaction despite leverage improvement.

Top-line and adjusted EBITDA were slightly better than pre-release expectations, but the bigger underwhelming surprise was the softer Q3 EBITDA guide (step-down) alongside explicit Q2 sand volume shortfalls and continued pricing support actions that imply near-term margin/volume trade-offs. Power contract is positive, but meaningful cash flow is ~a year away, so the market likely focused on the near-term deceleration.

Headline EPS matches the ~$0.21 consensus and management reiterated the already-expected FY2026 flat-to-up ~5% sales outlook. Upside is margin landing at the top end of the FY range (20.3%) and strong diversification/new business wins, but operating income declined on higher SG&A and ROCE remains far below targets, limiting upside surprise and keeping reaction around neutral-to-positive.

Revenues and EPS were better than the pre-release consensus setup, and FY revenue guidance was raised (midpoint toward 10–13%), which the note said was the key hurdle. However, consolidated EBITDA margin fell to 17.5% (variable comp/tariffs), tempering the upside versus the note’s margin-driven bear risks; still, Power Systems margin improved to 24.5% and demand/order visibility looked constructive (hyperscaler deal, extended lead times).

Revenue and adjusted EPS beat, and full-year guidance was raised, but the core issue highlighted in the note—margin/cash conversion risk—materially worsened in the quarter (U.S. Gas gross margin 4.2% vs. 7.8% and base gross margin down). The U.S. Gas margin miss plus elevated cost headwinds, even with the raised outlook, likely drives a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction consistent with the market’s prior pattern of not rewarding revenue alone.

Headline Q2 EPS beat the effective $1.30 whisper ($1.43 vs expected range), but management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance ($6.55–$6.80) which the pre-release note flagged as the key driver. Underlying beat quality wasn’t clearly attributed to one-offs in the provided facts; guidance and balance-sheet/ESA outlook were broadly consistent with the base case, leading to a near-median to modestly positive reaction.

Headline EPS margin confidence improved (Q4 GM in low 40s, ex-IEEPA) and some IEEPA cash has been collected, but the key disappointment vs the note is guidance: management cut back-half organic growth to ~flat-to-up ~1% (category weakening 200–300 bps) and lowered full-year outlook to the low end. That breaks the previously expected inflection narrative, a negative for this stock’s trading pattern.

No consensus/expected figures (revenue/EPS) were provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. The call delivered constructive operating/capital narrative (lower D&C costs, tighter basis, firm transportation add), but it also framed some items as not necessarily trend-setting (transportation decision) and did not provide a clear guidance change vs expectations; net reaction expected near median.

Q2 revenue was roughly in line, and adj. EBITDA margin was strong/sequentially up, but the key underperformance vs expectations came from guidance: full-year inflation was revised much higher and full-year adj. EBITDA was guided to the low end, with cash flow lowered and leverage not improving as cleanly as the H2 step-up narrative implied. Net effect should pressure the stock despite the operational margin resilience.

Q2 delivered stronger-than-expected sales and EPS on accelerating delivered comps and a higher gross margin, and management reaffirmed the key FY gross-margin range (excluding refunds), which directly addresses the note’s biggest downside risk. However, gross margin ex-refunds was essentially flat (so the headline beat is partly shielded by tariff refunds), and management highlighted new fuel/container/input cost headwinds plus aggressive purchase capacity/repurchase plans that don’t change the core margin outlook.

Revenue was essentially in line with consensus, but EBITDA/earnings quality relied on a tariff refund. The bigger swing factor was guidance credibility: orders stayed >$1B with double-digit Prepared Food growth, supporting backlog and the unchanged full-year targets, partially offset by company commentary that Prepared Food revenue timing slipped into the second half and implies EBITDA pressure there.

Q2 revenue and headline EPS beat the pre-release setup, helped by gross margin at 40.7%—but that margin upside included ~170bps of tariff refunds (one-time). Importantly, Q3 guidance at the midpoint (revenue ~$280M, adj. EPS ~$0.45, GM ~39%) is at/above the note’s bull/base thresholds, and book-to-bill stayed >1 with improved Europe/strong Asia—supportive for a modestly positive reaction.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, but the release features a higher/narrowed FY26 NFEPS range and constructive development catalysts (FERC certificate ahead of schedule) plus CapEx outlook reaffirmation. Reaction is modestly positive given guidance tightening/raises, but confidence is limited by missing revenue/consensus metrics and no explicit underlying margin or utilization commentary.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so EPS/revenue beats vs expectations can’t be quantified. The quarter shows strong operating earnings/EPS growth (55% adjusted operating EPS YoY) and improving ROE, and management reaffirmed full-year free capital generation/capital return—supportive for sentiment—though there was an unfavorable notable-item impact tied to limited partnership results and no guidance upside.

No pre-release note or explicit consensus/guidance figures were provided, so surprises can’t be quantified. Reported fundamentals were broadly strong (record net income and premium; combined ratio best in 15+ years) offset by competitive renewal dynamics and a higher expense ratio tied to a lease buyout; absent a specific guidance miss/raise, reaction is set near neutral-positive.

Q2 adjusted EPS ($0.77) beat consensus ($0.68) and FY26 revenue guidance midpoint was raised by ~$0.5B, both supportive. However, the raise is partly offset by a lower COVID assumption and the quarter featured large impairment charges and an unfavorable gross margin trend vs LY, keeping the reaction modest rather than strong.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so surprise counts vs expectations are unquantified. Underlying margin is pressured (adj. EBITDA margin down to 17.2% from 20.8%) due to a non-repeating project, which likely offsets the strong revenue/EBITDA growth and improved leverage; overall reaction is modestly positive given growth and international outperformance, but not strong due to contracting margins and limited visibility into next-period EBITDA.

Q4 topped expectations (EPS and revenue) while USFS local volume accelerated (2.9% in 2H; 2.6% in Q4). FY2027 EPS guidance ($5.02–$5.12$) is slightly above the pre-release $4.96 consensus despite the 53rd-week benefit and buyback pause, which should be modestly supportive. Offset: gross margin fell and the demand/guidance tone relies on only ~2.5% USFS local growth, limiting upside.

Reported Q1 revenue and EPS landed roughly as expected and full-year revenue/adj. EBITDA guidance was reiterated within the same range, which is the base-case for this setup. However, margin/earnings quality is not clearly improved versus the note’s bear-case concerns, and net debt rose further, keeping the reaction modest rather than strongly positive.

Despite solid AUM growth and +4% adjusted EBITDA, diluted EPS came in well below the thin consensus, with EBT down sharply YoY and maintenance reserve revenues falling on weaker flight hours/utilization. With the stock already rallied into the print, the miss—driven by profit/earnings components rather than revenue alone—likely drives a negative reaction.

Management lowered FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance into the mid-$50M range on the back of a weak first half, which matches/extends the base-case trim risk outlined in the note. Operating softness also showed up in Q2: TV One subscriber declines accelerated and Digital fell on reduced DEI spend, both reinforcing the negative trajectory despite the still-meaningful debt arbitrage from note repurchases.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Qualitatively, the outlook is a clear margin deceleration: Q3 BMD EBITDA guided down sharply from Q2 with supplier-transition drag and soft end markets, which likely overwhelms the good Wood Products margin/price update; the Hardie transition risk appears to be the key driver.

No pre-release note and no reported vs consensus revenue/EPS figures provided, but the release included a raised 2026 production range, improved operating expense guidance, record levered FCF, and a significantly upgraded Permian synergy target—offset partly by management guiding for natural volume decline in the back half and a slight 2027 decline.

Q2 results beat on EPS and sales, and management raised FY EPS guidance (midpoint meaningfully above the pre-release $45.25). However, gross margin expansion included a material 90 bps EPA/tariff-refund tailwind and Q3 operating margin is guided to drop mid-15% as refunds lap, tempering the sustainability of the upside.

Revenue growth and backlog conversion beat consensus, but underlying profitability was effectively flat (reported EBITDA distorted by a prior-year gain), EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed while margin expansion guidance was cut (200 bps to ~100 bps) and management signaled trending to the midpoint. The raise is only for revenue, so the net surprise skews negative versus the market’s expectation of an upper-half outcome.

Reported results beat consensus (fee-related revenues and non-GAAP EPS), and—most importantly—evergreen net inflows were strong (nearly $640M; >$19B AUM) with FRE margin expanding to 53%. Given the note’s credibility/information focus from the short thesis, the stronger flow/margin disclosure supports an upside repricing despite no explicit guidance details provided.

Q2 results beat expectations (EPS $17.73 vs ~$14.52 consensus) with unusually strong R&M capture (112%) and record-low unplanned downtime, but the Q3 guide flags a capture headwind from turnaround-heavy spend and a 94% utilization setup. With MPC priced for a good quarter (and crack-driven expectations already high), the downside comes from incremental deceleration in the next-quarter margin/capture outlook rather than the Q2 print.

Q2 revenue was modestly above consensus, but gross margin collapsed to 5.5% (below what investors were looking for after the Q1 high margin), and management sharply lowered full-year delivery/revenue/EBITDA guidance due to a delayed ramp. Despite strong backlog and solid aftermarket growth, the margin and guidance reset are negative relative to expectations.

Headlines were mixed vs consensus (revenue below and EPS below), but the release delivered strong demand signals: record $934M new orders, 3.0x book-to-bill, and record $2.4B backlog with mega-project detail. Margin was roughly flat and CFO commentary wasn’t a clear margin acceleration; net effect fits a modestly positive, options-sized but not perfection-level reaction given elevated IV and priced-in uncertainty.

No pre-release consensus figures were provided, so beats/misses vs expectations can’t be quantified. However, management raised 2026 adjusted EBITDA/EPS/net income and extended cash tax benefits, which should support sentiment; partially offsetting this, management flagged margin softness (NGL mix) and expects Natural Gas Pipeline earnings to decline in 2H as new Permian takeaway comes online.

EPS beat consensus ($0.86 vs ~$0.80; ~+7.5%), while FY2026 non-GAAP guidance was reaffirmed (no upside in the guide versus the pre-release range). Underlying drivers cited (liquidity/financing resilience, PJM allocation benefit, and nuclear capacity auction outcome) look supportive, but lack of a guidance raise caps upside versus what the market likely expected given prior beat history and “no beat” modeling.

No pre-release consensus/research note or reported revenue was provided, so EPS/revenue beats vs expectations can’t be quantified. Guidance was raised, but management flagged softer 2H PVC volumes and the Plastics decline/price environment pressured results; the pipeline update is positive but demand tone remains cautious, implying a mildly positive but not strong reaction.

Headline EPS and revenue were essentially in line with the pre-release setup, and guidance was reaffirmed. The key margin call was mixed: adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 12.1% (slightly below the ~12.3% consensus-implied hurdle), partially offset by record EBITDA and improved leverage/working-capital dynamics.

Q2 beat on revenue and adj. EPS, and FY adj. EPS guidance was raised above consensus, with margin expanding. However, the call also guided a notable second-half growth step-down (~2.5 points) despite the raise, which is not in the pre-release bull case and fits a fade-strength setup—hence a below-median reaction despite the upside.

TDG delivered a clean underlying quarter (52.8% EBITDA margin, commercial aftermarket +18%, OEM +17%) and raised FY26 guidance again (notably adj. EPS to $41.04 and revenue/EBITDA midpoints higher), with demand/backlog commentary supportive. The main constraint vs the note is that the stock had some prior run-up/anticipation and several “bear” risks (OEM destocking, margin dilution) did not worsen, keeping the reaction positive-but-not-maximum.

No pre-release note and no consensus figures were provided for revenue/EPS, limiting precision. The key actionable item is guidance: the company narrowed 2026 production guidance (bottom unchanged) while raising the bottom of total cash capex, which is generally consistent with maintaining capital discipline; overall implies stability rather than a negative surprise.

No pre-release note/consensus figures were provided, so this is scored on directional elements from the call: a higher, protected base dividend plus strong production/buyback commitments and Q3 implying ~1,000 bpd purely organic QoQ growth. The main uncertainty is lack of quantified financial/earnings benchmarks (revenue/EPS) and no explicit comment on underlying margins beyond cash-return framework.

Q2 delivered a large PEM EBITDA jump and cost-program contribution, and EPS improved materially versus the wide pre-print dispersion. However, HIP EBITDA was essentially flat with margin compression, management guided HIP full-year revenue/margin toward the lower end (residential outlook reset), and flagged Q3 pipe volume pull-forward—so the guidance/demand tone is not a clean upside confirmation versus what the market was already bracing for.

No pre-release note and no consensus expectations for revenue/EPS were provided. Management reaffirmed 2026 EPS guidance at the midpoint (no guidance change) while citing expanded electric/gas gross margins and continued customer growth/cold weather, suggesting a modestly positive but not strong reaction.

EPS missed consensus ($1.43 vs ~$1.48–$1.49) as higher interest/depreciation and lower transmission revenue offset weather benefits, and margins are contracting. Despite topping the FY26 guide range’s top end and strong demand/weather-normalized growth, the mix of a headline EPS miss plus utility regulatory uncertainty (rate-case decision timing) likely dampens the immediate upside; the market was already braced for a weather-aided print.

TPG beat on fee-related revenue (above the note’s $573.5M consensus) and after-tax distributable earnings (reported $0.69 vs $0.62–$0.64 consensus), but the key forward signal is negative: FRE margin was 50% only due to pulled-forward transaction fees, and management warned fees/capital markets revenue step down in 2H as closings moved from Q3 to Q2—cooling growth quality. Guidance (47% full-year FRE margin and >$50B fundraising) was reaffirmed, so the reaction skews modestly negative given the deceleration narrative.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat on a record quarter, and Illinois quality metrics were strong (hold-per-day +9%) with a positive Chicago timeline update (first locations within weeks). EPS undershot the consensus range (diluted EPS $0.15 vs ~$0.18 GAAP / ~$0.25 adjusted), and underlying growth quality is somewhat offset by Nevada blended hold-per-day decline (-15.8%) plus one-off noncash charges.

Revenue and key segment metrics (DAYBUE STIX adoption; NUPLAZID prescriptions/volume) came in stronger than the note’s base case, and DAYBUE guidance was raised. The main offset is a partial reset via lowered FY R&D guidance (plus the remlifanserin timing moving to Sep–Oct, but that was within the note’s Aug–Oct window), leading to a modestly positive but not outsized reaction.

Headline prints were strong, but the setup in the note was about Q3 fuel and integration/CASM. Q3 guidance calls for a consolidated loss (~$0.50) with operating margin ~2% and capacity down ~5.5% while nonfuel CASM ex-cargo jumps 10–12% and peak CASM pressure is acknowledged; leverage also rises with a ~$275M pilot retention bonus. Underlying isn’t obviously worse on demand (TRASM >20% YoY), but forward profitability trajectory clearly deteriorates versus the note’s base/bull framing for a de-risked transition.

Q2 headline results beat consensus, and Q3 revenue guide is well above expectations (midpoint $550M vs ~$410M consensus; and above the note’s base). However, gross margin guidance is cut to ~72% (notably below the note’s ~73% base), signaling mix-driven margin pressure despite the strong growth. With the stock already priced for perfection after a sharp run-up, the margin deceleration and lower GM guide are the key negative driver for reaction.

Q2 revenue beat the pre-release expectation, and full-year FCF conversion/liquidity looked better than feared. However, adjusted EBITDA/margin fell sharply and Q3 EBITDA guidance was weak, implying continued margin pressure near-term—exactly the risk highlighted in the note—so the net setup is modestly negative for the next-day move.

Headline growth and a raised FY26 guide (rev and non-GAAP EPS) beat the already-high expectations in the note, but the stock is priced for perfection and the guide remains within a narrow, top-of-range band. Margin came in strong (48% non-GAAP op margin) while disclosed Q3 OpEx step-up from a BD upfront payment and management transition adds near-term cost risk; the note already flagged an unquantified cybersecurity overhang, so incremental positives are only partially rewarded.

Q1 and FY27 were better than what the pre-release note expected: revenue ($166M) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.19) beat consensus, and management raised FY27 revenue and adjusted EBITDA with margin expansion (AGP-weighted mix). With the stock already up strongly, the upside is still notable but not a perfect-step change given high prior momentum.

Headline delivery beat both Street and the note’s inferred “bear trigger” (GM) with an even larger upside in EPS and a notable FY guide raise to ~$12.6B, but the pre-release note warned that the stock was priced for perfection after a run-up and that guidance conservatism/GM absorption risk was the real swing factor. While Q2 GM strengthened, the call also anchored aggressive supply commitments (price/mix risk) and the magnitude of the raise versus the note’s implied bar (only ~$11.9–12.0B / AI $4.0B) likely keeps the reaction capped despite upside. Net: positive fundamentals, but expectations/positioning suppress the stock response.

ATEC reported revenue slightly above the working Q2 bar (~$212M) and clearly beat on profitability (adj. EBITDA +53% YoY; gross margin +260 bps). The key incremental item is the FY adjusted EBITDA raise to ~$140M, but the setup already priced substantial sensitivity around EOS timing/FCF and biologics weakness; underlying cash flow was still modest and EPS was not clearly benchmarkable vs the note’s mismatched consensus series.

Ahead/inline on the key narrative drivers the note already anchored on (sHTG sNDA timing before YE26, accelerated potential Q2’27, and strong SHASTA efficacy). However, the quarter’s loss widened and underlying economics are less favorable than the note’s implied base (revenue helped by deals/REDEMPLO mechanics), which tempers enthusiasm on an otherwise well-de-risked setup.

Revenue and EPS were not the primary swing factors versus a note that already expected low-quality/volatile consensus and stressed EBITDA/gross margin. The key upside was gross margin expanding to 26.8% and an improved Q3 guide (closer to the high end, with margins near ~30%), alongside a stronger liquidity position. Underlying EBITDA remains negative, but the forward margin trajectory reduced the probability of the bear case.

Headline revenue and non-GAAP EPS were strong, but organic growth was only 7% (vs the note’s ~10–11% embedded consensus expectation), partially offset by a better-than-expected gross margin rebound to 66% and higher visibility (RPO +97%) plus CAIRO monetization metrics. Management reaffirmed the $100M run-rate target while hinting at more M&A, limiting the downside from the organic miss.

EVTC beat both revenue and EPS versus the pre-release base case, and the FY revenue and EPS guide were raised slightly above the note’s expectations. However, EBITDA margin still slipped (39.8% vs 40.3%) and leverage rose to 2.55x with Dimensa—limiting upside conviction versus the market’s “reaffirm/clean guide” setup.

Headline non-GAAP EPS was dominated by the already-expected acquired IPR&D charge (broadly in line with the note). Underlying momentum improved with strong base-business growth, HIV guidance raised, and PrEP exceeding $1B run-rate; partially offset by weaker cell therapy that stays a key risk. Net: modestly positive, not a major rerating.

Q2 beat on revenue/EPS with margin expansion, but the key forward read-through disappointed: Q3 room-night growth guided to 3%-5% (below the ~+5–7% market expectation) and full-year gross bookings outlook was lowered on weaker flight-ticket growth. With priced-in caution around forward growth/AI fears, the mix of a beat with softer growth guidance is a modestly negative setup for the stock.

Jacobs printed solidly with accelerating earnings power (EPS +~14%, EBITDA margin 15.2%) and record backlog, but the quarter was broadly consistent with the pre-release setup. The key incremental positive is guidance strength (FY26 EPS and FCF margin raised again) plus a confident Q4 margin step-up (~16%)—supporting a modestly positive but not euphoric reaction given expectations were already constructive.

EPS beat and a full-year adjusted EPS raise were delivered despite a small Middle East headwind that was already framed in the note. Guidance also improved/was reiterated above the expected base case, and margins expanded (28.5% vs 27.1% LY), but the stock was already near highs with a rich narrative, limiting upside reaction versus a perfect-score beat/raise.

Q2 revenue beat (record) and FY26 revenue guidance was raised, with Adj. EBITDA also at/above the pre-release bar (record ~$6.8M, nearly 10% margin). However, the call also confirmed a key weakness versus the base-case: scoliosis revenue fell due to zero 7D unit sales and VertiGlide set deployments were only $2.9M with most set deployment still due in Q3, keeping growth/FCF risk from fully resolving.

Headline revenue beat is largely mechanical from the merger, and adjusted EBITDA margin still contracted sharply. The key offsetting positive is the synergy target being raised, but 2H guidance embeds weak AMWD profitability (~$20M EBITDA on ~$730M sales; ~3% margin) and leverage remains elevated, keeping the near-term outlook credibility constrained versus the market’s “reinstatement/credit to the deal” hopes.

Q2 revenue and GAAP EPS both missed the pre-release working expectations, and the ingredient business outlook plus continued elevated S&M (34% of sales) argue against the clean-EPS rebound investors were looking for. Guidance was reiterated (10–15% e-commerce growth) but this reads more like reaffirmation amid investment-year drag than a catalyst reset, so the setup skews negative versus an already discounted print.

Q2 revenue was only ~in line with expectations, while ARR grew (retention ~103% overall) but adjusted EBITDA margin fell on acquisition/GTm costs. The key offset is a guidance raise for both FY revenue and FY adjusted EBITDA, plus higher hardware guide, which likely limits downside versus the pre-announced $3M ARR headwind risk (not clearly worsened). Overall reaction expected to be modestly positive but not strong given margin compression and the stock being priced near highs.

Q2 revenue/EPS broadly matched consensus, but the company lowered FY2026 total revenue guidance (midpoint ~$747.5M vs $757.5M prior) while EXPAREL volume growth stepped down and elective soft-tissue procedures slowed. Reimbursement wins/preferred formulary support were positive but not enough to offset the implied growth deceleration from the guide cut.

Q2 results beat on revenue (17% vs consensus ~$172.9M) and gross profit (17% to $122M vs expected ~119–121M), and margins held/expanded with a lower take rate. However, the stock still faces the feared H2 deceleration—management guided Q3 gross profit growth down to 5%-7% and reiterated the second-half Cash App drag—partially offset by raising FY revenue/gross profit bands and EBITDA growth. Net: positive but not a blowout vs what the note expected to be the battleground.

Pre-release note lacked a Q2 consensus revenue number and did not quantify an EPS/quarter expectation, so upside/downside cannot be cleanly scored versus consensus. However, the call delivered a clearly strong quarter (profitability, $55M total revenue, rapidly scaling Papzimeus) with reiteration of cash-flow breakeven guidance; the main offset is management’s commentary that future growth will decelerate (diminishing rate) and the implied normalization of margins from 95% toward the high-80s/low-90s steady-state.

Headline net sales/EPS landed roughly where the (low-quality) Street bars implied, while management maintained FY27 guidance (no raise). The reaction should be tempered by a contracting consolidated gross margin and professional services softness/delays, partially offset by strong open orders and growth in managed services/security gross billings.

Q2 results beat the street model (revenue and EPS), and the most important item—forward momentum—came in around expectations with Q3 guide decelerating but not breaking. Guidance for full-year adjusted EBITDA margin was raised to ~30% vs 29%, and management cited cost-per-transaction efficiency and improving Performance+ ROAS, offsetting the previously flagged infrastructure/margin risk. Net: a modest positive reaction consistent with a guidance stock printing better-than-feared rather than a true upside shock.

Only guidance items are provided: Rigel raised the FY26 upper bound via stronger contract revenue, but it also explicitly withheld near-term Vepinu (VEPPANU) launch guidance and indicated formal guidance near JPM may still exclude Vepinu—adding uncertainty versus the market’s likely desire for an incorporated launch/earnings bridge. Underlying product sales guidance was maintained and excludes Vepinu, so the raise is narrower/less growth-relevant than bulls likely hoped.

Q2 revenue landed slightly above expectations, but US procedure growth was weaker than expected (legacy AquaBeam weakness) and—most importantly—the company lowered full-year 2026 US procedure guidance to 54k-56k (midpoint down ~7k from the prior setup), while raising opex. Despite tariff-driven gross margin lift, the guide action breaks the math supporting the FY story, which is the key item priced into the stock.

Revenue and disruption were slightly better than the note’s base case (GVR disruption ~$7M vs ~$9M guided; lower construction drag supports the H2 narrative). However, consolidated adjusted EBITDA margin still contracted (~-281 bps to 40.8%) and the stock already traded up near the highs with a premium H2 expectation, limiting upside versus an otherwise de-risked trough quarter.

Top-line and underlying margin direction were broadly consistent with the pre-release setup (beat largely supported by tariff-refund timing and the quarter followed the expected trend). The key signal is the continued gross margin headwind for Q3 (maintained FY range and 53.5–54.0% Q3 guide implying ~88 bps decline), which offsets the strong demand/momentum into only a neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

Results were broadly in line with very low expectations for a milestone-driven business, but the quarter’s revenue is effectively flattered by a non-cash reversal (and underlying burn remains heavy with a larger operating loss). Incremental positives were mainly operational (equipment installed; commissioning starting Q4) plus the stated JV effort, which is already an expected swing factor per the note—so the net reaction skews slightly positive rather than a clear beat/raise outcome.

Q2 headlines beat on sales and adjusted EBITDA, and the company raised FY guidance (a meaningful positive vs the note’s base-case). However, gross margin fell more than expected (35.5% vs ~37.5–38% est.) with margin pressure tied to ramp-up costs, and GAAP EPS was weak due to FX, limiting quality of the beat; on balance guidance outweighs, but margin durability caps upside.

EPS materially beat the (indicative) $0.38 expectation ($0.51 adjusted) alongside strong operating metrics: 13% organic service growth and 90bp service gross margin expansion. Revenue upside is directionally positive but the note lacked a Q1 revenue consensus, while the key offset was distribution gross margin compression tied to prior-year rebate timing. Management reiterated/strengthened confidence with an FY outlook (service growth and margin expansion), supporting a modestly positive reaction rather than a breakout beat.

EPS materially beat (recurring/timing), and management raised FY EPS and FCF, but the core growth narrative lagged (cloud ARR growth below the low-double-digit target; consulting revenue down sharply) with a clearly weaker Q3 revenue trajectory guided. Net effect is neutral-to-slightly positive given the pre-print run and that key growth KPIs were not fully met.

Headline revenue came in below the note’s $79.4M consensus primarily because Revuforj net revenue (the key swing) was $55M vs an implied $61–62M bar. However, management confirmed funding adequacy (cash $575M) and provided some positive incremental detail (KMT2A restart rate improving to 50% from 45%), while the quarter’s new patient starts softness was framed as temporary—keeping the setup closer to the note’s bear/base spread than a clear miss. Overall reaction likely near-median given guidance was maintained and there’s no clear underlying deterioration beyond the revenue line.

Revenue and product demand clearly beat the note’s base setup (FILSPARI ~$141.1M and total revenue $169.6M well above ~$157.3M consensus), and management’s FSGS launch commentary emphasized outpacing the IgA launch without evidence of a demand bolus. Lack of explicit EPS/guidance detail limits confidence; also no margin/income quality check was provided beyond higher GAAP OpEx.

Top-line was roughly in line (slight upside), but the key overhang—margin/cost cadence—worsened: adjusted operating margin guidance was cut to ~12.5%–14% (excluding PAD), and service normalization plus PAD dilution (no margin yet quantified) undermines the prior margin-recovery thesis. With the stock already exposed via large implied move and high volatility skew, the guidance haircut drives a negative setup for the next-day reaction.

Headline profits and margins beat key prior-quarter softness expectations, with adjusted EBITDA rebounding to a 21% margin and contribution margin improving. However, FY guidance was reiterated (no Q2 beat/raise to rerate materially), so upside is likely to be modest-to-positive rather than a major re-acceleration signal.

Q2 revenue/EPS were not meaningfully better than what the note expected, but the company sharply cut FY26 revenue (to $100–110M vs $130–135M) and disclosed a key EG4/45X inverter ramp push to Q4 due to partner issues—plus gross margin fell to 39.3% and adjusted EBITDA collapsed with a still-challenged Q3 loss range. This is the core bearish guidance surprise, overriding any cash improvement.

Headline quarter was broadly in line, but management materially worsened the key Wynn Al Marjan timeline/cost story (budget +$600M; opening pushed to Sep 2027 and additional equity), which directly attacks the underwritten optionality catalyst from the note. Las Vegas and Macau hold commentary also reinforced ongoing pressure (unfavorable holds), limiting upside despite some volume recovery into late Q3.

Q2 delivered a modest upside to already-on-target consensus, plus margin expansion and strong operating metrics. However, the stock was priced for continued beat-and-raise (and much of the setup risk—base case about inline performance—was already highlighted), so the incremental reaction is capped despite a FY raise.

Despite strong revenue growth, the key margin debate was not solved: gross margin fell to 21.6% YoY down from 26.1% and management guided to moderate Q4 contraction (consistent with the note’s bear/base). The record $140M pipeline and strong adjusted EBITDA reversal offset, but market is still focused on margin normalization rather than growth, implying limited upside and some downside risk if the margin recovery timing slips.

Revenue and data center strength were solid versus consensus, and gross margin expanded ~200bp, but the key setup was Q3 revenue guide (the note’s bull/bear triggers) and management’s commentary still implies some cadence risk (Helios shipments ramping through Q4). Client/gaming softness and the large already-priced run reduce upside reaction despite an above-consensus Q3 guide and raised longer-term outlook.

Revenue came in roughly in line with the pre-release range focus, while adjusted EBITDA loss narrowed to near break-even. The key item versus the note was incremental positive DHA visibility (intent/sole-source direct contract expected) and a full-year revenue guidance low-end raise; however, subscription revenue still declined sharply YoY and the DHA scope remains in negotiation, keeping the reaction near-median.

Revenue and non-GAAP EPS landed essentially where the pre-print expected (and full-year guidance was reaffirmed). The key offset is that the company’s margin rebound (12.5% vs 6.6% in Q1) was good, but underlying pull-through for consumables and the newly detailed restructuring one-time cost/FX headwinds keep upside limited for a stock already priced near perfection on activist hopes.

No revenue consensus was available pre-release, and EPS consensus was limited (thin coverage). The print showed continued revenue decline and a deterioration in profitability (Adjusted EBITDA swung negative) while guidance remains withheld—incrementally worse than what investors were already wary of given the prior run of misses and lack of a forward framework.

Headline EPS beat consensus, but the note offered limited/fragile expectations and implied no forward guidance from the company. Underlying dynamics were mixed: volume re-stabilized and dealer growth hit records, yet forecast/collection dynamics remain a recurring drag (larger-than-Q1 cash-flow decline and provision gap tied to slower-than-forecast prepayments), keeping reaction near neutral-to-slightly positive.

Revenue came in far below the pre-release consensus/guide, while non-GAAP losses widened versus expectations. More importantly, the call signaled worsening structural cost pressure into 2027 and no fresh deal/timeline certainty (no STM update; no PowerAmerica win), which the note framed as the key swing factor—making this a downside surprise despite some technical/milestone positives.

Revenue and non-GAAP margin came in slightly above the guidance-anchored expectations, but ARR/NRR disappointed (NRR 102.4% with FX normalization only) and management flagged elongated mega-enterprise sales cycles pushing ~$8M of deals out of Q2. FY guidance was maintained, and the key platform-pricing datapoint (17% of eligible ARR) largely supports the existing thesis without a clear re-acceleration.

Headline gross margin and EPS benefited materially from IEPA tariff refunds/settlement reserve releases, with underlying operating income far weaker than the reported figure. Revenue also missed the pre-release base case driven by a sharp Products decline, while platform growth (subs/ARPU) was not enough to offset margin pressure, implying a negative/less certain trajectory.

Q2 delivered a clean operational beat (revenue above the high end; adj. EBITDA $363M above the $310–350M guide range, with synergy actions ahead of plan). However, guidance for Q3 substantially undercuts the Q2 momentum (rev and adj. EBITDA below Q2 actuals), and the pre-release note highlighted that guidance shortfalls—especially around synergy timing and platform migration—would drive negative repricing. Agent adds fell (though retention improved), adding to caution despite strong demand/outperformance.

EPS beat the note/consensus mechanically, but the key guidance held (FY adj. OI midpoint $2.2B; EPS $14.65) and management reiterated/leaned into RPT pressure (commercial-mix headwinds, ~1–2% FY RPT with slightly negative H2). With the stock already priced for near-perfection after two prior big gaps, the mix of beat-with-no-raise and soft underlying puts reaction near-median.

Q1 revenue, EPS and operating income all beat the note (and guidance was raised). However, the big negative is margin: Q1 gross margin fell to 61.6% (below what the note implied near-guidance performance), and Q2 usage growth is explicitly slowing to 30–35% YoY, a deceleration signal that has historically driven EGHT’s stock swings.

Headline revenue and GAAP loss largely track the note’s “scripted” down-quarter setup, and guidance was reaffirmed. However, tail (net adjustment) revenue materially undershot and management lowered the FY26 tail outlook, and the Q3 setup indicates even steeper enrollment/revenue declines—offset only partially by improved Q2 cash flow and stronger ancillary cross-sell. Net: negative surprise vs the note’s base/bull triggers, but not a total guide-collapse due to reaffirmation.

Headline EPS and margin beat were driven by a large tariff-refund benefit (700 bps; $0.52 EPS). Underlying performance weakened (Water margin down ~700 bps ex-refunds) and management lowered full-year EPS excluding tariff benefits to $2.70–$3.00, plus guided Q3 EPS and margin to be pressured—an unfavorable combo for a stock already priced for a near-term upside tail.

Q2 revenue/EPS beat and profitability/FCF trajectory held up (24% non-GAAP margin, Rule of 40), with EX ARR at 24% and NDR ~flat into Q3. The main market swing factor in the pre-note was FY confidence and CX stabilizing; while management guided toward strong FY FCF/FCF/share, the CX narrative remained low-single-digit and thus limits upside re-rating on this specific release.

Headline EPS was $0.84 vs $1.09 consensus (miss), but FY funded volume and FY adjusted EPS guidance were reaffirmed (no upgrade/trim). Underlying origination momentum (funded volume +21%, retail leverage) and the Onity MSR mid-teens yield offset some concerns, yet the quarter’s results were heavily affected by a $42M tax benefit and large GAAP fair-value noise, while Q2 EPS came in far below the bridge the note expected—keeping sentiment mildly negative rather than sharply.

Q2 underlying RLA and adj. EBITDA came in strong vs the guidance midpoint, but the setup was already “priced” around an in-line print with potential FY6 growth defense; more importantly, gross margin dropped sharply (−450 bps) and the FY outlook now expects full-year gross margin decline to be more persistent than implied earlier. The guidance raise supports the stock, but margin compression and the more explicit H2/U.K. deceleration temper upside, pointing to a modestly positive-to-middling reaction.

Q4 itself was comfortably strong, but—per the note—the stock was really trading on the initial FY27 guide and cloud growth quality. FY27 revenue midpoint ($658.5M) is slightly above the $656.3M consensus anchor and cloud ARR/NRR strength plus quantified Celeste AI contribution argue against a bear narrative, though license revenue decline is consistent with prior concerns.

Revenue and demand/mix indicators (ADS +9.3%, AOV +10%, Canada +33.7%) came in ahead of the Street’s base case, but non-GAAP gross margin (34.7%) matched the pre-release worry about compression rather than reversing it. EPS is effectively inline given consensus already assumed a large Y/Y EPS decline on margin normalization; guidance kept margins flat for the rest of 2026, limiting upside.

Q2 revenue was slightly below the expected range but EPS landed at the guidance midpoint. Key driver (Q3 EPS inflection) comes in at $0.37-$0.39 (midpoint $0.38) and gross margin steps up (to ~46-47% in Q3), which avoids the bear outcome the note emphasized; balance-sheet/OCF was also strong. Since the market already expected guidance to be the fulcrum and the stock wasn’t positioned as “priced for perfection,” the reaction is modestly positive rather than a beat-and-run.

KTOS posted a larger-than-expected revenue/earnings-power quarter and raised FY26 organic growth to 19–23% (above the prior range noted in the preview). However, management flagged meaningful second-half margin headwinds from FX, and cash flow remained negative on prepayments—offsetting some upside after the stock’s prior drawdown.

Kodak delivered a clear upside on the metrics the note emphasized (revenue, gross margin, and especially operational EBITDA), and liquidity/deleveraging improved. However, the note warned that GAAP results can swing on non-operational items and that AM&C growth had decelerated; while AM&C re-accelerated this quarter, pension income headwinds and higher silver-driven inventory add some uncertainty. With limited guidance context and no real consensus in the note, the reaction is modestly positive rather than a “beat-and-raise” type move.

The reported Q2 directionally supports the note’s margin/mix thesis (GOS margin 345 bps vs 330–360 guide; home-equity pivot profitability improving), and management monetized servicing rights and reiterated a supportive Q3 margin outlook (360–390 bps). However, the release did not provide enough detail to confirm a revenue/EPS beat versus the (low-confidence) $339.5M / +$0.03 consensus anchor, and Q3 lock/lock-volume range remains consistent with the note’s pipeline-drawdown risk, limiting upside for the highly levered narrative.

LMAT missed Q2 sales guidance and guided FY revenue down (organic growth cut) despite EPS broadly meeting. Margin expansion and higher Artegraft mix helped, but the market’s core focus in the note was getting the sales line higher and de-risking unit-driven growth; the continued export/supply/headwind narrative is a negative for expectations.

Headline FY2026 numbers largely match the already-preannounced setup, but FY2027 guidance stayed cautious (revenue per enrollment flat-to-slightly up, flattish gross margins, mixed early enrollment signals) while gross margin fell due to platform investment and Roscoe remains a known/quantified pressure. Net: modestly positive at the margin versus low expectations, not a true beat-and-raise setup for a big rally.

Revenue was essentially in line, while adjusted EBITDA/margin beat expectations. However, Tinder MAU remained weaker and E&E declined sharply (Azar headwind only partially offset), and key forward demand/investment narrative did not visibly improve enough to drive an upside re-rate versus an already priced-in setup.

Underlying Q2 strength (record revenue, higher GM/op margin) was already the base case for the quarter, but the key risk in the note was the consolidated Q3 AMI stub—Lattice guided Q3 combined revenue $245–265M (mid $255M) and EPS $0.54–$0.58 with margin/FCF-accretion narrative intact. The stock’s heavy prior run-up and very high valuation keep the reaction modest despite the guidance beat.

The quarter looks largely in line on the revenue/EPS lines (which were effectively pre-guided), but the call delivered stronger-than-expected operating traction: higher contract signing (multi-year high / ~5x YoY), acquisitions up sharply, and contribution margin at 5.8% supported by sharply lower marketing spend. However, Q3 guidance is directionally consistent with the note’s base case (CM down to ~4–4.5%), limiting upside.

Revenue and adjusted EPS beat the (functionally higher) pre-release expectations, and guidance was raised with margin/FCF improving. While demand tied to the post-Mythos AI threat was framed as early-stage (limiting upside narrative), the key “ETM monetization” indicators improved (billings/NDR, ETM mix), offsetting the historically high bar for this stock setup.

Despite reiterated FY guidance, underlying profitability missed hard: adj. EPS at $0.01 vs consensus $0.03, driven by lower gross margin and higher opex. Revenue growth and brand updates are roughly in line, but margin contraction and the weak EPS print (not a one-off) outweigh the acquisition contribution and keep the market focused on the credibility of the back-half earnings ramp.

Q4 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat the high end of guidance, and FY26 acceleration + strong ARPC/client growth were positives not fully assumed in the bear/base setup. However, the key event risk was the initial FY27 guide: management guided to ~7% total revenue growth and ~8% recurring growth (below the preview’s ~$1.89B / ~7.5% expectation with deceleration emphasized), with flat workforce plus 25 bps rate-cut assumptions. Overall that mix suggests a small net fade/near-median reaction rather than a strong relief rally.

Underlying profitability remains pressured (Adj. EBITDA down, cash profile driven by special items/divestiture timing), but PCF momentum is better than the note’s base framing: new $13B PCF deals and Q2 PCF revenue/cash strength (with a pulled-forward milestone), plus NaaS adoption metrics improved. Net effect is modestly positive versus the already-prepared bear/base setup, despite margin/cash still looking light on the quarter.

Revenue was materially above consensus ($214M vs ~$181–182M), with CRYSVITA and other key products accelerating, while the company reaffirmed full-year revenue and R&D/SG&A guidance. EPS losses were much smaller than expected, and underlying operating cash use improved sequentially, supporting the rebound narrative rather than requiring guidance relief to make the quarter work.

Revenue beat the ~$417.8M consensus, and the guided Q3 revenue growth (+7% to +11%) sits modestly above what was needed from consensus. However, gross margin fell to 20.7% (below the 21.1%–21.5% recovery zone highlighted as the credibility test), and the release attributes margin weakness to non-recurring workers’ comp favorability plus mix; the second key setup—Q3 margin trajectory—remains the market’s worry, driving a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction for an already well-rerated name.

Headline revenue roughly tracks the preview’s expectation that the quarter would look around ~$355–370M equivalent on known deliveries, but underlying profitability deteriorated (gross margin hurt by a large impairment; Adjusted EBITDA worsened). More importantly, management explicitly warned production/delivery will be below current consensus and withheld formal FY guidance until year-end, which is consistent with the bear scenario rather than a clean reinstatement—driving a negative skew despite liquidity runway language.

Top-line and EPS came in well, and the large-contract cohort growth plus multi-solution mix strength argue demand is durable. However, the key “bar” in the note was cRPO/retention and the market already expected an EPS beat; guidance was margin/FCF-forward and revenue guidance was largely inline, so upside is capped versus a larger re-rating catalyst.

The quarter delivered a clear upside on the key monitored volume line (record 9.5k net adds vs ~8.4k expected) and strong profitability/margin expansion, but GPV per location was flat (World Cup benefit noted) and the EBITDA beat was partly aided by an unanticipated ~$10m tariff refund. Guidance was raised in a way that appears broadly consistent with the market’s base expectations rather than a decisive acceleration vs the H2 bridge concern, limiting upside to the stock.

Results were far above the note’s base-case on both revenue and EPS, driven by an unexpectedly large IP licensing settlement and strong Benchmark/Cherokee contribution. While Deflecto was weak on EBITDA, management guided to operating leverage from inventory digestion; with the market tightly focused on an IP monetization/buyback catalyst, this qualifies as a genuine upside surprise rather than routine execution.

Underlying results (ex-cat) and margin trends were strong (record earnings; Lifestyle +21% adj. EBITDA; Housing ex-cats +18% aided by better non-cat loss ratio). The key upside is a full-year outlook raise vs the note’s base of reaffirming low-/high-single-digit underlying growth; no notable underlying negatives surfaced (placement rate flat YoY but explained by client transfer).

Q2 headlines were broadly in line on revenue (slightly soft residential AC demand) while adjusted EBITDA came in above expectations on mix/cost and TiO2 pricing strength, but management reaffirmed full-year targets and the key risk in the pre-note (H2 bridge/leverage path and TSS margin pressure) was not visibly removed. With a volatile, previously weak stock reaction history, the mix of modestly better operating details but no clear guidance kicker points to a near-median/limited positive move.

Headline earnings were roughly as expected given the pre-announced soft start, with FY27 FCF ($~180M) and the EBITDA/revenue framework reaffirmed. However, underlying margin still declined (adj. EBITDA down 7% Y/Y; fixed services revenue fell 27% with stabilization deferred until after ViaSat-3 F2), and there was no deliverable catalyst (e.g., F2 timing/FCC update or DAT separation decision) despite the post-Hughes-bk momentum run, creating mild downside/mean-reversion risk.

BLMN delivered a sizable EPS beat and expanded operating margin, plus it raised FY26 adj. EPS guidance to $0.90-$1.00 (above the $0.75-$0.90 prior range) — a clear upside vs the note’s “raise not guaranteed” setup. However, the key re-rating debate (traffic shortfall/Outback dynamics) remains mixed (traffic still down; mix improvements emphasized), and Q3 guide includes a tax-rate-driven loss, tempering conviction—hence a near-median reaction rather than a blowout.

Q2 headline EPS/revenue beat, and the FY26 adjusted EPS guide was raised, but the pre-release note already expected a raise and flagged the market focus on HCB MBR conservatism and whether the raise was “big enough.” The reported HCB MBR was affected by favorable prior-year development/exchange updates, reducing the quality of the margin beat versus what the note was waiting to see; 2027 commentary also highlighted headwinds (Caremark membership/retention/340B). Net: modestly positive, but likely more “proof it’s still on track” than a fresh re-rate catalyst.

DT beat the top and bottom lines and also outperformed its Q1 margin/EPS guidance; unlike the pre-release setup where a beat-without-guide-improvement was expected to be a fade, management raised full-year non-GAAP EPS guidance and maintained the ARR CC trajectory. The market still had a downside skew from prior May caution, so reaction is positive but not maximum.

Q2 showed clear upside on revenue, GMV, and especially adjusted EBITDA margin versus both consensus and guidance—highlighting operational leverage. However, the key demand metric (active buyers -10% from Q1) stayed weak, the company lowered its full-year revenue take-rate outlook (24–25% vs 25–26%), and it flagged likely negative FCF for 2026 due to an accounting/payment reclassification—so despite the GMV acceleration and outlook upgrade, the quality of the profit/buyback story is less clean than expected.

Q2 results beat expectations across revenue/EBITDA/EPS, and—critically—FY guidance was raised (organic growth, EBITDA, EPS) plus gross margin expanded. While the pre-release note flagged a low H2 bar, management confirmed acceleration via strong U.S. Pet/Zenrelia & Quattro momentum and raised the innovation target; the main offset is higher Q3 OpEx (+~11% CC) and seasonally weaker second half language, which limits upside. Revenue/earnings upside vs consensus drives a positive but not extreme reaction given prior positioning and already-low bar.

Q2 revenue largely matched the pre-set trough (non-charging down but charging revenue up 19%, 18th straight double-digit growth). The key negative was the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut to a larger loss (negative $25M to negative $5M) with Q3 still negative—worse than what the note assumed would be reaffirmed/only modestly changed. The better charging momentum and Tesla V4/Magic Dock deal were offset by softer underlying throughput drivers and weaker profitability outlook.

The headline quarter wasn’t meaningfully better than what the note framed: EPS came in at $0.72 (near the $0.64 consensus) but underlying margin and profitability deteriorated (gross margin down; adjusted operating income/EBITDA down). Guidance was reaffirmed at the midpoint (still broad), so investors mainly reacted to the deal-opportunity narrative—kept intact—but not to improving fundamentals.

Despite merger-context noise, the print delivered strong AUM/A and net flows with an EPS operating outcome roughly in line with expectations (non-GAAP $1.70 vs $1.66 consensus). The notable improvement was higher AB performance fee guidance (and overall growth narrative), but the move was not a clean upside beat because some underperformance came from alternative portfolio lag/below-plan drag and the call emphasized a neutral-to-slightly-positive near-term impact from the Employee Benefits sale rather than a major earnings expansion.

FRPT delivered an above-consensus Q2 (notably despite slight unfavorable price/mix) with expanding margins and raised FY26 sales and adj. EBITDA above the expected reaffirm range, plus a higher 2027 gross-margin floor. The only meaningful caution is higher-than-expected logistics costs, which were already a risk but partially offsets upside.

Q4 and underlying margins/ARR were better than consensus (revenue above the top end; gross margin expansion; SaaS ARR positive with Platform ONE bookings ahead of target). The key is FY27 guide: revenue midpoint ~ $1.39B (roughly in-line to modestly above the note’s ~1.36B Street/base range), but it still does not clearly validate the bull reacceleration needed to justify a further rerating after the stock’s run; Q1 guide implies sequentially flat revenue.

Headline Q2 revenue/EPS were essentially in line with the note’s framing, but management cut FY outlook to the low end (midpoint $13.70 vs $13.82 consensus) and explicitly baked in persistent Middle East travel headwinds. With the stock already near highs and priced for the Worldpay/margin narrative, the guidance reset is the main negative driver.

Q2 headlines beat (revenue above the high end; adjusted EBITDA/margins well above the low end) and guidance was raised. However, the pre-release bear case was specifically about margin collapse in H2 and inorganic growth masking organic softness—PathFactory helped, but management still flags continued headwinds/attrition and defers meaningful AI revenue to 2027. Net: upside surprises exist, but the growth-quality concerns temper the reaction.

Q2 RYTELO net revenue came in above the ~$55.3M consensus while management reaffirmed FY26 opex and moved RYTELO guidance to mid–high end (a mild raise vs the note’s “defend the range” setup). However, gross-to-net rose to 20.7% and management is still only evaluating an IMPACT MF interim threshold (no clear tightening/acceleration), limiting upside—so the reaction is likely around median/choppy.

AFFO was ~0.76/sh and adjusted EBITDA ~320M, beating the note’s modeled bogeys, and the company raised full-year AFFO to $2.80-$3.05. However, same-store NOI still came in negative and management also guided to tougher y/y comps in Q3 with multiple offsetting negatives (FX tailwind diminishing, container volume softness, and GIS outlook lowered), plus a major fire drag expected in Q3-Q4—limiting upside reaction despite the raise.

Q2 revenue was essentially in-line and adjusted EPS came in below the note’s implied consensus range, though margins expanded strongly. The key negative was the cut to full-year U.S. Omnipod growth (to 17–19%) driven by weaker Type 2 retention/utilization, plus a mid-teens constant-currency exit growth framing—materially worse than the note’s base/bull paths—driving a negative expected tape despite good gross margin.

EPS and several revenue lines beat (notably digital ads and digital subs), but underlying operating costs ran above the 8–9% guide and Q3 digital subscription growth was guided below recent trends. With the stock priced for strong subscriber execution, the deceleration in Q3 plus margin/cost overrun likely drives a negative-to-muted reaction despite headline beats.

Q2 sales and adjusted EBITDA came in stronger than the note’s ~$370–385M/~21% zone and direct delivery returned to growth one quarter early. However, FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance was held (no improvement), which limits upside given the stock’s run-up into the print; tone also acknowledged ongoing margin pressure from freight spot rates.

Underlying quarter financials weren’t provided versus the pre-print consensus (so beats/misses can’t be scored), but the company meaningfully lowered 2026 cash opex guidance to $375M (comforting the FY26 < $390M runway narrative). Management also reinforced platform/portfolio execution via Genentech target validation and provided additional REC-4881/REC-7735 updates without any runway deterioration—overall supportive for a stock still levered to the next discrete catalyst window.

Headline revenue slightly beat, but EPS missed and restaurant-level margin contracted to 23.0% despite beef inflation staying elevated. Guidance sentiment leaned weak (management guided to the low end of the EBITDA/net income range), and the credibility/deterioration risk—already central in the pre-announced setup—tips the reaction negative despite no major guidance cut.

Q2 delivered a profitability inflection (non-GAAP op income/net income) and stronger-than-guided gross margin, but the key contested item—Q3 revenue—implied a sequential decline consistent with the pre-release bear/base framing. The big margin beat was partly tied to $13.3M IEEPA tariff refunds (excluded/flagged in the note), and the Q3 guide still suggests volume/mix headwinds, limiting upside reaction.

Revenue and backlog came in better than the pre-set “roughly flat / margin headwind” setup, but adjusted EPS landed essentially inline with the working consensus and gross margin guidance still implies ~200 bps of YoY headwind. Q2 growth guided to mid-single digits (vs flat-ish expectations) supports a modestly positive tape reaction rather than a rerating.

Underlying drivers (gross bookings above the high end of guidance; strong FCF; AV deployment/city scaling progress) were generally the base-case swing variables from the pre-note, so upside is capped. However, the mobility take-rate decline is a real negative (not framed as one-time in the note), partially offsetting the otherwise strong demand/EBITDA tone and keeping the reaction near-median to mildly positive.

Headline revenue and EPS were broadly in-line given the known ODM/net-commission accounting reset, and management maintained FY26 guidance. Positives were margin expansion and strong Retail/recurring mix, but VCP remaining contract value (RCV) and Restaurants/SMB weakness looked weaker than the note’s “watch” thresholds, creating a mixed setup where a modestly positive tape reaction is more likely than a clear beat-driven rerate.

Management reiterated FY revenue/adj. EBITDA and FCF guidance; underlying EBITDA performance was close to the guidance-implied cadence despite headline optics (net revenue up but EBITDA down). Experiential execution was strong, but Branded and Retailer economics remained pressured and free cash flow still reflected elevated DSO—limiting upside versus what the pre-release note feared.

Q2 delivered a clear bookings and revenue outperformance plus materially higher adj. EBITDA margin (36.4%) and a sizable FY26 FCF guide raise to at least $480M (above the note’s base path). However, the Q3 guide implies deceleration in both bookings and revenue versus Q2, partially offsetting the upside; additionally, eGate coverage is still only >70% (below the note’s ~80% target), which is a negative catalyst even though margins are expanding.

AMPX delivered a clear beat on revenue and improved margins (27% vs 20% in Q1; above the note’s 23–24% base). FY26 guidance was raised for both revenue (to at least $140M vs prior $130M) and gross margin (to 28%) while reiterating >$4M adj. EBITDA. The main offset is limited concern from the expected-in-setup pressure on the margin/EBITDA path, but the raised guide and margin recovery point to a more favorable outcome than the note’s base case.

Q2 revenue and non-GAAP EPS trajectory were broadly in line with the note’s base expectations (CB-3/HPC-driven setup largely matches). The key added positives (Hawesville/Anthropic contract details and Abernathy sale cash timing reducing immediate equity risk) are supportive, but underlying profitability worsened materially (adj. EBITDA much more negative), which offsets the headline comfort—yielding a modestly positive, not a “beat-and-raise” style move.

Headlines are pressured: Q2 revenue declined further (~-11% y/y) with a large network revenue drop and service request/lead declines, which reinforces the bear thesis even though margin commentary was slightly supportive (July margin above Q2). The non-cash impairment is one-time and doesn’t help; importantly, the company did not reinstate guidance and reiterated that accelerated growth is targeted for 2027, leaving near-term uncertainty as the dominant driver.

Q2 revenue/EPS were roughly in line to slightly below the note’s setup, but the key swing factor was the FY26 adj. EBITDA guide cut. Despite a record Q2 and backlog strength, management explicitly pushed the remaining EBITDA to be heavily back-loaded (more in Q4) and lowered full-year guidance, which contradicts the note’s “maintain/upper-half” bull requirement for margin recapture.

Q3 revenue/EPS exceeded both thin consensus levels and company outlook, and full-year revenue guidance was raised with improved organic outlook. However, margins remain a work in progress (EBITDA margin only modestly up vs prior quarter, and SMS gross margin fell sharply), with Q4 organic revenue still expected to decline low single digits—offsetting what could otherwise be a stronger beat-and-raise reaction.

The quarter missed on adjusted EPS ($0.38 vs ~$0.47 consensus) and—more importantly—FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance was cut (midpoint ~$875M vs prior $890M; below the $885–915M expected range) citing cost pressure/deferrals. Despite decent utilization (94.4%) and >70% contract ops margin (71%) plus a new 8-year 665k hp contract and dividend raise, the guidance reset and AMS revenue drop drive a negative reaction.

ORLADEYO growth and improved reimbursement/peds prescribing were better than the note’s base-case (which already assumed conservatism on guide). Most importantly, total revenue guidance was raised meaningfully versus a Street already above the top of prior guidance, while non-GAAP cost guidance was cut, pointing to underlying margin expansion; the only offsets are that ORLADEYO revenue itself looks only modestly above the note’s ~$161M consensus baseline and the navenibart upfront boosts headline revenue.

Q3 revenue and Land growth were broadly in line with expectations, with customer metrics improving. However, underlying adjusted EBITDA was guided/impacted by a non-recurring $16m self-insurance charge and a fuel headwind, and—more importantly—full-year adjusted FCF was cut materially (to $70–80m from $100–115m), pulling the 2H cash/EBITDA conversion narrative into question versus what the market expected.

CDW beat on EPS and gross profit dollars, and raised FY guidance modestly—positive. However, guidance still flags weaker gross margins in 2H and services growth was only +1% (hardware-led), which directly targets the margin/quality concerns in the pre-release note, capping upside despite the headline records.

Headline results and especially Experiences momentum (record revenue and raised OI guidance to the high end) and parks volume (3% attendance growth) are stronger than the note’s base/bear concerns. However, the note already highlighted Disney’s high beat frequency and guidance reaffirmation as the base case, and key Q3 consensus levels aren’t provided in the facts, limiting how much the quarter alone can surprise versus expectations.

Q3 broadly met expectations (revenue and adjusted EPS essentially inline), but the operational narrative was better: USHS OI accelerated (16% to $966M) and margins expanded. Guidance was raised only slightly (and the pre-note suggested the raise could be buyback-driven), so upside is capped; offset by renewed caution: weaker U.S. and International revenue growth outlooks and a modeled MWI/Covetrus closing headwind for FY27.

Revenue came in slightly above the high end, but the release confirms the key solvency/contract risk in the note (cash below the $15M covenant and a direct margin covenant breach requiring waivers). Gross loss worsened and Q3 EBITDA loss guidance implies continued profitability pressure, only partially offset by stronger bookings and the new ELOC. Overall: more negatives than positives versus what was feared/positioned for.

Q2 headline revenue and adjusted EPS were roughly in line with the pre-release consensus. The main incremental positive was materially stronger commercial momentum (wins +30% YoY, record pipeline) with leverage improving, but guidance midpoints were maintained/tightened with no new upside—limiting upside surprise versus what the market already anticipated.

Headline results show organic revenue growth and higher EPS, but adjusted EBITDA margin of 25.9% is below the note’s expected ~27%+ step-up, implying a weaker underlying margin trajectory. Full-year revenue/EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed, so the reaction is likely muted/negative rather than a sharp selloff—especially with deleveraging and interest guidance help offsetting some concern.

Revenue was essentially exactly where consensus/positioning implied (revenue pre-announced). The key delta vs the pre-release base was guidance narrowing to the $300–350M range framed as consolidation (a negative demand/cost-visibility signal) and persistent adjusted profitability pressure (Q2 adjusted EBITDA and product adjusted gross margin still deeply negative), with increased concentration risk around Frontier. Although gross margin improvement continued and cash/free-cash-flow conversion looked strong, the earnings story remains a margin-and-cash execution risk rather than a clean upside beat-and-raise.

Headline performance is largely in-line with the pre-built trough-quarter setup (reaffirmed FY27 revenue flat/down 2% and adjusted PTI/FCF ranges). Upside is that signings were stronger than feared (Q1 signings 3.9B), but EPS/margins reflect the expected workforce charge and revenue is only modestly better, limiting the upside; downside catalysts (guide reset, FCF disappointment beyond tolerance, new control/SEC issues) were not reported.

Quarterly net sales roughly matched the $172.6M consensus, and EPS appears near consensus, but underlying profitability deteriorated: adjusted EBITDA margin fell sharply to 19.6% versus expectations of ~21.5–22%, driven by higher tariffs and a non-repeat. Free cash flow was stronger but largely benefited from a one-time IEEPA tariff refund, and guidance was only reaffirmed. Overall, the print is neutral-to-slightly positive versus the already-cautious setup, with reaction capped by margin/FCF quality concerns.

Headline collaboration revenue was far above consensus (mostly milestone/option-fee accounting), and the company also pulled forward BROADEN-2 timing into year-end 2026—both were largely expected in the note’s bull/base framing. However, R&D came in materially higher than implied by the pre-note range (22% sequential growth), and the guidance centers on timeline delivery rather than incremental business upside beyond what was already anticipated, keeping the net reaction near neutral.

Q2 revenue and software were modestly above the pre-release consensus/guide (software $36.8M vs ~$36.1–37.1M). More importantly, management raised FY26 revenue and software guidance and gave materially better Q3 adj. EBITDA—offset only partly by the ongoing view that higher ingest-fee headwinds could emerge under the new platform model. With the stock already down sharply and a bear/soft-guide narrative pre-priced, the net setup reads neutral-to-positive rather than a large upside beat.

Q2 EPS and operating margin materially beat the note’s $2.42 whisper (EPS $2.70, margin +110 bps). However, the guidance action is a clear cut: FY26 RV shipment forecast lowered to 280k-300k (toward the bear/base in the note), and FY revenue/EPS guide trimmed to $3.9-$4.1B and $8.25-$8.75, offsetting much of the upside from the quarter.

Revenue beat was notable vs the pre-release yardstick (record quarter, even after some pull-ahead). The key margin uncertainty also resolved positively with GM at 44.1% (above the 43.5% “past highs” threshold). EPS beat similarly supported the print. However, the Q3 guide implies sequential softness and explicitly acknowledges additional pull-forward and seasonality, capping upside reaction versus a pure beat-and-raise scenario.

Reported Q2 cleared the high-end of the guide and beat the note’s “whisper” expectations (especially adj. EBITDA and WAU), with a full-year guidance raise plus a solid Q3 revenue/EBITDA range. The note already expected a beat cadence, but the magnitude—record EBITDA and all-time-high WAU with acceleration in self-serve—supports an outsized positive re-rating despite the stock being less than “priced for perfection.”

FY26 net sales guidance was raised modestly and adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised back to the pre-May profitability range, aided by CMS reimbursement restoration; however, underlying Q2 gross margin was still pressured and management guided to slower core organic growth in 2H (2–3%) with EU MDR creating a 2027 headwind, offsetting the bullish guidance read-through. Overall reaction looks near-median to slightly positive versus an event that was already largely framed around CMS reversal and guidance asymmetry.
