Q2 net sales and multiple growth drivers beat, and organic guidance was raised (above the note’s expectations), which should be supportive. However, margins contracted materially (gross and operating down ~120/210 bps) tied to manufacturing costs and channel investments, and EPS was flat with underlying profitability worsening—limiting upside beyond the modest pre-run/high hurdle setup.

Revenue came in around the low/upper end of the very thin consensus range and gross margin meaningfully recovered (supports the revenue pace). However, EPS stayed at/near breakeven and the quarter still showed an operating loss, plus the facility relocation timeline slipped—an overhang emphasized in the note—so the net reaction looks neutral-to-slightly positive rather than a clean beat/raise.

Underlying margin was strong (record 18.5% EBITDA margin, 70 bp expansion) and EPS growth outpaced revenue, with AMS/DRS delivering a 14th straight mid-teens+ quarter. However, reported organic revenue growth slowed to ~4% with installation timing slipping into H2 (not a “streak-break but a growth decel” signal), and the Malaysia deconsolidation optics/bridge risk were not addressed in the call facts provided; overall this reads as a quality beat with partially offsetting growth-trajectory concerns, leading to a muted/near-median reaction despite a guidance raise.

EPS $1.12 versus $1.08 consensus is a modest beat that likely wasn’t the key event given the merger arbitration setup and the note’s expectation of limited upside. The main incremental negative is management’s second-half buyback pace (~$350M) alongside guidance that Variable Investment Income will remain below target for the remainder of the year, which tempers the quality of the earnings outlook versus what the market was bracing for.

No consensus revenue/EPS in the note, but the company meaningfully cut full-year NOI guidance (midpoint implied -~2.4%) citing delayed industrial lease-up and D.C. multifamily headwinds. The call also highlighted continued weak conversion of signed/negotiation activity and prolonged rent-collection/eviction drag in DC, which is negative versus the note’s key watch items.

EPS beat was aided partly by nonoperating items, but the core momentum improved meaningfully versus the already-set “≥30% sequential” bar. The key upside surprise is the strong DSA bookings/backlog (net book-to-bill 1.9x, backlog $1.97B) plus a raised FY EPS guide and improved margin/outlook for a steep 2H ramp. The main offset is guidance complexity: tax-rate headwinds and a lack of near-term pricing improvement (pricing stable; pricing gains only in 2027).

Reported Q2 revenue and the underlying EBITDA/margin profile look weaker than the market’s expected setup (despite the divestiture-related noise already being widely discussed). Guidance was raised, but the new FY EBITDA range implies only a modest step-up while management flagged separation/working-capital headwinds and Scent normalization in H2, which tempers enthusiasm.

Q2 revenue was roughly in line, but margins collapsed (21.5% GM; EBITDA margin 8%) and ODR organic declined. More importantly, management reset FY revenue up while cutting adjusted EBITDA, confirming the market’s key bear risk (margin/near-term execution), supporting a downside-biased reaction despite bookings strength.

Headline quarter read-through appears largely in line with the pre-print’s “base/in-line” expectations (EPS beat not expected to be the stock-moving item). The incremental $100M spend and improving share/mix narrative were positives, and management reiterated the base investment year / margin trough framing with no major deterioration in underlying trend; thus reaction is neutral-to-slightly positive versus what was already anticipated. Direction is tempered because reported underlying numbers vs consensus and the exact FY EPS midpoint shift were not provided in the call facts.

Q2 beat on both revenue (+8%) and adj. EPS (+9%) versus the pre-release consensus, and EBITDA margin expanded sharply (350 bps sequentially) with synergy progress running ahead of plan. However, management reiterated FY guidance and flagged roofing demand down mid-single digits in the first half with softness expected to persist, plus ag-tech backlog declined materially—limiting upside beyond a modest relief rally versus the note’s concern about the back-half bridge.

Reported value-added sales and EPS significantly exceeded the note’s real bar (VA ~$308M vs ~$301M implied; EPS $1.90 vs $1.60 management-implied). Guidance was raised meaningfully (FY adj EPS $6.80-$7.20 vs $6.00-$6.50 prior), and backlog/FCF improved versus the note’s FCF risk, supporting a strong upside move despite minor one-time help to margins.

Headline Q2 results beat consensus, but Q3 guide is meaningfully weaker versus what the note anchored to: EBITDA margin steps down to 20–22% (from 24%) while Roofing/ARMA point to demand pulled forward and pricing/volume softness, plus Iran cost inflation worsening. Given the event-driven/transaction overhang, the reaction is muted but still negative because the forward trajectory deteriorated versus expectations.

Q2 revenue modestly beat ~$362M consensus and adjusted EBITDA rebounded sharply with expanding High Purity Cellulose margins (19% vs 9% in Q1). EPS loss was essentially inline, and the key swing factors in the note (H2 ramp credibility, pricing power, strategic review timing) were reinforced rather than weakened; the only notable drag was the continued Paperboard segment loss (expected from the setup).

Operating EPS beat ($1.30 vs $1.15 expected), with a stronger expense ratio and higher net investment income. However, management reaffirmed FY underwriting fee guidance ($30–35M) despite only $23M booked in H1, while non-cat accident-year loss ratio worsened on a mix shift—an item the note flagged as a key uncertainty for the stock’s premium multiple.

Revenue came in essentially flat (~$783M) and explicitly below company expectations, while management did not reaffirm/upgrade 2026 revenue growth guidance—keeping the core margin/revenue credibility risk in focus. Filing progress is positive, but the lack of guidance confirmation plus ongoing nebulized pressure/COGS overhang is more consistent with a modestly negative tape than a relief rally.

Q3 underlying adjusted loss (-$0.26) and revenue direction were not reported as a clear beat vs the note’s calibrated expectations to guidance; management reaffirmed both FY26 ($3.90-$4.10) and FY27 ($5.40-$5.60). The key offset is downside: O&M and corporate/interest costs widened, reinforcing the transition-year drag even as Gas Utilities narrowed its loss.

Q2 delivered modest revenue/EPS upside and, more importantly, book-to-bill (1.32) plus a higher gross margin trajectory (22.6% and Q3 GM guided to 24% one quarter early) validate operating leverage. Q3 revenue guidance midpoint ($960M) is above the pre-release $920–950M bar, reducing the main bear risk (soft Q3/order-book slope), though the stock’s run-up and ongoing dilution/FCF drag temper upside reaction.

Q3 headline revenue/EPS and margin (EBITDA margin +30 bps) beat the note, and SSS guidance was raised. However, management guided to persistent higher base-oil/lubricant costs, including Q4 300–400 bps margin compression and only a narrow FY EBITDA margin squeeze (less bad), while FY EPS was capped at $1.70–$1.75 (below the note’s $1.80+ “raise needed” bar). With the stock already positioned for a clean beat-and-raise, the costs/2H margin signal and EPS restraint likely dominate near-term sentiment.

Q2 operating margin and EPS beat with strong buyback/FCF, but the quarter’s setup largely matches the pre-release rubric (autos roughly flat; turbine launch on track). Guidance is raised only modestly on the EPS low-to-midpoint (driven by first-half buybacks) while sales/margin/FCF are maintained and battery remains a stated headwind—limiting upside versus what the market already expected from a priced-for-optionalitiy stock.

Q3 headline revenue and loss are roughly in line with the pre-release setup, but EBITDA contracted and subscribers, while up YoY, were below what the base-case math framed as the key risk check. The decisive incremental item vs the note is the FY26 adjusted EBITDA guide raise to $90–$100M (midpoint +$5M), but that comes with weaker underlying Q3 EBITDA and contracting margin, keeping the expected reaction modestly positive rather than a strong upside squeeze.

Q4 EPS and margins beat on very large favorable raw-material timing, but the key center of gravity—FY27—shows a flat EPS midpoint with weaker cash conversion (~20% FCF/ANI) and a front-loaded timing fade by Q3 plus normalized mid-teens EBITDA margin guidance. Given priced-for-perfection positioning, the beat is likely not enough to offset deterioration in the quality/mix of earnings and cash outlook implied by the guidance.

Despite strong bookings/book-to-bill (notably Sensors 1.44 and record Sensors bookings) and a humanoid robotics production ramp signal, revenue came in below expectations ($83.9M vs ~$87.4M). Adjusted EPS also missed ($0.04 vs ~$0.19) and FX headwinds were called out. Guidance for Q3 ($84M–$89M) is effectively in line, so reaction is mildly negative-to-neutral rather than sharply bullish given the multiple is priced on execution.

Revenue came in roughly in line with the pre-release bar, but underlying profitability deteriorated sharply: Adjusted OIBDA collapsed to ~$12M and the company swung to an operating loss, largely tied to BravesVision revenue-recognition/cash-cadence timing. The call did not provide the Q2 BravesVision KPI clarity the note flagged as the main upside trigger, and management effectively reinforced ongoing elevated BravesVision costs and slower cash cadence—incremental negatives into a stock priced near the top of its 52-week range.

Reported results beat consensus on both revenue (+2.7%) and adjusted EPS (materially above the weak $0.30 anchor), with broad margin strength: total GM 17.2% and specialty GM 20% (18.7% ex duty). However, management also guided Q3 structural margin to normalize to 8.5%-9.5%, which tempers the longer-duration narrative versus what the note suggested could hold at higher levels; combined with the stock already running into the print, the reaction is modestly positive rather than explosive.

Headline revenue/EBITDA show weakness versus what the note modeled (Q2 adj. EBITDA $115M vs ~$124–130M base). While FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance is reaffirmed and offset by a higher IMPACT savings target ($70M+), the Q3 setup is “approach Q1” (i.e., not a step-up), volumes are still soft, and revenue is biased to the lower end—features more consistent with a negative/at best contained rerating. Exchange headwind was reaffirmed at $35M (conservation risk stays), despite some mitigation via member migration rather than self-pay.

Headline Q2 EPS (reported $2.45) lands essentially in the same zone as what was largely pre-sold via the May guide and the note’s central case; moreover, FY26 EPS and the ~$700–$800M FCF guidance were maintained. Offsetting negatives emerged vs the note’s implied H2 earnings-risk: additional AC absorption charges ($20M incremental) and the Ibn Sina JV equity earnings miss pushes weakness into Q3, keeping the market focused on H2 credibility and working-capital optics.

Q2 adj. EPS/EBITDA and U.S. RevPAR tracked above the pre-release setup, and—more importantly—management raised full-year guidance for EBITDA and RevPAR, while net rooms are improving to ~1.5%. The only offset vs. the note’s bear risk is that the company did not disappoint on the U.S. unit trajectory.

Headline EPS and results were roughly in line with what the note expected, and guidance was reaffirmed with capex unchanged. Upside came from operational execution (UAE wells, Delaware/Eagle Ford cost declines, Utica synergies), but with FY26 guidance maintained and the stock not signaling a major macro/volume step-up, the reaction is likely modestly positive.

Headline revenues beat the $462.35M consensus, and Performance Chemicals/ Oilfield Services operating income outperformed the note’s base-case narrative. However, EPS did not beat (adjusted ~in line vs $1.06 consensus) and Fuel Specialties margins are explicitly pressured further in Q3 due to the pricing lag—matching the note’s key risk—so the net reaction skews muted.

Management raised FY26 written premium growth to 16–17% and (critically) adjusted EBITDA to $270–280M vs the note’s base expectation of limited upside/mostly reaffirming near the high end. Underlying earnings power looks stronger: H1 adjusted EBITDA +32% and loss ratio discipline held at a 41% loss ratio with combined ratio 88%. Partially offset by retention sliding 50 bps YoY and sequentially, suggesting growth is coming with some quality dilution.

Despite a strong quarter (record revenue, record Data Analytics contribution, higher EBITDA and EPS) and a major FY2026 guidance raise, the setup was priced for perfection after the PREPA headline with essentially no near-term financial impact and possible legal contingencies. The magnitude of the raise is upside, but the narrative risk (long-dated backlog, conservatively excluding Montana Power Services, and thin disclosure on tax/EPS drivers) tempers the next-day reaction.

Revenue came in close to the note’s bottom-up “real” range (5.5–5.7M) and modestly above it ($6.5M reported vs note’s $5.5M base), but the key risk in the note was a strain/backup to the “exceed 2025” FY2026 guide—management reaffirmed that outlook. Offsettingly, gross margin fell sharply (41% vs 46% YoY) with APC margin deterioration, and net loss widened, so the print looks more like a “keep the story alive” quarter than a clean acceleration. Net reaction likely slightly negative-to-neutral-to-mild positive versus what was already expected.

Headline revenue was softer mainly from timing/metal price effects (consciously flagged in the note), while underlying cash generation was strong (FCF near record; site-level FCF records). The notable incremental positives were cost/Greens Creek cash-cost guidance improvement and Greens Creek output/cost guide raise, but Keno Hill production was cut/delayed (bear-case risk), limiting upside for a stock already up ~8% into the print.

Underlying profitability improved (GM +1.3 pts; non-GAAP performance margin +9 pts) and FY guidance was raised, but the pre-release note already expected an at-least-modest revenue/EPS guide lift and highlighted the key asymmetry (oral franchise reality). The release provided supportive Foundayo commentary (prescribers up, new starts improving, volume doubling into late July), which reduces the downside risk, leading to a modestly positive but not euphoric reaction.

Sales came in essentially in line with the note’s base expectations (~$426M vs $425.8M). EPS beat ($1.96 vs $1.81; ~8% upside) with expanding gross margin (35.5%) and Project Apollo savings now at least $25M annualized; the guidance/tailwind is incremental positive versus the note’s base. Frozen beverage was a headwind, but its magnitude and mix were largely telegraphed in the preview, limiting downside surprise.

Revenue and the data-center/critical power ramp commentary (plus ~$40M new awards) beat the note’s near-term margin-bridge concerns, but adjusted EBITDA margin compressed more than expected and—most importantly—FCF guidance was cut to $7–15M, reinforcing the liquidity/covenant narrative. FY EBITDA was maintained while sales were raised, creating an offsetting setup that should temper the upside.

Revenue (+32% YoY) beat the ~$23.56M mechanical consensus and adjusted EBITDA remained strongly positive (7th straight quarter). However, gross margin expansion was partly driven by tariff-related one-time net benefits, and Q1 backlog of ~$24M is below the note’s $30M bull trigger, keeping the upside capped despite reiterated FY27 revenue ($95–97M).

Headline profitability was strong and supported by exceptional margins (capture), but the key differentiator vs the pre-release setup was that Q3 Hawaii capture is guided to fall below the typical 100–110% range—matching the note’s key bear risk (turnaround/lag), compounded by sequential margin softening (July index down). With the stock already priced near the Street target, downside skew dominates.

Revenues beat the pre-note base case (~$8.8M) at $9.3M, bookings came in strong (15.1M; ~1.7x b/b) and the company raised FY2026 growth guidance to 25–30% (from 20–25%). EPS is also much better than the pre-guided $-0.02 to $-0.03 range on an underlying basis. While the gross margin printed below the 40% normalization (39.1%), the quarter’s demand/bookings and the guidance raise dominate.

Despite a reaffirmation of full-year 2026 EPS/adj. EBITDA (already braced in the note), the quarter showed worse-than-modeled profitability with gross margin at 4.9% (vs ~6–6.5% expected) and an additional FCF cut of ~$200M, partially offset by a very large backlog print (nearly $13.9B) and commentary that most legacy renewables are progressing to completion. Overall, credibility and liquidity concerns dominate.

EPS beat was driven largely by IEEPA tariff refunds (underlying EPS roughly in line), while the key disappointment was guidance: full-year ex-refunds margin was cut to 21.3% and free-cash-flow guide was reduced to $600M (below what was needed to sustain credibility). Underlying demand was mixed (AMC strong, but PES weaker/IPS air pocket) and price/cost headwinds persist.

The headline largely matched the pre-release setup (guidance for FY26 adjusted EBITDA affirmed; revenue/EBITDA sequential improved), but there was a key operational negative: Government Services profitability was still pressured by delayed deliveries and transition/penalty costs, only partially mitigated by a one-time jet fuel mechanism. Offset was an important positive—Offshore Energy Services 2026 operating income guidance was raised on stronger rates/activity—yet it likely doesn’t fully close the buy-side concern that the Government Services inflection needed to be visible now.

EPS came in below the already low bar because the alts drag/severance cost in Q2 was worse than the ~pre-announced $1.90 area ($1.51 reported, with ~$0.90 drag cited). While excess capital/cash conversion and stop-loss reserve/claims commentary were generally constructive, the print likely resets disappointment risk within the takeover-priced setup and dampens odds of near-term strategic upside.

Headline earnings are hard to map in the stub-period quarter, but the operational/guidance read-through was better than the note’s base: Q2 volume landed at the top end and management gave a stronger-than-expected Q3 step-up (oil 550k–560k bbl/d; total capex $1.4–$1.5B) while reaffirming/bolstering the $1B+ 2027 synergy target. Dividend raise and renewed buybacks also support a positive repricing; no offsetting margin/cost deterioration was flagged.

While headline EPS/revenue vs the $0.31/$560M consensus are not provided in the call facts, the release delivers the key qualitative items the note worried about: no BP preferential-right gutting of the Shell/Coulomb scope (BP declined) and an upgraded full-year 2026 stand-alone production guide alongside record adjusted FCF/EBITDA. With leverage down and margins described as accretive/expanding, the outcome is better than the note’s bear vectors, though some valuation/positioning risk caps upside reaction.

Headline revenue modestly beat, and IHOP comps were stronger than the feared weakness, but adjusted EBITDA fell (54.2M vs 56.2M) and H1 adjusted FCF collapsed—reinforcing the note’s concern about margin/FCF pressure. Guidance was maintained, yet management explicitly signaled trending toward the low end, which is a negative given the stock’s leverage and cheap multiple.

Q2 operational momentum exceeded the note’s functional whisper: revenue was well above consensus and EBITDA margin expanded sharply (10.4% headline; E&M 10.8%), alongside major backlog growth to $4.55B. Full-year guidance was raised (revenue and EBITDA) even though second-half margin is guided lower (~8.5%), which tempers perfection but still supports an overall positive repricing.

Reported adj. EPS and the exclusion guidance are stronger than the pre-print bar, with logistics (DKL) delivering record EBITDA and management reaffirming DKL/third-party mix while emphasizing better Q3 margin capture from easing backwardation. Offsetting downside risk was that Q2 underlying refining/RVO dynamics appear to be partially offset (RVO adjustment excluded in the call’s underlying view), reducing confidence that the Aug 3 SRE optionality fully shows up here versus what the note most feared.

Q2 landed within EBITDA guidance and the underlying sales/EBITDA narrative (legacy +~11% growth and volume strength) looks on track, but FY guidance was raised in a way the note flagged as largely pre-priced (pass-through and Calabrian mechanics). The main incremental negative is leverage rising to ~2x immediately post-close (no trailing EBITDA yet), which tempers the upside. Net: modestly positive/neutral reaction.

Headline GAAP net income turned positive, but the call attributed it to stronger commodity prices/lower costs and marked turnaround. On the clean metrics, Adj. EBITDA ($85M) and operating cash flow ($60M) were roughly in the pre-release range, but free cash flow was much lower than the note’s expectation (+~$25–35M) and production fell short with mechanical issues, partially offset by the completed Suroriente carry/capital program. No explicit FY26 hedge/EBITDA guidance update was provided in the facts, limiting confidence.

Q2 confirmed the guided trough with improved operating loss and positive operating cash flow, plus stronger bookings and meaningful tariff refund contribution; management reiterated only a moderate full-year operating loss weighted to H2, which is broadly consistent with the note’s expectations, so the reaction is mildly positive versus prior negativity but not a major repricing signal.

The quarter looks underwriting-constructive (combined ratio ~inline-to-slightly better; earned premium up) but the expense ratio remains high (~40.9% vs ~36–37% targets), which reinforces the credibility gap on the expense-program story. Guidance is reaffirmed (~15% Belmont core GWP growth) despite only ~3% growth in H1, and the demand commentary shows intensifying E&S competition with moderating rate momentum—so the print is unlikely to offset the raised bar for premium re-acceleration that the market was already focused on.

Revenue matched expectations (and was largely pre-announced). EPS/headline guidance were maintained at the existing $4.85, which sits slightly below consensus (the note already flagged a likely reaffirm as a mild negative). Underlying operating margin compressed (17.9% vs 20% prior year), partially offsetting tariff-refund optionality; the repurchase authorization is a modest positive but not enough to overcome the conservative guide/margin tone.

Q2 results beat consensus (record revenue/EPS and margin/EBITDA expansion), and FY revenue was raised. However, management signaled ongoing caution on capital project timing (Q3 guide offers no upside vs the Q2 beat), gross margin fell on mix, and leverage/net debt increased sharply—offsetting the beat and leading to a modestly negative reaction versus what the market already expected from the pre-announced guidance sensitivity.

The quarter was largely in line with a market that expected ugly results and already anticipated phosphate volume pressure from prior curtailments. However, the call reinforced worsening underlying dynamics—Q3 phosphate volumes guided lower (1.1–1.4 Mt) and stripping margins expected to decline sequentially—while sulfur costs step up materially, which is slightly more negative than the note’s base case despite incremental reassurance on SG&A and CapEx cuts.

Headline EPS and consolidated EBITDA missed sharply versus consensus and, more importantly, OSB earnings worsened with Q3 OSB EBITDA guided to about -$45M (vs expectations around -$15M). Guidance changes also undercut the earlier trough thesis: CapEx was cut, but Siding margin guidance implies durability is not improving and OSB price assumptions deteriorated (~$12/6% since May). Despite a Siding sales/26% margin showing resilience, the bigger, less-priced-in OSB deterioration drives a negative reaction.

Underlying coal economics were weak (EBITDA down, cash margin down) while 2026 guidance deteriorated: production and sales were cut and capex was raised, implying continued funding pressure for Maven/Brook. Positives (liquidity >$400m, additional buybacks, coal inventory held for better prices, and more non-rare-earth framing for Brook economics) were largely expected from the pre-note; the guidance reset is the new negative driver.

The key delta vs the pre-release note is guidance language: management now expects 2026 EPS in the top half of $2.95–$3.15, citing improved second-half visibility. Underlying Q2 EPS was only modestly above expectations and segment trends are mixed (NWN gas down, Water below plan; SiEnergy strong), so upside exists but is not a clear beat-to-feared outcome given the stock’s de-risked setup and already-anticipated H2 bridge.

Q2 adj. EPS missed consensus/whisper expectations, largely from storm/union-driven O&M pressure (margin contracting). However, full-year EPS guidance was reaffirmed within the prior range ($2.02–$2.07) and the key data-center bill-reduction and pipeline metrics stayed intact, limiting downside reaction versus what was feared in the note.

Reported EPS/operating results were solid, but the key Japan suspension driver came in only modestly better ($105M vs the note’s ~$140–160M expectation) while full-year POJ AOI guidance was maintained ($525–575M). Management also provided no new numerical upside EPS growth target, keeping the setup closer to the note’s base case than the bull case, leading to a near-median reaction.

EPS was broadly inline versus the pre-release setup: the California incremental benefit is landing in Q2 but without a disclosed upside versus the note’s base expectations, and FY26 guidance was reaffirmed. However, the Great Basin expansion capex jumped ($600M) while demand strength is confirmed, offsetting some optimism; overall, guidance stability keeps the reaction near-median.

Q2 EPS came in well above the $0.65 consensus ($0.82 vs $0.65) and full-year adjusted EPS was narrowed toward the top of the prior range (upper half / $4.89–$4.95), with additional Texas HB 4384 contribution. However, management also guided that back-half O&M growth will drop but acknowledged the near-term O&M cost pressure is still present (O&M +6.6% in Q2 and sequential growth expected to fall below target), making the outcome feel partially countered by cost risks already embedded in the note’s back-half-loaded bear case.

The release delivered negative guidance action: management lowered FY2026 outlook due to a more expensive HIYA DTC digital marketing environment and reduced near-term Rise sales, plus additional Rise packaging-related margin/top-line pressure. The goodwill impairment and persistent elevated tax rate reinforce deteriorating underlying conditions, which dominate any cash-flow relief.

EPS of $0.38 non-GAAP matched consensus expectations ($0.38). Management reaffirmed the 5–7% EPS growth through 2027 and the Q1 2027 merger close timing (no incremental regulatory/close-date news provided in the facts), so the print was not a new catalyst versus what the pre-release note already framed as the key swing factor.

Reported results beat the pre-release risk case materially on both consolidated revenue ($396M) and—critically—adj. EBITDA ($93M) vs the company’s own $77–80M guide, with record Water Infrastructure (≈58% margins) and all three segments outperforming. Guidance was also supportive (Q3 EBITDA $90–94M and FY Water Infra growth reiterated; capex raised to $250–290M), which limits downside despite EPS being a likely headline optics issue versus the dispersed EPS consensus.

Revenue and EPS beat the pre-release modeled bar (≥$250M and EPS ≥$0.58). Underlying performance (ex-one-time CERIS settlement) was also strong, and demand indicators (claims volume +8%, new sales +60%) plus continued buybacks reduce downside risk; no guidance change was provided in the facts.

Headline EPS beat was driven by tariff refunds, but the refund magnitude was below the note’s base-case ($15.3M recognized vs $18.6M expected), and management flagged unsustainability of wholesale margin with the incremental tariff rising to 12.5% from July 24. Underlying operating margin/SG&A pressure looks worse than what the note assumed, offsetting the otherwise supportive inventory growth plan.

Q2 beat on both revenue and adjusted EPS, with adjusted EBITDA margin up 150 bps. More importantly, FY2026 revenue and adjusted EBITDAR guidance were raised (midpoints above prior/Street bars) while leverage/liquidity remained strong—an upside outcome not fully captured in the pre-release setup despite the stock trading near its highs.

Headline totals largely align with the note’s expectation that the market was sensitive to bookings/ARR rather than revenue, but the report delivered stronger underlying growth signals (core revenue +14%, ARR up to $65M, >1M installed units expected early). Guidance also reaffirmed an H2 lift and reframed an acceleration inflection, supporting a modestly positive reaction given the micro-cap low bar and previously washed-out sentiment.

Core EPS and underwriting margin improved versus already-modest expectations, helped by a much stronger combined ratio (91.5%) and a large uplift in alternative investment returns (7.1% vs 1.2% last year). The $125M Charleston Harbor gain is a pending/expected item (not in the quarter), so upside is mainly underwriting/investment performance rather than a headline one-off; however, the note already flagged headline noise from timing of that gain, and the quarter’s earnings lift is partly variability from alternatives.

Headline adj. EPS ($9.41) is above stale consensus (working ~$7.40) but is strongly helped by ~$450m mark-to-market gains; excluding those, underlying performance is less of a standout versus an already “peer-strong” setup. Guidance/positioning leans more constructive (higher repurchase/confirmed capture and midstream trajectory), but Asian/Middle East and Russian offline volume + CPChem/chemicals were not addressed as upside, leaving mixed sentiment and keeping reaction near-median.

Q4 beat the already-high guidance ceiling (revenue $8.3B vs $7.60B top; EPS $2.28 vs $1.80 top). More importantly, Q1 FY27 guide is well above the expected ~$1.90/~$2.10 framing in the note (Q1 rev $9.15B vs $7.8–8.0B implied/upper expectations; EPS $2.85 vs ~$2.10+ bull/base). Margin expansion and improving working capital/leverage further reduce the quality concerns around memory pass-through.

Against a note with very limited/fragile consensus, the quarter’s revenue and EPS appear roughly in line with the modeled base case (~$117M rev, ~$0.26–$0.28 EPS) but key operating metrics were better: origination/purchases (implied by $758M originations), delinquencies, and net charge-offs all came in healthier (NCOs 7.28%, DQ 12.16%). With no guidance details provided, the most likely outcome is neutral-to-modestly positive reaction rather than a large repricing.

PLMR delivered a solid adj. EPS beat on Q2 and raised FY2026 adj. net income guidance to $270–280M, but the note’s bear risk was centered on guidance not rising (or any margin deterioration). Management still guided for a rising loss ratio (mid-to-upper 30s) and the adj. combined ratio worsened to 76.7% vs 73.1%—a negative for the growth-at-good-returns narrative—so the net reaction skews mildly negative despite the guidance raise.

Underlying profitability improved (GM/EBITDA up; Trio COGS lowest since 2019) and full-year production guidance was raised for both potash and Trio, but Q2 revenue is roughly flat and EPS is supported by the note’s base case range; moreover the pre-release setup suggested guidance delivery/“in-line with guidance” is often met with a muted or range-bound reaction. Not a clear upside shock versus what the note already modeled for a base case beat.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, so beats/misses on revenue and EPS are unquantifiable. Management reiterated full-year guidance; the key incremental positives are stronger gross margin/ASCENIV performance and a new clinical data point, partially offset by only modest adjusted net income growth from a higher tax rate.

Management delivered a substantial operational beat (Q2 medical margin +197M and adj. EBITDA +$70M) and raised FY26 guidance materially, including the implied H2 air pocket. The key offsets are membership continuing to decline year-over-year and the added risk-adjustment (though still prudent/within their framework) keeping some uncertainty around underlying sustainability versus Q2 outperformance.

Q2 revenue was essentially flat vs the working consensus, but adjusted EBITDA rose 16% and margins beat (61.1% vs ~60%) on tariff-related and full-price mix benefits. Importantly, FY net sales and adj. EBITDA guidance were reiterated (no raise), while Australia/NZ was weak and Q3 outlook implies margin pressure (59% GM, air freight/tariffs) with a Q3 one-off distribution move charge.

Headline revenue landed roughly in-line with the pre-release base case despite a worse Auryxia decline, while Vafseo/VOICE read-through was supportive (early VOICE superiority, >10.5k active patients). However, management reiterated a 2027 Vafseo revenue decline tied to the TDAPA end (pricing down into the lower ESA range), and cash burn/margin look weaker (larger net loss), keeping upside capped versus what the note suggested for a clean re-rating.

Q2 revenue ($80.1M) and non-GAAP EPS ($0.25) beat the derived/anchored expectations, with gross margin holding (80.3%) and strong product momentum (~25% Y/Y, $49M). More importantly, management raised FY26 revenue growth to 12–14% (vs 10–12% expected) and EPS to 14–16% (vs 12–14%), which was the key missing ingredient in the pre-release note.

The company raised FY26 net revenue guidance to $525–540M (well above the pre-print’s $500M Street vs $480–495M prior range), while delivering strong Q2 momentum (23% sequential, 59% YoY) with record >280k prescriptions and improving profitability plus positive operating cash flow. The only notable offset is the CCO resignation (management/process risk), but gross-to-net stability supports the raised trajectory.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. Directionally, the release showed strong volume growth (fourth consecutive quarter of accelerating test volumes), operating leverage, and reiterated FY revenue guidance with very strong gross margin (~82%) and improved losses, which would typically support a mildly positive reaction.

No pre-release note or quantified consensus was provided, so comparisons are directionally inferred. The guidance was modestly raised (midpoint +$1M), but the quarter still showed worsening GAAP losses and a meaningful EMEA revenue decline, partially offset by US growth and improving ex-one-time gross margin.

Guidance was lowered on MEATER softness and near-term channel disruption, which typically outweighs the offsetting gross margin and adjusted EBITDA support; additionally, management highlighted a meaningful Q4 weighting for remaining 2026 results and ongoing retail arrangement evolution (Lowe’s).

Headline underwriting was better than what was guided in Q2, but management guided Q3 adjusted EBITDA to land within range (not beat), citing timing—so the key upside is largely in the past quarter rather than a stronger forward trajectory. With no provided pre-release numbers and no explicit revenue/EPS surprises, the net reaction is neutral-to-slightly positive.

Strong top-line momentum and a clear guidance raise (net sales growth outlook to 18%-20% and adjusted EPS to $3.50-$3.55). Margin performance includes a large EPA tariff refund benefit, but underlying EBITDA growth also remains strong, suggesting the market should respond modestly positively rather than aggressively given limited EPS/revenue consensus detail.

With no pre-release consensus note, the key fresh signal is the Q3 guide: revenue is down and adjusted EBITDA implies a sharp margin step-down (~35% to ~28% midpoint) tied to renewed marketing spend. The Tech 2.0 migration delay (rollout pushed to very early 2027) further pressures the growth narrative despite an underlying EBITDA margin beat vs the high end of current-quarter guidance.

No pre-release consensus numbers were provided, but management reported continued beats versus its own prior high-end guide and raised full-year guidance with margin expansion. However, Q3 implies decelerating gross bookings growth and margin expansion is expected to moderate before improving in Q4, limiting upside for a stock that is likely already expecting strong execution.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but the company lifted full-year revenue guidance (midpoint to $333.5m) and raised full-year gross margin guidance despite acknowledging gross margin was boosted by a one-time tariff refund; underlying EBITDA improved and management indicated businesses remain on track (including Evolysse/international each >10%).

Q3 revenue and adjusted EBITDA came in above the pre-release base-case, and FY26 adj. EBITDA guidance was raised modestly. However, unit sales fell (inventory timing into Q4/2027) and the Micro Bird consolidation explicitly compressed gross/EBITDA margin, making the beat partially optics-driven versus what the note already modeled; net reaction skews modestly positive.

Quarter materially exceeded the company’s own high-end guidance with record margins, large operating profit upside, and retention improvement, and management raised full-year 2026 revenue and operating profit. The main offset is customer concentration rising and some of the revenue upside being episodic/live-event driven, which tempers confidence that results fully normalize.

No pre-release note or quantified consensus was provided, so surprises vs expectations are largely indeterminate. While volume/revenue growth and cash position look supportive, adjusted EBITDA loss widened and management reiterated a potentially confirmatory/long-dated FDA timeline, which tempers the upside.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided. Underlying performance excluding the large Omni goodwill impairment improved meaningfully, with Expedited Freight and Omni Logistics margins up versus a year ago; however, the quarter also includes a very large non-cash impairment and intermodal is targeted for divestiture, tempering conviction on forward run-rate.

Headline earnings and gross margin benefited heavily from a large one-time tariff refund; underlying gross margin was in-line and underlying operating profit is guided to decline high-single digits despite revenue growth. The main incremental negative is the worsening underlying operating profit outlook versus prior guidance and ongoing margin pressure (SG&A/ERP depreciation), which likely caps upside after the one-off tailwind.

Quarterly revenue and profitability improved vs the already-soft expectations, and FY GAAP revenue guidance was raised—helped by margin/FCF and capital actions. However, the key credibility metrics deteriorated vs the note’s base: NRR fell to 89% (not the 90% floor) and downmarket ACV declined further with longer cycles; plus the goodwill impairment is a severe balance-sheet signal. With the stock already rallied into the print, the guide-tone/quality doesn’t fully offset the demand-metric weakness.

While Q2 growth and RPO visibility look exceptionally strong, the call highlights underlying profitability pressure (more SkyWater-related spending/integration costs and worsening adjusted EBITDA) and combined guidance is effectively delayed due to consolidation. The guidance raise is also complicated by excluding SkyWater for the standalone range, limiting signal vs expectations.

EBITDA/margins beat slightly and full-year EBITDA target is reaffirmed, while growth remains supported by improved GGR/turnover commentary. Offsetting concerns are the newly higher UK remote gaming duty depressing interactive margins and management calling out pro-forma (rather than reported) FCF due to a restructuring cash outflow—so overall the setup looks modestly positive rather than a clear upside surprise.

No pre-release consensus figures were provided, so surprise assessment is limited. The quarter showed strong operating momentum (FCF inflection, 31% EBITDA margin, higher volumes) and management raised full-year sales/production guidance, but net selling price realization declined and management cautioned about second-half weaker PLV range and relativities—implying a likely modestly positive but not euphoric reaction.

With no pre-release note/consensus provided, the standout upside is gross margin expansion and an improved gross margin guide, but the revenue outlook was narrowed with international ramps pushed into 2027 plus a US FDA application withdrawal that delays US oncology entry. Net: mixed fundamental signals (profitability/margins positive vs growth/international and timeline negatives) suggest a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction.

Revenue growth and customer momentum (including the largest-ever deal and retention near 109%) appear solid and are not clearly flagged as worse than expected, supporting a modestly positive tape. However, non-GAAP gross margin declined and full-year margin/operating income guidance was cut (despite revenue raise), limiting upside to a near-median reaction.

MGNI delivered beats on contribution and adjusted EBITDA with expanding margins, and—more importantly—raised full-year contribution and EBITDA growth guidance. While Q3 guides to some CTV deceleration and acknowledges managed-service drag, the raise and margin strength likely dominate, leading to a moderately positive reaction.

Although gross margin expanded and the newer multi-month patient mix improved retention/lifetime value, Q2 adjusted EBITDA missed and the company cut full-year and Q4 guidance into loss/breakeven territory, signaling weaker near-term profitability and delayed EBITDA accretion (Zyosted investment into mid-2027).

Headline Q2 performance was broadly in line on revenue but the company cut full-year revenue and sharply guided Q3 to low-single-digit growth, reflecting AI-driven traffic disruption. While EBITDA margin and cost savings improved, the deceleration in top-line appears to drive the reaction lower versus what investors likely expected given the lack of a pre-release note.

EPS beat and a (small) FY27 guidance raise were supportive versus a setup where reaffirmation was the main risk; however, the quarter still included weak Medical-Surgical operating profit and management flagged generics/product timing benefits that unwind later, limiting upside. Net: positive but not an outsized beat-and-raise shock.

Net product sales growth and an improved commercial cash contribution margin support the quarter, but the FDA’s Phase 3 requirement for volixibat that delays the NDA to 1H27 is a meaningful negative catalyst shift. Guidance was raised, but without a pre-release note/consensus, the surprise level is unclear.

No pre-release consensus or guidance was provided, so surprise vs expectations can’t be quantified. Management highlighted rapid marketed-product growth and improving Furoscix margin trajectory, but the quarter also showed GAAP/non-GAAP losses driven by sharply higher SG&A/R&D and meaningful gross-to-net pressure, keeping the net reaction around neutral.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but the release showed margin expansion (gross margin above guidance) and a constructive Q3 outlook with improving working-capital metrics. Despite that, the longer-dated GaN monetization suggests limited near-term upside beyond the margin/demand trend, so reaction is modestly positive.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but results show strong operating leverage (gross margin up to 72.1%), materially improved profitability (EBITDA loss narrowing 79%), and a raised full-year revenue outlook with a solid Q3 range. Mix of improved growth and margin should drive a modestly positive market reaction absent other known risks.

Guidance was lowered for full-year adjusted EBITDA and restaurant-level margins contracted ~190 bps despite hedging; same-restaurant sales declined and traffic headwinds are expected to persist into Q3/Q4. Cash generation and $10–$15m of cost savings are positives, but the underlying profit trajectory looks pressured.

Q2 delivered the expected growth mix (transit +32%, billboard +8%) and expanding OIBDA/AFFO. The key for this setup was FY AFFO guidance: management raised full-year growth to low-20s (vs the note’s base of mid/high-teens and bear of cautious reaffirm), plus an explicit Q3 World Cup benefit—together more positive than what the market feared, though revenue was largely telegraphed.

No pre-release consensus was provided for the financials, but the release delivered clear deterioration/softening: full-year 2026 revenue guidance was lowered, full-year gross margin guidance was pressured with compute/memory inflation and additional transition costs, cash breakeven moved out to 2028, and restructuring was initiated. The only notable offset was progress on Revio/SparkNext adoption (software uptake) and stated chemistry cost-down, but near-term funding/transitional demand headwinds dominated.

No consensus/research-note numbers were provided for revenue/EPS or for the guidance baseline, limiting beat/miss scoring. However, the FDA accepted the NDA/EMA expedited review and expanded access adoption are clear positives, partially offset by guidance-driven cost pressure (higher operating expense outlook) and a substantially wider GAAP net loss driven by R&D/G&A and non-cash warrant fair value changes.

The release delivered a clear guidance cut: 2026 cash generation midpoint moved to ~$287.5M vs the prior ~$350M (about -26%), alongside lowered aggregate subscriber value and continued affiliate volume collapse. While storage attachment hit a record 74% and distributed power economics stayed on track, the underlying guide deterioration is the dominant signal versus what the market expected, implying a modest-to-meaningful negative reaction.

Headline Q2 revenue ($41M) and FY revenue guidance (kept at $65–$75M) land broadly in the range anticipated in the note, and cash/runway guidance remains intact (YE cash near $600M, into 2H2028). The key difference vs the pre-release emphasis is that PEAK-1 and PEAK-20 timelines are confirmed (reducing downside), while the notable potential negative is the ARC-20 readout being pushed to an October/ESMO event rather than a nearer quarter catalyst, keeping expectations from improving at the margin.

Political advertising strength and a raised full-year political advertising figure, alongside a raised full-year adjusted EBITDA despite core advertising crowd-out, is likely net positive. However, the core advertising revenue decline and explicit cut to core guidance, plus Tennis segment EBITDA deterioration, cap upside and point to mixed underlying demand.

Underlying operating momentum looked roughly in-line with the pre-release framework (ACV helped but reported/revenue optics remain distorted). The main true surprise was the raised drug discovery revenue guidance (to $65–75M), partially offset by continued deterioration in software gross margin as hosted mix rises.

Revenue ($15.9M) and RPO ($80.7M) came in above the pre-release base expectations, with data/analytics mix improving and Merlin still on the October launch timeline; operating leverage flipped to positive adjusted EBITDA/operating income. Guidance was effectively reiterated (Merlin timing/cash funding) and there were no notable underlying negatives beyond the still-lumpy Space Systems mix.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations are largely unobservable. Still, the company delivered strong underlying growth (record interventional dry eye, glaucoma growth with utilization/active accounts strength), raised full-year revenue guidance, and narrowed losses, supporting a modestly positive reaction. Tariff-refund/treatment of litigation fee appear to support headline margin/cash, but underlying dry eye margin expansion and lower adjusted cash burn mitigate headline one-timers.

No pre-release note or consensus provided for Q2/earnings metrics; however, 2026 net product revenue guidance was narrowed and the midpoint shifted toward the lower end, and second-half product revenue is guided modestly lower than first half. With limited upside disclosures, the update likely reads as a mild de-risking/near-term conservatism despite steady franchise adherence.

Despite strong underlying operating metrics (gross margin expansion, higher active buyers/orders/new buyers), management lowered full-year revenue guidance and flagged a meaningful 2H promotional headwind. The negative guidance signal likely outweighs the good quarter, implying below-consensus expectations for forward growth.

Despite margin expansion and cash flow improvement, the company cut full-year revenue and—critically—lowered adjusted EBITDA guidance (and Q3 EBITDA outlook) after a reported miss tied to higher marketing spend and a delayed NY relocation. Overall reads as growth deceleration/earnings delivery risk into the next quarters.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so surprises vs expectations can’t be quantified. Still, the print shows subscription AOI up 24% with operating margin expanding to 15% and net pet adds accelerating (18,800; 39% YoY), and full-year AOI/subscription revenue growth remains strong with narrowed ranges—likely supportive for the stock near-median-to-positive.

Headline EPS and FY guidance were raised, but the raises are explicitly driven by a large Q2 one-time tariff refund and tariff benefit embedded in margin. Underlying Q3 framing worsened (ERP orders largely reversing with Q3 sales guide -3% to -4%, more negative than the note’s base expectation), which is the dominant driver for a stock priced near highs with a pre-flagged ERP pull-forward risk.

The key pre-release yardstick was a Cornerstone-inclusive FY26 guidance reset (deal-math midpoint ~$2.1B). Management raised FY26 Adj. EBITDA to $2.025–$2.225B (midpoint ~$2.125B), which is effectively in line with the note’s base-case rather than a clear beat. Q2 underlying metrics were strong, but the guidance reset was largely expected for this event.

With no pre-release note or consensus numbers provided, the main actionable signal is management cutting full-year guidance and attributing a sizable FY2026 EBITDA shortfall to weak Q4 starts and an adverse mix shift. Despite better-than-expected UTI division starts and outperformance at new campuses, the guide reduction and margin pressure likely dominate near-term sentiment.

Reported Q2 revenue/EPS beat and—more importantly—raised FY26 sales guidance and delivered a strong Q3 setup (net sales $1.10–$1.14B; EPS $1.21–$1.27). The key demand indicators (book-to-bill 1.49, N+M mix shift) were better than what the note’s base/bear mechanics implied, so reaction is solidly positive despite some expectations already reflecting an AI narrative.

Q4 beat both guide and (published) consensus, but more importantly the Q1 FY27 revenue guide ($450–460M) clears the pre-release “whisper/buy-side bar” (~$443–448M) and suggests an accelerating path toward the $500M+ calendar 2027 run-rate. Margin expansion and data-center mix progress reinforce. However, the Q1 guide includes a small tariff-refund benefit (one-time-ish) and the equity offering/FCF balance-sheet risk remains an overhang versus the note’s bear triggers, limiting upside to an upper-median reaction rather than “blowout.”

Headline Q2 revenue and net income benefited from the Astellas upfront/equity recognition ($315M cash; $238.9M recognized). Operationally, key program updates (ECLIPSE enrollment completed; SOLSTICE 96-week efficacy and safety) were directionally supportive, but the R&D spike (Sanofi milestone + manufacturing) worsened cost optics vs the note’s “accounting noise” framing. Cash runway into 2H’28 was reaffirmed, limiting downside and keeping the reaction mildly positive despite the EPS consensus being effectively treated as unreliable in the pre-note.

Headline revenue/EPS (loss widened) and especially NEREUS first monetization (only ~$1M recognized vs an expectation closer to a more meaningful early datapoint) were weaker, while cash fell sharply. Although management reaffirmed FY revenue ($240–290M) and guided FNAPT+Basanti sales ($150–170M), the report increased the near-term credibility risk around the cash runway rather than alleviating it, leading to a modestly negative-to-neutral reaction given the stock was already near lows.

Q4 and FY2026 showed strong operating leverage (large margin expansion) plus a Q1/FY2027 guide that implies continued double-digit growth and durable exabyte/price trends. With no pre-release note to anchor consensus, this scores as a broadly positive guide-and-leverage setup consistent with options pricing implying only an ~12% absolute move and some downside protection.

Because revenue/EPS risk was largely removed by the Aug 3 preliminary 8-K, the print itself is mostly a confirmation. Incremental positives came from stronger subscription mechanics (6–7% subs growth, Apple deal coverage expanded) and operating cash flow conversion (55% over nine months), while guidance was reaffirmed including high-end 150–200 bps margin expansion and FY27/AI timing remains “material.” CFO transition did not appear to derail the call.

The quarter met the pre-announced high-end sales and better-than-feared EBITDA, and FY guidance was maintained (so little upside vs the already-de-risked setup). The key incremental item is Q3 guide for gross margin (~46%) and an EBITDA loss widening to the ~$3.25M range, consistent with the note’s bear risks—limiting any positive rerating.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, so the beat/miss can’t be quantified. With only directional qualitative items available (inventory normalization and strong U.S. MIPLYFFA sales offset by continued enrollment/timing uncertainty and regulatory setbacks), a roughly median reaction is most appropriate.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, and the call commentary emphasizes ongoing commercialization progress (sensor wins, optical connectivity JDA) and disciplined opex with flat non-GAAP operating loss. With directionally supportive business updates but no quantified guidance/expectations to benchmark, the event is treated as approximately neutral to modestly positive.

No pre-release note or quantified consensus was provided, so beats/misses vs expectations can’t be measured. Management guided to continued consumer revenue decline in Q3 with gross margin slightly down, offset by an improving AirgainConnect pipeline (greater share in trials/post-trials) and positive adjusted EBITDA, suggesting a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction absent evidence of a larger upside/miss versus street expectations.

Q2 delivered a clear upside on both revenue and underlying profitability: adjusted EBITDA of $23.7M and gross profit swing ($+19M) versus the ~$17–18M EBITDA bar in the note, plus a meaningful 45Z contribution. However, management commentary acknowledged export volume softness from geopolitical/freight headwinds and did not indicate an upsized 45Z framework beyond staying on track for 90M+ gallons—so the “margin/Q3 crush commentary” risk looks mitigated but not eliminated, keeping reaction near-median. No formal guidance changes were provided (aligns with the note’s expectation of no guidance).

With no pre-release note, expectations are inferred: management cut full-year total revenue guidance to $300–320M due to further softening pricing, while reported combined ratio deteriorated sharply (74.3% vs prior period) and E&S/ACES contributions are now behind plan. Offsetting positives (maintained pre-tax earnings guidance, strong book value growth, likely special dividend/buybacks) are outweighed by worsening underwriting/price dynamics and deferred initiatives.

Revenue and operating performance beat the company’s own Q2 guide (tracker-driven growth, improving margins) and the firm raised full-year adjusted gross margin by 100 bps. However, management also flagged second-half margin pressure and potential revenue softness from permitting/site-readiness delays plus weaker free-cash-flow conversion outlook due to collections timing—offsetting the upside and keeping the net reaction near neutral-to-mild positive.

Revenue and EBITDA landed just below the guidance midpoint/range, but margins expanded ~300 bps and Q3 guide implies strong margin levels (around 83%) with management attributing the miss to timing/pace of model improvement rather than demand deterioration. Overall reaction expected to be near-median despite the slight under-in-the-range print; option market suggests moderate move with downside skew.

Organic revenue grew 6.7% (vs consensus implying ~+4.3%) and underlying adjusted gross margin hit 43.8% (above the note’s low-40s expectation). More importantly, management raised FY organic revenue growth to 5–7% and adj. EBITDA to $23–25M (midpoint above the $20–23M range), which meaningfully de-risks the back-half ramp the note focused on; one-time tariff refund boosted headline gross margin, but underlying profitability metrics improved.

Quarterly growth and ARR/retention were solid, and management raised full-year revenue, but gross margin fell materially with AI inference and Statsig integration costs—plus the Q4 outlook implies some deceleration. With no pre-release consensus provided, reaction is judged as modestly positive but constrained.

No pre-release note or consensus figures are available. Results showed strong AI-driven thermal segment momentum (AI mix >40%, book-to-bill ~1.4) and improving gross margin/EBITDA near 15% of sales, offset by ongoing weakness in semiconductor fabrication (down >13% YoY) and no expectation of SiC recovery.

No pre-release note or consensus numbers were provided, but the company raised full-year revenue growth guidance (32%-34% vs prior 30%-32%) alongside strong momentum metrics (ARR +39%, NRR record 126%) and continued bookings strength. Margin benefit was aided by tariff refunds, but demand/contracting indicators point to durable growth rather than a one-off.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so comparisons to expectations are unknown. The company raised full-year system comps/revenue/EBITDA, but management also flagged deceleration in Q3 comps and net margin pressure from higher coffee/occupancy costs, alongside COGS/occupancy headwinds—pushing the setup to a modestly positive but not strong reaction.

With no pre-release note or consensus provided, the dominant surprise from the call is the sharp full-year guidance cut plus worsening underlying trends (procedure revenue still expected to be YoY negative in both Q3 and Q4, gross margin contracting, and elevated clinic attrition). The only positives (cash up, supply continuity restored, supplements growth) appear insufficient to offset the guidance reset.

Underlying quarter was broadly in line, but guidance was trimmed: gross billings growth narrowed (3–4% vs 3–5%) and—most importantly—gross margin guidance moved down to 2.70–2.75% (from 2.70–2.85%), alongside continued client workforce reductions (WSE +1%). With the stock already up ~33% into the print and trading with no valuation cushion, the de-risking on margin drives a negative setup for the next few months.

Revenue landed above the top end of the company’s $60–65M range, but underlying profitability worsened: adjusted EBITDA margin deteriorated and the guide implies a sequential step-down (Q3 $60–65M vs $68.8M Q2). Additionally, cash burn is still material and the EPS improvement was dominated by a large non-operating debt-extinguishment gain (one-time).

Even though margins improved and retention strengthened, the reported growth backdrop is still sharply negative (revenue/billings down ~mid-30% YoY) and free cash flow worsened materially with low cash versus needs. Q3 guide implies only flat sequential performance, limiting upside versus expectations.

No pre-release consensus provided for exact beats/misses, but the call included broad full-year guidance raises and continued margin/operating leverage expansion alongside better-than-initial medical cost trends. The main potential offset is seasonality (Q4 expected loss) and the ongoing CMS appeal of the 4.5-star recalculation, limiting conviction.

Strong quarter with accelerating top-line and meaningful margin expansion, plus guidance raised across revenue/EBITDA/EPS. However, with no pre-release consensus note provided, the magnitude of surprises vs expectations is uncertain; reaction assumed mildly positive rather than extreme.

LOQTORZI Q2 net sales (13.6M, +15% q/q) is roughly in the expected range, but cash fell sharply (105.3M vs the 125–135M implied in the pre-note) and the major value catalysts slipped further: casdo data availability pushed to Q4 2026 (only ~50% of 3 scans) while mature tagmokitug is now projected for October. Management also reaffirmed 2026 revenue guidance, but the FY26 top-line guide (57–62M) remains below the pre-release consensus implied path that required substantial 2H non-product inflows.

With no pre-release note/consensus provided, the clearest actionable signal is guidance: management lowered full-year revenue and EPS and guided Q4 to a sequential sales/EPS decline amid stated industry demand constraints. Gross margin also fell (only partly one-time), and a major customer change drove backlog cancellation and an inventory write-off—together indicating deteriorating near-term fundamentals despite a hyperscale order win.

Record Q1 revenue/EPS and supportive commentary around the HPMS pipeline are offset by sequential gross margin compression and a tighter-than-historical seasonality backdrop, with Q2 guidance also featuring a largely one-time margin tailwind that will normalize. Underlying near-term profitability/demand signals look mixed, implying a near-median tape reaction.

The key seasonally-weighted Q2 CAFD printed at $167M (below the ~$190M note midpoint), and management lowered FY2026 CAFD guidance to $430–470M from $470–510M—moving the outcome closer to the pre-release bear case. Offsetting positives (PPA restructurings across ERCOT projects and repowering/large digital pipeline commentary) were not enough to offset weaker wind-driven cash flow and the credibility hit from a guidance cut.

Headline EPS and revenue beat consensus, but the call delivered key thesis negatives: Dice revenue/bookings and recruitment customer count declined and management guided that Dice bookings will not return to growth in 2026, offsetting the positive CJ pipeline and higher CJ bookings. The stock was already priced for an H2 inflection, so guidance-action appears limited, leaving the market to focus on underlying growth risks.

No pre-release expectations were provided, so beats vs consensus are not measurable; however, management delivered record growth plus margin expansion and—most importantly—raised Q4 and full-year guidance with accelerating EBITDA and ARR trajectory toward the 2028 target. Strong cash generation (100%+ conversion) further supports the positive read-through.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so surprises are inferred from directionally strong results: clear margin expansion, robust sequential/incremental growth, and a relatively upbeat Q3 guide (revenue +30% YoY; GAAP GM to 35%). Demand/inventory commentary also supports durability (inventory days down; below normal channel range).

No pre-release consensus for revenue/EPS was provided, but the company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA margin to 26.5% (and upward gross margin) and issued Q3 guidance consistent with continued mid-teens growth and strong margins, suggesting earnings power strength rather than deceleration. Option skew/volatility implies a moderate-magnitude move.

Despite a strong Q2 driven by accelerated MCM deliveries, management cut full-year revenue/EBITDA and guided to a sharp Q3 sequential step-down amid expected naloxone price erosion and competitive pressure; the impairment and competitive outlook reinforce a negative setup for the stock.

Q2 headline revenue/EPS land roughly in the soft-consensus range, with margins up and growth mix tracking the note. The key compare is the re-guide: FY revenue/EBITDA were raised, but adjusted EPS/FCF were held, which is exactly the bear trigger the note flagged around Celero stub accretion/integration drag. Data growth is still strong in Q2 but management explicitly guided moderation, limiting upside despite the margin improvement.

Quarterly revenue was in-line with guidance, but adjusted EBITDA beat the top end of guidance while management guided the full-year toward the low end, citing slower new customer acquisition. The guide softening tied to acquisition concerns and declining third-party partner revenue likely outweighs the EBITDA margin outperformance for the stock reaction.

Q2 EPS beat consensus (and collections/purchases were strong), and management raised FY EPS and collections guidance with improving cash efficiency/ROIC. However, the pre-release note flagged that the key risk was margin-driven “revaluation” in the beat and guidance reaffirm/caution on a stock already priced for momentum, keeping the reaction closer to median-positive than a large upside jump.

No pre-release consensus/figures were provided, and the company did not reinstate formal guidance due to Iran-driven visibility issues and disclosed megaproject delays/limited backlog usefulness—both increase uncertainty. The 'uniquely strong' MPD pipeline and gradual margin improvement from the low-capex Saudi facility are offsets, but near-term growth timing remains undated.

No pre-release note and no consensus/option-directional guidance means beats/misses can’t be quantified, but the company lowered full-year revenue guidance (midpoint -$50M) citing slower NET patient kinetics—an explicit deceleration signal. This, more than the repurchases, is likely the dominant driver of a below-median stock reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, so surprises vs expectations are not directly quantifiable. However, management lowered the full-year 2026 gross margin target to the low-to-mid 20% range amid persistent pricing troughs and inflationary pressures, while gross margin and net income declined sharply—likely outweighing positives like DLA contract resolution and pricing stabilization.

Despite a strong Q2 headline driven by ~$5–6m pull-forward revenue, management cut full-year 2026 revenue and guided Q3 to weak growth with negative adjusted EBITDA, plus gross margin pressure and further declines in Subscribe services—net negative against market expectations. The guidance deterioration and cash/collections risk likely dominate.

No pre-release consensus figures are available to score revenue/EPS, but the company raised full-year 2026 revenue guidance on Blade strength while noting constrained aircraft availability. The credit is partially offset by a wider underlying Adjusted EBITDA loss and higher cash burn in 2H, keeping the net reaction near-median.

Top-line and operating margin both came in above the ~$650–700M/6.7–7.1% operating-income consensus framing, and NIMAL improved to 21% with NPL near historical lows—incremental reassurance versus the note’s margin/credit bear triggers. Despite ongoing investment, the reported quality of earnings (better credit economics, improved NIMAL, strong Brazil unit metrics) should support a modestly positive post-print move rather than another negative surprise.

Headline results beat the company’s own guidance (record revenue, strong non-GAAP EPS) but the release also flags sustained product margin headwinds and higher opex/litigation that pressured GAAP. With no pre-release consensus note, directionally the upside is partially offset by underlying profitability pressure and modestly cautious Q3 positioning (nonproduct revenue not scaling linearly).

MSI delivered a sizable EPS and revenue beat with operating margin expansion, then raised FY26 guidance (revenue and EPS) above the already-high pre-release expectations. The only meaningful offset was a small sequential backlog decline, but demand/backlog and margin commentary outweighed that, supporting a positive next-day move.

Q2 beat on EPS (>$0.41 vs ~$0.34 consensus) with strong margin expansion (adj. EBITDA margin to 14.7%) and a clear full-year EPS/guidance raise. However, the pre-release note already flagged that a reaffirm was the base case and that a raise may be limited by Investor Day optics, so the reaction is constructive but not maximally positive.

No pre-release consensus/positioning note was provided, so surprises rely on qualitative call commentary. The company delivered strong underlying margin expansion and raised FY guidance, but also guided Q4 EBITDA down due to timing/tax/hiring factors, limiting upside for the next catalyst.

Headline revenue and gross margin beat, but the key H2 regulatory catalyst (InteliQuick CT/NG) was withdrawn/delayed out of 2026—worsening the very risk the stock had been priced for. Q3 revenue guidance is essentially inline, so the delay likely dominates despite improved margins and Ebola/Colli-Pee updates.

Q2 revenue/recurring revenue and adj. EBITDA margin came in ahead of the note’s base, and FY26 guidance was raised (revenue and EBITDA) with a structurally higher margin outlook—key mismatches vs a setup that expected mostly reaffirmation at elevated expectations. Absence of one-offs further supports a positive repricing despite already-strong price action into the print.

Q2 prints were largely inside the pre-release setup on revenue/EPS, but the call delivered clearer-than-expected credit improvement (NCO 12% vs guidance, delinquency 4.0%) plus a meaningful improvement to profitability via much lower interest expense and cost discipline. Guidance: raised FY adjusted EBITDA midpoint (+6% at midpoint) while maintaining adj. EPS and revising FY NCO to 11.7%, which is supportive to the H2 math. Given the stock was up and expectations were centered on “on track,” the upside reaction looks more likely to be modest-to-positive than a blowout.

Q4 delivered upside on both revenue and adjusted EPS versus the note’s base consensus, with broad-based margin expansion and a particularly strong digital/REA and Dow Jones subscription net-add profile. However, the pre-release setup already highlighted ongoing profitability growth and a likely base-case beat-and-hold; without disclosed forward guide changes, the reaction is positive but not a runaway beat.

Headline revenue and EPS beat were largely anticipated as Flyover deal timing was expected to lift results, but guidance was raised. However, margin declined ~90 bps and the beat is partially tied to acquisition/weather dynamics (and headline includes deal-timing noise), leading to a muted, slightly positive reaction rather than a strong upside. One-time insurance is excluded from adjusted EBITDA.

Results beat the guidance midpoint (revenue and adjusted EBITDA well above) with expanding transaction margin and sharply improved FCF. The main offset is noted softening in June high-value sender growth tied to FX/RBI measures, and no consensus/estimate baseline is provided for the full guidance/quarter.

Headline profitability (combined ratio improved to 92.1%) is roughly in the note’s base/bull framework, but growth disappoints: revenue is flat-ish and gross written premium declined again, while PIF is guided to ~flat full-year—below the note’s base case of mild improvement. Offsetting items (impairment) also weigh on investment income, and management flagged the 26% expense ratio as unsustainable, limiting confidence in margin durability. Net: negative setup versus what investors were hoping for from continued growth and better underwriting quality.

Revenue came in far below the key “TVA/PPA progress” proxy (reported ~$0.1M vs consensus range that included a ~PPA/TVA scenario), while guidance/catalyst timing stayed broadly in the “discussions/late this year” mode rather than delivering definitization. However, the market narrative already discounts P&L and options implied an ~11% move, limiting downside reaction to modestly negative.

Revenue and gross margin came in clearly stronger than the note’s low-consensus range, but the key risk highlighted in the note (cash runway/capital raise timing) didn’t get resolved—cash is below what would be implied by the prior framing and adjusted EBITDA loss worsened year-over-year. With the e-commerce strength largely pre-announced (so not much incremental upside), the reaction is modestly positive rather than a rerating.

Q2 beat consensus and, more importantly, the Q3 combined revenue guide ($285–$295M) clears the note’s base and lands well above the $250–265M expectation. Gross margin expansion to 67.1% and TPD tracking (~$85M in Q3) support the deal thesis, making the guidance raise meaningfully better than what the market modeled.

No pre-release expectations were provided, but the call highlighted severe EBITDA deterioration (83% YoY, down sequentially) tied to Google monetization disruptions and a restructuring that left limited cash. Guidance is withheld amid volatility, which typically pressures the stock despite some early session recovery signals.

Q2 revenue was a clear beat versus the $52.5M expectation and margins improved (GAAP gross margin +6 pts; non-GAAP +8 pts sequential). More importantly, FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $230–$260M (excluding LivePerson), which addresses the note’s main H2-hockey-stick credibility concern; strong win-rate/customer commitment commentary supports demand quality. No meaningful underlying offset flagged vs the pre-release bear framing.

Underlying profitability improved with EBITDA more than doubling and expanding margins, but GAAP results include a sizable noncash unrealized gain and guidance implies roughly flat EBITDA margins with only modest acceleration in revenue. Backlog slipping due to delayed 400 back-of-store contract timing tempers the longer-duration growth narrative.

Reported revenue and (adj.) EPS beat the pre-release setup, and—more importantly—management raised FY2026 adjusted EPS to $5.15-$5.45 (above the $4.90-$5.30 prior range and above the note’s base/bull expectations). Civil/building/specialty margins and near-record backlog (with ~1x book-to-burn) improved the core operating story despite backdrop of tough prior-year comps.

Q2 came in ahead of both guidance/Street on revenue and EPS, and—critically—Q3 revenue ($200–220M) clears the pre-release “H2 hockey stick” risk while gross margin guides higher (41–42%). Full-year revenue was raised (to $780–810M) with EPS cut reflecting investment spend, but the underlying demand/order momentum supports the guide.

Quarterly revenue/EBITDA margin and the FY revenue/FCF raise are positives, but Q3 guidance implies very low (near-flat) growth with margins flat and management flagged further automation-driven headwinds plus ongoing top-client reductions. Underlying profitability is under pressure given cost-of-service step-up and declining Trust & Safety.

Underlying credit/earnings power came in stronger than the pre-release bar: NPLs fell to 9.6% and resolutions cleared at ~102.7% of par alongside higher-than-guide NIM (3.66%). The main near-term headwind was Q2 production of $672.6M missing the ~$680M bear threshold implied by the note’s volume risk, but management reiterated 2H acceleration with positive submission trends and no formal guidance cut.

Even with Q2 beat versus internal expectations, the company cut full-year guidance and guided to contracting commercial segment margins (low-60% range) and service profit pressure (Gov’t Solutions NYC pricing changes). Renewals with Avis/Hertz were executed at materially less favorable pricing terms with volume-modulation options, implying demand/price headwinds beyond the quarter—likely a negative market reaction.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so the score relies on qualitative read-through: revenue and behavioral subscribers declined materially YoY while guidance was reaffirmed. The key positives were the clinical subscriber/revenue strength and improved EBITDA margin vs the prior quarter, but the large behavioral decline and reaffirmed (not raised) outlook likely limit upside.

No pre-release consensus was provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. The release shows strong user/ARPU trajectory signals and advertising growth, but also highlights negative gross margin in advertising, ARPU pressure from footprint outpacing revenue, and notable weakness in Pay TV and Consumer Electronics; capex guidance is raised, which can weigh on near-term sentiment.

The quarter beat expectations on both revenue and cash EPS, and management raised full-year revenue and cash EPS guidance. However, the revenue beat was partly driven by favorable macro, and margin guidance for the back half is slightly below prior year levels, which tempers the upside reaction.

Without a pre-release note or consensus, the clearest deliverable is operating improvement: adjusted EBITDA margin expanded to 12% and Q3 guidance implies higher margins (13%). The demand backdrop is described as subdued, with revenue growth driven by paid employers while revenue per paid employer is slightly down, leading to a moderately positive but not euphoric reaction.

No consensus/research-note benchmarks are provided, but management delivered strong profitability (record adjusted operating margin) and raised FY26 and Q3 expectations with an expanding margin profile. Reaction likely positive though the guide/demand narrative includes some normalization in Cash App actives growth and lending growth, limiting upside.

Headline results beat the high end of guidance, and full-year FX-neutral GMV and non-GAAP operating income/EPS growth were raised. However, Q3 guide implies deceleration (10%-12% total; 7%-9% organic) and Depop is a near-term headwind, muting the upside despite the raised full-year outlook.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, but the company raised full-year revenue guidance meaningfully (midpoint growth implied to ~14% vs ~6% previously) alongside improved gross margin and a sharp reduction in free cash outflow—supportive for next-day sentiment. However, gross margin guidance remains mid-to-upper 30s and FCF/earnings still negative, limiting upside conviction.

No pre-release note/consensus was provided, so surprise metrics vs expectations are unknown. The print shows an improving legacy profile at Ting (first positive adjusted EBITDA, improving cash flow) but comes alongside domain subscriber declines and weaker Wavelo profitability plus a wider GAAP loss—likely a mixed, near-median reaction.
