EPS (adjusted operating) came in above the pre-release range (1.26 reported vs $1.19–$1.21 expected) but the bigger item—capital return guidance—was a raise that is only partially “new” given the note’s focus on buyback-driven EPS and ACT’s topping range. Underlying credit is still favorable (14% loss ratio aided by a smaller reserve release), but management also reiterated/expanded the message that delinquencies will rise in 2H from seasonality and newer, higher-risk vintages—limiting upside versus a priced-for-perfection setup.

Q2 headline numbers beat consensus (revenue and EPS), but the real swing item was guidance framing: energy storage volumes are cut (flat to down 4% vs prior), and mgmt guided sequential decline in Q3 with higher-cost spodumene flowing through. While specialties outlook was raised (bromine), the broader lithium/energy-storage deceleration is likely what the market trades.

P&L contained a small EPS/worse burn versus the note, mainly from higher SG&A including a one-time legal charge. However, the key catalyst sentence held (topline in late Aug/early Sep) and cash runway into 2028 remained intact, tempering downside versus the note’s bear case primarily tied to any Q3 timing slip.

Q3 beat on EPS and revenue and the FY26 guide midpoint was raised (incrementally positive). Offsetting that, adjusted operating margin fell and management flagged FY27 as only low single-digit revenue growth with modest EPS leverage plus Alaris becoming a defined 200bp headwind; Q4 growth also decelerates to ~2.5%. With the stock seemingly positioned for a Q4-bridge/guidance event (per the note) and options pricing downside skew, the net reaction is modestly positive/near-median.

EPS beat is reinforced by a genuine volume inflection (reported organic +4.3% vs guidance-consensus concern about FX-aided growth) and record margin expansion (18.3%). More importantly, full-year adjusted EPS and EBITDA and FCF were raised versus a note where the H2 bar was low but organic/second-half credibility was the key risk—overall this shifts outcomes toward the bull case.

Q4 and FY26 showed solid operating performance (FCF 735m; EBITDA margin 12.3%) with improving leverage trajectory. Initial FY27 guidance implies revenue roughly in line with the note but upgrades FCF materially (≥900m vs prior $725m base) aided by ARKA-related credits/refunds; EPS/earnings power therefore supports a mildly positive reaction rather than a full beat-and-raise blowout given the note already anticipated a conservative FY27 start and ARKA interest drag.

Q2 revenue was in-line with the guide, but non-GAAP operating income/margin materially beat the high end and NRR improved. Offsettingly, full-year 2026 revenue and non-GAAP operating income were cut meaningfully at the midpoint, implying a weaker H2 monetization profile—so the dominant post-print catalyst is negative despite the strong underlying profitability print.

Revenue came in around the pre-release bear/base band (management’s Q2 print is not meaningfully worse than the ~$851–865M whisper). However, CELSIUS brand declined ~12% YoY and management explicitly guided the flagship to remain flat sequentially in Q3 before growth in 2027—consistent with the market’s thesis-resolving concern. Alani outperformance (21% net sales growth; 56% retail growth) is a genuine positive versus the note’s base expectations, but margin guidance stayed high-40s with EBITDA down YoY, muting any upside.

Underlying beats were broadly expected (stabilization narrative, AFFO ~0.30–0.33 band), but the quarter delivered stronger physical/economic occupancy inflection and guidance was raised (midpoint $1.29 vs $1.25 in the note) alongside EQT JV regulatory approval on schedule—supportive for sentiment. However, same-store revenue guidance was reduced materially vs the pre-release model due to the JV accounting mechanics, and there was still a large non-cash impairment, keeping the reaction from being more than mildly positive.

Datadog beat on Q2 revenue and EPS and raised FY26 revenue above the pre-release ~$4.42B bar, but Q3 guidance explicitly shows deceleration (28–29% YoY) and gross margin fell to 79.6%, keeping the stock from getting a strongly positive repricing at a crowded, high-expectations setup.

Q2 net product revenue (~$199.9M) and adjusted EPS ($1.92) beat the pre-print ~$200M/$1.70 expectation, with strong Journet demand. However, the most important guidance line (full-year total revenue) was cut/derailed via a Nuscenta franchise decline (down to $825–855M) despite raising Astaris revenue ($65–75M), and the updated EBITDA guide implies essentially flat performance—offsetting the beat and tempering the upside reaction.

Revenue decline was largely mechanical and guidance was reaffirmed. The underlying driver—adjusted EBITDA of $28.8M (+43% YoY) with margin expanding 340 bps and U.S. sales/door up ~33% to ~$697—beat the note’s base/bear framing, while net leverage improved to 5.4x and capex/FCF strengthened. No material negative guidance signal to offset the operating beat.

Q2 showed strong topline and positive core organic growth (2.5%) plus higher full-year core sales/EBITDA guidance. EPS beat is modest and partially offset by disclosed financing drag/equity headwinds, while Middle East remains a clear downside pocket—though management frames it as potentially recoverable with rebuilds. Overall outcome is modestly better than what the note’s base/bear risk framework implied, supporting a moderately positive tape reaction.

Q2 top-line/EPS beat and AI revenue was strong, but the guidance package deteriorated: FY26 revenue growth was cut (and the organic profile stays weak), Q3 implies essentially flat sequential revenue, Americas growth nearly stalled, and cash-flow/FCF conversion guidance was reduced with rising DSO plus large AI-led deals pushed into 1H’27 (unsigned). For a stock already priced for perfection after the AI narrative, the guide/demand/cash-flow disappointments dominate the headline beat.

Core operating metrics came in better than the pre-print’s “watch the EBITDA and FERC language” risk framing (record rail revenue/EBITDA and record ex-Longridge EBITDA), with no clear evidence of demand deterioration. However, the release doesn’t confirm the dominant FERC catalyst or a shift in the key near-term “balance-sheet fix” timeline, so upside is likely contained and below a full beat-and-raise outcome for the equity narrative.

On the underlying metrics, the quarter shows same-park attendance +4% and adj. EBITDA +7% with ~120 bps margin expansion—consistent with the note’s base case, but the tone is stronger (pass mix yielding higher average prices; wildfire disruptions contained). Guidance risk was the July air-quality setup; management still expects YoY adj. EBITDA growth in both Q3 and Q4 with Q4 weighted—better than the market’s fear of near-term deceleration. Headline EPS/reported revenue comparison vs consensus is not fully computable from the provided facts.

Pre-release note framed this as a timing/runway quarter with no meaningful revenue and with the key risk around H2 2026 RA/CLE topline language. The call instead delivered value-driving clinical/commercial timing updates (dermatomyositis launch timeline and multiple H2’26 readouts), plus large settlement cash—supportive versus the note’s cautious “boilerplate” base case, but the note’s specific financial/EPS beats were not the focus and guidance/timing for IMVT’s core RA/CLE toplines was not clearly contradicted.

Revenue and (importantly) adjusted EBITDA margin came in better than the pre-print setup, and FY guidance/Pharma Direct growth were raised. However, the pre-release note emphasized MACs/prescription deceleration risk; reported MACs fell 12% Y/Y to 5.0M (below the 5.1–5.3M stabilization debate), and prescription revenue is down materially, creating offsetting skepticism despite the subscription/Pharma Direct offset narrative.

Headline EPS and revenue beat consensus largely on JDE Peet's consolidation and timing/tariff refund offset, but the key underlying pressure remained in U.S. Coffee (operating income down 24.7% on inflation/tariffs) while FY guidance was only reaffirmed (no meaningful raise). With the market already set up for an optical unmodelable quarter, the print looks more ‘better-than-feared vs bear’ than a clean upside re-rating; reaction expected near median.

While Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat and FY revenue/EBITDA guidance was raised, the pre-release note flagged that Q2 revenue was likely a 'phantom miss' vs management’s own run-rate, and the call highlighted margin pressure (MER 95% vs 93% with higher-than-Q1) plus limited visible Q3 expansion driven by delayed recognition (Q2-to-Q3 increase cut to $4–$7M). The raised guide is partially offset by a weaker quality-of-earnings narrative and a more cautious 2027 tone (Medicaid headwind, Tech & Services likely flat/down), implying a modest/negative market reaction versus a crowded, short-heavy setup.

Q3 beat on revenue/EPS with very strong demand commentary (China utilization >95%, longer inbound POs) and Advanced Solutions strength. More importantly, Q4 revenue and EPS guidance were raised well above the pre-release implied bar (~$328M rev / ~$1.13 EPS), which should drive a positive reaction despite the already-high expectations around the guide.

The release clearly beats the setup’s key tape tests: BRINSUPRI Q2 revenue is stronger than the $285M/whisper $290–300M bar, new patients and prescribers corroborate organic demand/persistency, and FY26 BRINSUPRI guidance is raised to $1.25–1.4B (vs the note’s de-facto requirement of ≥$1.10B). With no offsetting negative operating cost or margin deterioration mentioned, the expected next-day move is strongly positive.

Q1 and FY27 guidance both beat the pre-release setup (revenue +6% vs +2% expectation; EPS $1.14 vs ~$1.07–$1.09), and Plasma/Vascular Closure trends confirm the bull case. However, underlying margins and operating income were down YoY (GM -40 bps, adj. op margin -70 bps), tempering the enthusiasm despite raised guidance.

The headline EPS print missed expectations materially, and the quarter also included a very large non-cash goodwill impairment plus credit-loss allowance and continued adverse commercial auto reserve development—confirming the bear-case quality concerns rather than the preview’s base (earn-in improving CA ratios). Revenue appears roughly in-line, but the underlying tone remains weak with profitability still dependent on additional California rate actions.

Revenue came in ahead of the note’s base/bull expectations, but the key bear-case metric (patient starts) disappointed versus the note’s base range (160 vs ~205–220) and management explicitly highlighted the depletion-driven decline in total starts. With no FY26 guidance, the net reaction is roughly neutral to mildly positive.

The note’s bear risks (BLA timing/cash/runway and safety) were not triggered—in fact management reaffirmed FDA acceptance by year-end and provided favorable lonvo-z safety/efficacy plus continued nex-z dosing progress and MAGNITUDE enrollment. With the stock already at an inflection from de-risking and high binary optionality, the reaction is likely positive but not euphoric.

Reported Q2 upside (revenue growth, materially better MLR, and record profitability) matched the note’s “guidance is the story” framing, but OSCR delivered an actual FY26 EFO raise plus improved FY MLR/SG&A. While favorable prior-period development (and a potentially uncredited Wakely tailwind) still complicate the underlying read-through, the raised guidance and improved cost ratio more than offset the disclosed higher back-half churn timing.

Headline results beat consensus (revenue and EPS) and FY EPS growth guidance was raised to ~6% (vs prior ~4%), but the market’s key focus—system-wide same-club sales and sequential member momentum—remains largely consistent with the note’s base/bear arithmetic. The margin contraction and the continued pause in Black Card pricing limit upside despite a guide raise.

Revenue and margin dynamics largely matched the note’s framing of soft Q2 and H2-weighted conversion. Bookings/RPO were much stronger than the note’s underlying “watchful” risk (mostly due to the announced FAU-like system sale), but the widened adj. EBITDA loss and continued opex pressure offset, resulting in a roughly median reaction.

Headline Q2 metrics beat the company’s high-end EBITDA guide and underlying profitability improved (spot mix up; gross profit per load strength). However, Q3 guidance embeds a sequential decline in gross profit per load and Last Mile faces a $3–5m headwind plus free cash flow remains pressured by working capital and QuickPay usage, limiting upside.

Revenue/backlog and FY revenue guidance largely matched the pre-announced setup (no real surprise). The reaction is driven by underlying margin/burn: gross margin (~29%) stayed below the note’s mid/high range and operating cash burn ($11.1M) again ran above the guided $8–9M average, despite reiterating cash/burn optics; new contracts are supportive but don’t immediately fix H2 ramp/cash burn risk. With the stock likely already priced for the known revenue beat, the incremental disappointments skew negative for next-day reaction.

Revenue and adjusted EBITDA materially beat the pre-set base case, with MirrorEye setting a new sales record and net debt falling faster than feared. However, adjusted gross margin declined YoY (currency/material and factory-built transition costs), and guidance was only reaffirmed (no upside), tempering the upside versus a guidance-raise scenario.

The quarter itself is mainly a cash/milestone accounting outcome already framed in the setup note. The key actionable updates (RGX-202 confirmatory timelines ahead of schedule, BLA module submission in Q3 2026, runway into Q4 2027/into H2 2027) are consistent with the note’s base/bull possibilities, not a clear step-change above that expectation; upside is modest given pre-announced milestone mechanics.

Q2 revenue is roughly in line, but North America comps (-8.3%) undershoot the already-weak expectations and, more importantly, the company suspended the dividend and cut 2026 adjusted EBITDA to $180-$190M (below the $200-$210M floor), with NA comps guidance worsening to -6% to -8%. International growth is a bright spot, but the guidance + capital allocation reset points to a negative repricing.

Q2 operationals beat (EBITDA $37.4M, margin +310bps; practice collections +12.4% with 19.2% attributed-life growth) and management raised multiple FY26 guide lines with attributed lives now above the prior high end—consistent with the base-to-bull framework. The main swing factor is guidance: while the note expected EBITDA guide action to drive tape, the call suggests practice collections deceleration to ~3% YoY in 2H (conservative framing), tempering upside and keeping reaction around mildly positive rather than bullish.

The print largely confirms what the note framed as the key swing factor: Catalent Indiana classification is still pending and Sept 30 PDUFA timing remains intact, which supports the base case. Offsetting is a tangible positive—more commercially-ready vials from the second facility—while the lack of Catalent resolution vs the typical 90-day window is a clear negative relative to the bull-case expectation of near-term clarity.

Headline EPS matched the consensus high end, but revenue came in meaningfully below $1.89B expectations and Q2 Mattress Firm margins declined. More importantly, FY26 adj. EPS guide was lowered to $2.85–$3.15 with an industry down mid-single-digit framing—worse than the note’s expectation of a reaffirm/upper-half outcome—driving a downside-biased reaction despite improved North America margins and cash flow.

Headline Q2 revenue/EPS beat, but the key is guidance: FY2026 pro forma constant-currency revenue growth was cut to 3.5–4.5% (from 4.5–5.5%) and Interventional integration is delayed. Margin also contracted (gross margin -280 bps), offsetting the EPS raise (driven by buybacks/lower interest/tax). Net is a growth/guidance disappointment for a stock that was priced around a steep H2 EPS ramp.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA landed slightly better than the pre-release model, helped by stronger Ignite/digital and a record Interactive margin. However, the Interactive segment still shows year-over-year revenue decline and management’s guidance posture is effectively neutral (no change indicated vs the reaffirmed FY framework), while FCC impairment drove large headline losses—so the market reaction is expected to be modestly positive rather than a rerating.

Revenue and adjusted profitability improved versus expectations, but the key setup in the note was about H2 revenue durability. Management guided Q3 revenue to $12–14M (a sequential decline) and positioned capacity/delivery wave mostly in Q4, undercutting the sequential-growth expectation embedded in the preview. With the stock already heavily run up into the print and valuation-sensitive positioning, the guidance deceleration dominates the operational beat.

ARR growth hit 12% cc (a modest positive vs the 11.5% “streak” bar), and FCF trend remains healthy (FCF ~$498M TTM). However, revenue beat appears largely consistent with FX tailwinds, the company reaffirmed FY FCF/outlook without raising the cc momentum ranges, and margins are still explained as investments/front-loaded costs—so there’s no clear re-acceleration signal strong enough for a large re-rating.

Revenue landed at the low end of guidance (not a beat vs the pre-release setup) while Q2 profitability benefited from a large tariff-refund item, and active customer growth remains weak (~4.1%) with soft traffic into June. FY guidance was reaffirmed and Q3 calls for heavy pre-launch investment, but the underlying demand/margin setup keeps reaction more negative than neutral.

The release improved streaming profitability (higher streaming adjusted EBITDA/margin; accelerating ex-FX growth), but linear advertising declined nearly 30% with continued international weakness, and management did not change transaction expectations (declined deal questions). Given the pre-release note framed this as largely an arb/CMA headline into 7 Aug and the guidance/action risk was already central, the fundamentals surprises likely produced only a modest, near-median reaction rather than a clear re-rate.

Q2 headline revenue and EPS beat expectations, and full-year revenue guidance was raised to mid-single-digit YoY growth (above the prior flat premise). However, gross margin missed the ~43% outlook (42.7%) and the Q3 guide implies EPS ~1.11 with GM ~43%, leaving less room for multiple expansion versus the note’s focus on a stronger H2 ramp.

Headline revenue and EBITDA came in better than the Q2 setup in the note, and margins expanded. However, Payment Software decelerated (9% / 7% cc vs the note’s double-digit Q2 guide ask) and Q3 guide implies a softer revenue/EBITDA cadence, which for a stock priced off Biller optionality is more important than the beat-and-raise. Biller sale confirmation remained absent (no-comment).

Despite the stock being priced for a modest beat, the release delivered a meaningful beat in both revenue ($435M vs ~$386M consensus anchor) and adjusted EPS ($2.21 vs ~$1.80), alongside a clear positive swing in long-term net inflows and an upward long-term EBITDA margin guidance (49% to 50%). While management did guide fee rate to a normalized 46–47 bps range, the combination of record inflows, synergy already fully realized, and margin expansion supports a moderately positive reaction rather than perfection.

Results were better than the already-strong preprint expectations, led by cloud subscription acceleration and a materially higher Q2 adj. EBITDA. The key driver (cloud subscription revenue guidance) was raised further, while Q3 total revenue guide stayed broadly consistent. Despite the beat, the stock was already priced for perfection and the NRR was only flat vs the prior quarter (115%), limiting upside to a modest positive reaction.

Headline Q2 revenue beat and written comps surged, but the EPS/EBITDA picture is pressured. Guidance was raised on net income/EBITDA while revenue was held, and—critically—underlying margins contracted (even excluding the tariff refund), with Q3 comps/delivered guidance not clearly better than the market’s “high-end/bridge” expectations. With the IEEPA refund known as a catalyst to watch in the note, upside is partially priced in, keeping reaction near-median.

Q2 revenue was well above the $40–42M bottom-third-of-guide expectation (49.8M reported), and management guided Q3 back to positive adjusted EBITDA (7–15M) with strong EI/Thermal Barrier recovery signals. Offsetting negatives are very low reported Q2 gross margin (7%) and continued incident charges through Q3—however, management frames much of this as recoverable via insurance, keeping the overall surprise net-positive.

Q2 topped the already-highly-stale revenue consensus and showed a clear adjusted EBITDA inflection, while demand commentary/backlog quality improved (international subscriptions +80%+ of funded backlog). However, FY revenue and adjusted EBITDA guidance were reaffirmed rather than raised, which limits upside versus the note’s “credibility checkpoint” and keeps reaction near median.

ATI delivered a major upside to the Street: Q2 EBITDA/margins beat the top end of prior guidance, and full-year guidance was raised materially (EBITDA midpoint +35%, EPS midpoint to $5.04, FCF midpoint +51% vs prior consensus). Record backlog and strength across AA&S and defense (naval nuclear contract extension) further reduce downside, with no evident underlying margin deterioration.

BRLT delivered upside to already-high expectations on revenue and especially adjusted EBITDA, with gross margin up ~360 bps sequentially and cost leverage. More importantly, full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance was raised to $13–$15M versus a ~$9–$11M expectation, indicating the feared H2 shortfall did not materialize. No offsetting demand/order deterioration was flagged (orders only slightly down; ex-sub-$500 and two-year stacked growth positive).

Revenue was essentially in line and full-year guidance was reaffirmed, which fits the base case. However, adjusted EBITDA declined to $5.9M and the quarter highlighted additional pressure (AI R&D expensing) plus a liquidity/financing change (new $60M ATM), which is worse than what the note framed as the main watch items for de-risking the H2 ramp.

Quarter revenue and EBITDA cleared expectations, and cash improved, but the Q3 guide implies a sharp EBITDA step-down ($1–$2M) despite the pre-release focus on sustaining an EBITDA floor. The market was already braced for transition risk; the beat likely offers limited upside, while the weaker sequential profit outlook offsets it.

Revenue fell further short of the note’s ~$239.7M expectation and off-net/declining consolidated trend persisted, offset by a clearly supportive wavelength/connection beat and a higher adjusted EBITDA margin. Guidance specifics weren’t provided in the call facts versus the note, and the reported leverage improvement and big data-center gain are largely financial/one-off/credit-supportive rather than a clean re-rating trigger; net reaction looks modestly positive-to-neutral.

Headline results were strong (record revenue, materially higher adj. EBITDA margin, EPS $0.45 vs $0.42) and full-year guidance was raised to levels implying continued momentum. The key market overhang in the note was the Q3 optical/memory headwind and positioning near the 52-week high; management reiterated a contained Q3 gross-margin headwind (~75 bps) and provided improved 2H visibility, which argues the upside dominates but with less-than-maximum enthusiasm.

While EBITDA guidance was raised and narrowed, the new full-year midpoint ($502.5M) is slightly below the note’s bull/base expectation of ~$480–510M with skepticism around momentum/cushion; operationally, Iraq timing is confirmed earlier (early Q2 2027), which is a positive versus the note’s bear risk. Offset by indication of contracted business strength and increased FSRU conversion capex, which tempers the quality of the raise.

Revenue and Take 5 comps slightly exceeded what the note framed as a low bar (+3% mid-range), but adjusted EBITDA/margins were pressured (restatement costs at the top end of the annual range and Take 5 margin down ~70 bps). FY guidance was reiterated with results expected near the low end, so the upside is limited versus the market’s already-subdued setup.

Q2 revenue matched the ~$582M working consensus and EPS of $0.90 beat the $0.82–$0.84 consensus range, helped by tariff refund benefit. However, management reaffirmed full-year guidance (no raise) and reiterated seasonally softer Q3 with international/mid-east headwinds, limiting upside given the stock’s recent run-up. Overall, this reads as a modest beat with guidance not changing the valuation narrative.

Q2 revenue of $29.1M beat the pre-print ~$26.6M expectation, and FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $104–108M vs an “at least $100M” baseline. However, adjusted EBITDA fell to $7.6M (from $9.8M) despite higher GM, and the call reiterated below-expectation enrollment due to training challenges—tempering how strong a reaction should be.

Underlying operating momentum was stronger than the note’s base: Etsy marketplace GMS hit $2.6B (+7.5% YoY) and active buyers and app GMS accelerated, while take rate rose to 25.9% and adjusted EBITDA margin came in at 29.2% (above the guide band). Management also raised FY26 GMS to mid-single-digit and gave solid Q3 GMS guidance (above prior expectations), which should support a modest-to-positive post-print reaction despite largely “priced for meeting” setup. The main offset was the still-flat YoY active buyers (habitual/repeat growth but no clear re-acceleration in the buyer base) and workforce charges (largely non-recurring).

Q2 results materially exceeded consensus (revenue and EPS), and importantly management raised FY26 guidance across revenue/EBITDA/EPS. However, the pre-release note emphasized guidance-driven risk and that H2 growth was “derisked”; the company still guided to moderating growth in Q3/Q4, which limits upside and keeps the reaction only modestly positive versus a full beat-and-raise backdrop.

Despite record order intake and first data-center awards, Q3 revenue missed (production delays) and—critically—management cut FY26 revenue/EBITDA midpoints sharply (EBITDA to negative), undermining the margin/“Q4 catch-up” math from the pre-release note. The new information mainly increases timing/working-capital risk, which should drive a negative reaction.

Headline Q4 and full-year results beat both consensus and the note’s “real bar,” with advertising surging on World Cup and EBITDA/margins rising strongly. Management also confirmed favorable FY27 demand/digital trajectory and kept the Roku close timing/FCF framing supportive, leaving little in the way of the main bear-case risks (World Cup margin phasing and weaker FY27 framing).

Q2 showed strong operational momentum versus the preview (member growth +1% after years of flat/negative; EBITDA up 10% with margin expansion to 34%). Full-year guidance was raised (revenue and EBITDA), but some of the quarter’s outperformance is weather/cost-development and management flagged that weather benefits will reverse in Q3, tempering conviction.

Headline growth and raised guidance are supported by tariff-refund benefits and a pulled-forward GTS launch, but underlying first-half EBITDA and gross margin (ex-tariff) were weaker and management guided to 2H net sales down low single digits with EBITDA declining vs 2H 2025—offsetting the raise and tempering the likely reaction.

Reported EPS benefited from much stronger gross margin (33.5%) and GRE profitability normalization, offset by weaker customer metrics (meters/RCEs down, new adds down) and higher SG&A for acquisition. With revenue slightly down and the pre-release note already framing margin recovery as the key swing factor, the setup looks less like a clear upside shock and more like an on-plan-to-modestly-better margin story plus ongoing book shrink risk.

While military/government demand and Galileo/5G momentum were better than the note’s base expectations, Gogo cut full-year revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA guidance (litigation/mix) and lowered the Galileo aircraft-online target to the mid-500s vs ~600 prior. The guidance reset against the FCF/deleveraging line is the dominant negative given ~FCF is the stock’s key trigger.

IOVA delivered a clear quarter beat with substantially stronger gross margin (56% vs 41% Q1) and management signaled a full-year revenue guidance raise via a Q3 update due to very strong Q3-to-date. Given the stock was coming off a sharp selloff and guidance credibility was the market’s key worry, the operational upside (margin + Amtagvi beat/ATC progress) is more than what the note expected, driving a strong positive reaction despite some remaining guidance execution risk.

No pre-release consensus was provided, but the print featured a raised full-year adjusted EPS guide (new low above prior high), record orders/revenue, and margin expansion targeting ~20.5%—a net positive setup for next-day reaction. Offsetting factors were management’s explicit moderation in second-half comparisons and delayed Middle East orders, keeping confidence moderate.

Reported Q2 revenue and adjusted EPS beat the pre-release consensus backdrop, but the dominant narrative item—FY2026 revenue guidance ($450–500M) and capex ($350–500M)—was reaffirmed (no upside squeeze). Underlying margin pressure remains (advanced tech and SWU margin compression), keeping reaction near median even with stronger topline/backlog commentary.

Despite Q2 headline revenue slightly below the modeled/consensus band, the key driver was a full-year guide raise (revenue and adjusted EBITDA) alongside firmer LINZESS demand/price dynamics and leverage de-risking (convert repaid). This directly addresses the note’s main “judgment” items (FY26 outlook, demand trajectory), though the company did not provide quantified 2027 MFP commentary, limiting upside.

Headline EPS and revenue came essentially in line with the note (EPS within the -$0.60 working range; sales broadly ~4.2B). However, underlying profitability was worse than the preview’s base/bridge check: SOI was $36M with Americas and EMEA both losses, and unit volume declined 4% vs the ~-10% drag expectation, while guidance was reaffirmed but free cash flow remains a burn. Net effect is modestly negative vs prior expectations given the limited cushion and continued cash burn despite the improved APAC mix.

Q2 headlines beat the pre-set $1.17B revenue and implied $1.24 EPS anchor, and FCF exceeded the $10M guide. However, FY2026 guidance was cut (notably GRLNF and non-GAAP EPS) versus what the note treated as a must-reaffirm/credible H2 ramp, and the Middle East headwind plus added interest burden from the new term loan weigh on the back-half. Net: mix of beat with a disappointment on the reset of forward expectations.

Q2 revenue and profitability materially beat (15.2% adj. EBITDA margin vs ~13% guide-implied), and FY26 guidance was raised to ~$1.705B midpoint revenue and ~$225M adj. EBITDA midpoint, exceeding the note’s base case need for a meaningful EBITDA lift. While Q3 EBITDA guide softens sequentially due to investments, this is framed as intentional and largely aligns with the note’s embedded EHR/drag risk rather than signaling broader deterioration.

Underlying results appear strong: record adjusted EBITDA with expanding margin (plus improved leverage). However, management flagged meaningful Q3 sales headwinds from tornado damage and a full-year inflation headwind weighted to the second half, which likely tempers any upside beyond the good Q2 print.

Headline revenue and EPS were far worse than the pre-release consensus, but the bigger issue for valuation is the regulatory timeline: Zynquista resubmission is pushed to end-October (and a 6-month review still implies Q2’27 decision), fighting the note’s bull/better-than-feared setup. Underlying operating loss also widened, and the improved SONATA enrollment timing helps only modestly versus the timeline disappointment.

Q2 revenue and EPS came in comfortably above the pre-release setup, and the company nudged full-year adjusted EPS guidance up at the low end to $9.00 while reaffirming the royalty range. However, management continues to emphasize heavy reliance on the back-half ramp and provided no royalty guidance raise, limiting the upside versus the market’s already bullish XOMA narrative.

Q2 revenue and profitability beat the note/consensus, but the bigger watch items (RIN realized price lagging index; REC/power ramp only beginning with programming changes and no EPS guidance) are unlikely to resolve the FY26 EPS risk. Full-year guidance was reaffirmed, limiting upside versus the market’s bear/base setup (which already flagged RIN-inventory depletion and EPS vulnerability).

Reported Q2 and the Q3 semiconductor/equipment momentum framing came in stronger than the pre-release note’s base case, but the Q3 gross margin guide drops to 47% from 47.6% and explicitly includes ramp headwinds (50–80 bps). Net: upside guidance/demand supports a positive move, tempered by the margin/ramp caution and the stock’s already-strong run-up/premium positioning.

Q3 revenue and adjusted EPS beat consensus, but the key is guidance: Q4 revenue of $415–425M and adj. EPS $1.97–2.03 clear the note’s ~“needs ~$375–390M” framing with stronger Data Center and I&D expectations plus continued margin expansion to 60–61% (vs ~59.5% expected). Book-to-bill records and strong bookings language reinforce the upside rather than signaling deceleration.

Headline EPS and operating/gross margin beat expectations, but the upside is partly explained by pulled-forward government orders (quality concern) and FY27 guidance was reaffirmed. Q2 guide is roughly flat (consistent with the note’s base/bear setup), limiting how much of the beat changes the forward narrative.

The quarter itself appears broadly in line with the pre-release framing (small revenue/EPS signal; cash runway addressed). The call added pipeline/timing specificity consistent with the note’s base case (initiation targeted, BLA pathway reiterated) with no clear negative runway/funding downgrade, limiting upside. Slightly higher operating expenses vs a year ago points to burn/margin pressure, tempering the reaction despite strong program readouts (Phase 2 efficacy) and trial clearance/RMAT.

Headline earnings missed heavily due to large solar impairment charges, which were not in the modeled yardstick; however, the core operating picture (adjusted EBITDA and most segment OP) was broadly in-line or better. Guidance tone turned more cautious (possible additional solar impairments/curtailments in H2) and FY operating profit/net income expected to be below 2025, offsetting the underlying margin upside.

Revenue/EPS were not meaningfully better than what the note modeled (milestone/phasing-driven quarter). The only incremental upside vs expectations was a small raise to FY26 adjusted revenue midpoint (+$5M), but management reiterated that the guide excludes Sanofi royalties/supply/milestones, limiting upside enthusiasm. Expense trajectory remains strong (continued massive opex reduction), partially offsetting the milestone uncertainty and keeping reaction near median.

Q1 revenue/EPS and FCF beat the (stale) consensus backdrop, but the key risks from the note largely remain: Clear Eyes stays supply-constrained and organic momentum is soft into Q2 (retailer timing reversal), while gross margin is down Y/Y and the full-year margin improvement is attributed mainly to acquisitions rather than an organic GM stabilization. Guidance was raised, yet the note already framed the event as acquisition-driven, limiting upside.

The key pre-release yardstick (adjusted pretax/ROE support) deteriorated: management lowered expectations and guided to the low end while operating around ~9% (below the ~$20M quarterly pretax “floor” implied by the note). While originations and refinance recapture improved, servicing adjusted pretax income fell ~60% YoY as MSR runoff jumped nearly 80%, which undermines the “transitory” setup the note was watching for.

Reported revenue and—especially—adjusted EBITDA ($206M, 28.2% margin) beat the pre-release base case, but management guided to finishing the year toward the lower end and warned H2 SuperPlay revenue declines due to deliberate front-loaded UA tied to the earnout. Added demand/DSI softness plus weaker engagement (DAU/paying users down) offset the margin upside, resulting in a roughly neutral-to-slightly-positive reaction versus the note’s expectation.

Headline regulatory messaging (no efficacy issues, no AdCom, clean BIMO/inspection) largely matches what the market was waiting for, and cash/runway into 2028 remains intact. Offsetting, Q2 burn and operating expenses rose (G&A/R&D up) and POWER1’s miss still implies more uncertainty, so the print is not likely to re-rate much at this valuation backdrop.

Q4 revenue beat vs implied guide, but FY27 guidance frames a transition year with revenue down at the midpoint. Despite strong Q4 gross margin, FY27 revenue directionality and the higher-than-feared churn (with part of it attributed to a reactivation algorithm change) keep the net setup roughly inline-to-modestly positive. Stock positioning isn’t described as a major beat-run-up from the note, so reaction likely stays near median.

Despite revenue/orders coming in stronger than the note’s base, EPS was weak and profitability deteriorated: gross margin only partially excludes impairments and Q3 guide steps down further to 16%–16.5% (below what the note viewed as the ~17% threshold). Incentive costs rose again and management withheld full-year guidance due to demand uncertainty, driving a negative setup for the stock.

Unity delivered a clear underlying Vector/strategic acceleration (near record EBITDA margins) and raised Q3 strategic revenue guidance materially above the pre-release setup’s demanding ramp expectations. The main remaining uncertainty is EPS conversion, but margins/FCF and the Q3 guide point to a strong next-day tape.

Q2 revenue and (especially) adjusted EBITDA came in below the $14–22M guide and FY outlook credibility was damaged by the decision to suspend/withdraw all guidance including full-year EBITDA. While CTV and enterprise trends showed some stabilization, the key issue is the loss of guidance and elevated bad-debt/DR-weakness signals, which are bearish versus what the note expected.

Management delivered the key narrative catalyst (first-ever positive operating EBITDA and small positive non-GAAP EPS), which is broadly consistent with the pre-release setup, but guided that 2H inflection will be more meaningful in 2027/2028 (less near-term upside than a bull case) and reported entertainment segment EBITDA down YoY on higher rooftop costs and lost sponsorship renewal. Net: modestly positive/near-median reaction rather than a clear beat-and-raise.

VAC delivered contract sales and VPG well above the high end of guidance and beat Q2 adjusted EBITDA vs the midpoint. The key swing was a full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance raise (+$50M) with higher contract sales growth guidance and a stronger implied H2 ramp, countering the market’s H2/sector-read-through concerns. Offset: sales reserves rose to 13.4% and management expects a similar rate in H2, which is a mild quality/margin risk.

Management reaffirmed FY26 guidance (already the key ask in the pre-release note) and volumes were inside the guided Q2 window, but underlying EPS/pretax margin performance deteriorated and Midwest premium inflation is tracking higher than initially expected. Overall read-through is slightly negative, but largely offset by reaffirmation within consensus and no explicit guide cut.

The quarter largely tracks the pre-release setup: Experiences/Hotels & Other are consistent with the guided direction (Experiences bookings +5%, Hotels & Other down ~21%). The notable disappointment is Q3 guidance that implies further continuing-ops revenue declines (-7% to -10%) and prudence on profitability, which tempers the optionality narrative; buyback proceeds are framed for debt/share repurchases but no new repurchase authorization or timing was provided. Net reaction expected is slightly negative-to-neutral given the market already anticipated an in-line tape with downside skew risk.

Q2 results were slightly worse on revenue and meaningfully worse on underlying profitability, but the key structural point (reaffirmed FY26 revenue $775–800M and adj. EBITDA $0–10M; Q4 ~30% gross margin run rate) was fully in line with the pre-release note. Excess breaker impact, butter exit costs, and peak supply-management were acknowledged as drivers, limiting incremental downside from guidance credibility. Net: modestly positive given reaffirmation despite bad-margin optics.

Reported Q2 delivered a step-up in the load-bearing metric: adjusted EBITDA margin rose to 19.2% vs the 18.1% floor highlighted in the note, and full-year revenue and margin guidance were raised. Underlying cash flow was positive (FCF +$19M) and leverage came in better than pro forma guidance; synergy timing shifted to 2027, which limits upside vs the note’s more optimistic bull framing but doesn’t negate the margin/guide outperformance.

EPS was effectively inline, while the key underlying swing was cash conversion and segment margin quality. Although operating margin expanded, a large portion was the IEEPA tariff refund (one-time) and Repair Solutions margin declined and triggered leadership change plus a downward segment revision. Cash/FCF was much better than Q1 (98M vs 28M), and the full-year EPS guide was raised, but Mobility Tech guidance was cut and the FY operating margin expansion outlook was trimmed—netting a modestly positive, not a beat-and-run-away.

Headline beat (revenue, EBITDA, EPS) plus a raised FY2026 guidance midpoint is a real incremental upside versus a note that already flagged a reafﬁrm-only as the main downside risk. Underlying margin improved and Greater China held up, offsetting previously flagged second-half supply/inspection headwinds. Remaining risk is the guided moderation in Greater China growth and the specified $100–$150M 2H revenue impact, but the raise should support the stock near/above prior highs.

Adjusted core EPS beat the note’s ~$0.90 expectation (reported $1.19), helped by financing volume growth and record servicing. However, reported diluted EPS was dragged by new charges tied to legacy fraud and management flagged Q3 credit charges plus a conditional guide toward the lower end of original ranges if conditions persist—blunting the upside and offsetting the beat.

Q2 revenue and margin were roughly in line with (or modestly above) what the pre-release note modeled, but the bigger takeaway was strong Recorlev demand (record starts/referrals) and >50% YoY growth in Adj. EBITDA. The company raised/tightened FY2026 revenue to $385–390M, which is effectively consistent with the note’s base/bull expectations, but the required H2 ramp is still intact; the only meaningful overhang is the large one-time GAAP charge tied to retiring converts, which doesn’t count for underlying.

Headline results beat on revenue and underwriting income, but the key ex-cat/ex-reserve profitability signal was not meaningfully better than the pre-print’s base case: P-L combined ratio and underlying improvements relied on reserve releases and expense ratio offset, while auto margins were acknowledged as below the mid-90s target and BI severity remains a watch item. With the stock already hot and positioned for a margin inflection, this reads as largely expected/low-quality upside, leading to near-median reaction rather than a sustained rerate.

Revenue and billed-hours disappointed vs the preview’s base assumptions, and Q2 adjusted EBITDA stayed negative (though losses narrowed). Offsetting factors were lower GAAP/adjusted losses and management reaffirmed FY revenue “relatively consistent” with 2025 and gross margin guidance toward ~36%.

Quarter was roughly in-line on revenue but EPS missed due to weaker profitability. The key surprise was a significant FY26 guidance cut (midpoint adj. EPS $6.20 vs $6.925 expected), alongside deteriorating U.S. Companion Animal/Deramtology demand signals (U.S. Dermatology share down sequentially and intensifying competition), which is the credibility/trajectory issue the pre-print flagged.

Q2 delivered a clear EBITDA/margin beat and management raised FY2026 sales/EBITDA while also reaffirming share buybacks through deal closing—supportive for deal-execution credibility. Offsetting this, FY EPS was cut (despite the EBITDA raise) due to higher depreciation/interest and tax mix, limiting upside versus the note’s “credibility print” expectations. Net effect is modestly positive.

Q2 revenue was essentially in line with expectations, but adjusted EBITDA margin came in ahead (29.4% vs ~28.5% expected and above the top end of the Q2 guide) and ARPD hit a new record, with Premium Plus penetration tracking toward the 15% target. Offset: management reaffirmed flat-to-+2% revenue and guided Q3 margin to 28.5–29.5% (not a clear further acceleration vs the note’s key H2 credibility question), while traffic/DI units declined and the site growth turnaround was pushed out to 2027.

Underlying volume/mortality softness was worse than expected (Q2 comp volume -3.5% vs base-case flat/low-single-digit), and management cut FY26 revenue guidance by ~$5M due to weaker H1 volume and delayed acquisitions—undercutting the H2 “hockey stick.” While EPS/margins held up (EBITDA margin +70 bps) and pre-need/insurance funded sales grew strongly, the guidance downgrade is the dominant driver.

The quarter’s headline profitability underperformed (EBITDA down and swung to an adjusted net loss) but free cash flow improved and management reaffirmed the FY adjusted EBITDA guidance midpoint with an above-consensus implication for the guide credibility versus the note’s base/bear risks. Netting those forces, the release should be viewed as closer to “not worse” than a clear beat, with modestly positive bias from the maintained guide and liquidity/FCF progress despite weaker margins and tariff/duties headwinds.

Q2 adj. EPS ($0.88) landed essentially within the dispersed consensus band and kept FY26 guidance on track at the $4.24 midpoint. The key narrative driver (data-center ESA momentum) was reinforced with explicit confidence of at least one more ESA in 2026 and upside to the pipeline, offsetting the still-planned equity issuance.

Q2 operational metrics cleared the key EBITDA/barrelline: adj. EBITDA $60M and 4.6% margin vs the note’s guidance-implied ~$54–$65M and ~25% flow-through. Management also raised FY2026 revenue to ~$5.0–$5.1B and guided Q3 EBITDA margin higher (5%–5.5%). Given the stock had run ~10% into the print, the upside is likely capped, but fundamentals support a modest positive reaction.

Adjusted EPS beat amid expanding EBITDA margin and continued core pawn strength (same-store core GP +13%). Revenue appears broadly in-line versus consensus, while scrap margin declined faster than the prior-quarter peak narrative—partly consistent with the note’s gold-normalization risk—so the reaction is modestly positive rather than strong.

Adj. EBITDA of $93.3M matched the published UBS/consensus anchor and did not beat the pre-note $95–105M whisper; carbon/net EBITDA was strong (~$59M) but 2026 45Z credits were not monetized, adding a cash-timing question. On the positive side, Q3 crush margins were guided to stay only slightly below Q2 historically high levels, supporting underlying earnings stability.

Underlying profitability and the combined ratio materially beat the note’s base case, with the ceded-premium ratio decline to ~41%-42% supporting the reinsurance savings story. However, the guidance-like items provided (Florida rate reductions 3%-5%, ceded ratio trajectory, and continued GPW decline/flat-to-down premiums in force) temper enthusiasm versus a “growth inflection” ask, and EPS appears driven by favorable prior period reserve development rather than only ongoing underwriting.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA topped expectations (and margin expanded vs. a setup that feared the margin/growth narrative would break). The key offset is APAC declined and underlying organic growth was only mid-single digits, but Q3 revenue/EBITDA guidance (midpoint) supports continued growth and suggests the market doesn’t fully get a “streak ended” outcome.

Q2 results largely match the pre-announced de-risked quarter (EBITDA and DPU in/near the guided range) with notable upside from higher RPD and margin expansion. However, FY26 liquidity/pro-forma appears slightly weaker vs the note’s stronger liquidity expectations after financing, and the key overhang is still the margin/demand durability given the heavy vehicle-recall headwind; net reaction is modestly positive rather than a strong beat-and-raise.

Reported adj. EPS of $0.65 misses the note’s $0.78 expectation, driven by alts returns collapsing to 5.9% (below the feared 8% bear-band and well under the rebaseline risk the note flagged). Guidance/near-term alts returns (Q3 ~7–8%) still implies continued underperformance of the long-term 12–14% target; despite record AUM and solid core retail sales, the earnings power narrative deteriorates, which should pressure the stock.

Q2 revenue came in above the pre-release expectation and adj. EBITDA margin cleared and exceeded the ≥2.5% gate (3% vs ~2.6% expected), while management also raised full-year expectations—supporting the 2H inflection narrative. Offsetting the beat, underlying revenue still declined ~3% y/y (vs the note’s target ≤-2.3%), and EPS was high relative to consensus largely despite underlying pressures (more uncertainty on sustainability).

Underlying profitability delivered a clear EBITDA beat versus the $230–240M guide framework used in the note (Q2 $281M) and, importantly, raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA by $70M (+7%)—both better than the note’s base/bull expectations without any sign of a decelerating 2H EBITDA ramp (Q3/Q4 guided at the high end of what the note modeled). The main offset is capex being raised materially and volumes still flat year-over-year due to curtailments falling mostly into 2H (not fully realized upside in the quarter).

Q2 revenue matched the pre-release consensus and the quarter showed broadly supportive unit economics (service GM up to 36% and LEO now 55% of airtime revenue) plus a stronger-than-whisper vessel outcome (ending ~10,700, above the ~10,600 bull threshold). However, terminals were below Q1 and FY26 guidance was not meaningfully updated versus the already-high consensus underwriting, limiting upside.

Adjusted EPS $2.43 beat the $2.30–$2.36 consensus range, and ROE hit 17% while MetLife added a large $3B authorization—both broadly supportive. However, the key earnings-quality swing was weaker RIS/private-equity performance: total spread fell to 97 bps (below the 100–120 bps guidance range) and variable investment income was below run-rate, which partially offsets the headline beat given the stock is already near all-time highs.

Revenue was roughly in-line, but EPS missed meaningfully (non-GAAP $0.08 vs ~$0.12–0.13 expected) alongside deteriorating underlying profitability signals (GAAP loss, non-GAAP income down). Demand narrative was mixed-to-improving (stronger bookings/TCV and Data & AI sequential growth), but the Talent business weakness and SG&A step-up risk kept the bar for a positive reaction from being cleared.

Quarterly revenue and adjusted EPS/EBITDA margin were roughly in line with the pre-release setup, but guidance shifted negatively: full-year diluted EPS midpoint cut (midpoint to $8.05 vs ~$8.40 consensus) and free-cash-flow guidance lowered (and FY27 incentive economics explicitly capped via the VA MDE incentive pause). Elevated DSO (98 days) and higher net leverage further tilt toward a weak/negative near-term reaction despite efficiency margin gains.

Headline quarter looks solid (prod above midpoint, liquidity intact), but the release meaningfully raises 2026 and potentially 2027 capex with exploration-driven risk: Bubale adds ~$190m (incremental spend) and Hai Su Vang-4X is a dry hole with results trending to the lower end of Vietnam. With the stock already positioned around an oil-price-driven beat being 'mostly noise', the bigger capex/earlier FCF risk dominates despite continued first-oil timing.

Q2 revenue and underlying profitability beat expectations, with EBITDA margins expanding to 13.9%. The key driver was the guidance update plus a completed $124M refinancing, which reduces balance-sheet overhang; notably, the FY sales guide was raised but still sits near the pre-announced range, limiting upside versus what was already priced.

Q2 retail performance beat the note’s base case (record revenue, 34.4% margin, EBITDAR $517M) and retail FY guidance was raised. However, Interactive guidance revenue was lowered (to $1.57B), partially offsetting the otherwise small-loss/in-line Interactive quarter; with the stock already up ~33% and options implying a modest ~8-10% move, the net is neutral-to-slightly positive rather than a rerating blowout.

Revenue and underlying profitability beat helped by tariff refunds (optically positive). Management also raised FY revenue and FCF guidance and incorporated TRISM into growth expectations (Integrated PayTech to ~20%), which is better than the pre-note’s base case of an unchanged/stale FY guide. Offset: while EBITDA guidance is held at low-to-mid single-digit growth, prepaid remains choppy and much of the Q2 margin upside is timing/one-off (tariff refunds), limiting confidence in persistence.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, but the company delivered record revenue/EPS growth plus a full-year net sales, adjusted EPS, and EBITDA margin guidance raise, alongside improving gross margin and strong Engineered Products backlog/bookings. Offsetting negatives include a strategic review overhang (Southwest Steel Processing expected to be loss-making) and mixed segment profitability (Supply Tech margin roughly flat; Assembly Components operating income declined).

Q2 results and—most importantly—FY26 adj. EPS guidance were raised materially (to $12.20–$12.70 vs ~$11.50 base in the note), with cloud/core services gross profit growth supporting margin durability despite a hardware gross margin decline. Fourth-quarter EPS growth was guided to slow (expected) but the raised guide offset the risk, supporting a positive though not euphoric reaction given the stock’s already strong run-up/priced-for-raise setup.

Q1 revenue and margins beat, and—most importantly—management raised FY27 constant-currency revenue growth (to 5–6%) and lifted operating margin expansion (to 60–80 bps), including improved gross margin outlook. China is guided to moderate to mid-teens (a known sensitivity from the note) and North America had timing effects, limiting upside versus a potential “priced-for-perfection” raise.

Revenue and bookings materially beat the pre-release setup (record revenue, record backlog, >1.0x book-to-bill), and FY revenue guidance was reaffirmed with improved visibility. Main offsets were still-negative adjusted EBITDA and management’s caution on near-term gross margin due to EAC adjustments; with guidance held at the same $450–$500 range the market’s core thesis doesn’t break.

Q2 beat was driven by upside EBITDA/margins and air bookings +1% vs near-flat expectations, consistent with the note’s “volume miss but rate/mix + cost offsets” base case—so not an outsized surprise. However, guidance was meaningfully improved (FY pro forma Adj. EBITDA to ~$600M and FCF to ~- $65M vs -$70M), plus the quarter’s margin expansion and resilient corporate demand improved the probability of the bull/base path. Offset: the Q3/Q4 EBITDA guide implies seasonality but does not clearly re-accelerate beyond expectations, keeping reaction around the positive-moderate range.

Q2 delivered upside momentum with revenue/EBITDA well above the pre-release modeled baseline (~$205M rev, EBITDA ~$88–92M) and Q3 adjusted EBITDA raised to $90–105M (above the ~$80–95M range referenced in the note). While some EPS may be pressured by interest expense (and EPS vs consensus is closer to inline), the combination of stronger operating performance plus higher guidance supports a moderately positive tape reaction versus a stock that was positioned to discount execution risk.

UGI reaffirmed FY26 adjusted EPS guidance ($2.75–$2.90), which was the market’s key baseline per the pre-release note; the quarter showed lower Q3 segment EBIT (AmeriGas pressure) consistent with downside risk, with mixed operational updates (better attrition/leverage) that only partially offset weaker profitability.

Q2 and (especially) FY outlook were stronger than the pre-print base case: revenue, adj. EBITDA margin expansion, and adj. EPS exceeded the note’s ~$0.24/Q2 expectation while management raised FY revenue/EBITDA and the FY EPS range slightly. The only notable headwind is Nordion’s strong first-half indicating tougher comps (already flagged as the key risk), limiting upside reaction. Leverage and liquidity improved further.

EPS of $1.00 was roughly inline-to-slightly below the pre-release EPS expectation (~$1.14), but management stayed on track/explicitly reaffirmed RJO synergy ramp (run-rate exiting Q3 ~$37–38M; mid-$40M target by FY-end; $50M by early FY27). The key offset is that physical/precious metals rose YoY but fell vs the prior record quarter and FX/CFD was weak, muting the upside; with the stock not positioned as a deep-beaten name, the net effect points to a near-median reaction.

Quarter delivered an EPS beat on record EBITDA and margin expansion, driven by better-than-typical fuel surcharge recovery and stronger independent case acceleration (now 5.1%). However, management reaffirmed FY guidance and the note already flagged a low quarterly bar; upside is therefore moderate rather than a rerating.

Q3 itself is essentially in-line vs the preview’s “formality” framing (EBITDA only slightly below the ~$41M expectation). The key change is guidance: full-year adjusted EBITDA midpoint raised to $230M, but the note’s main caution (conservative back-half / credibility line around Salt costs) is reinforced by higher-than-expected Goderich production & distribution costs and a narrowed salt guide. Net effect is a modestly positive, not outsized, reaction.

Revenue beat driven by ~9% organic growth and positive FX. However EPS is slightly below the note’s $0.62 consensus despite strong margins (record 34.9% gross; operating margin 10.2%). Orders/book-to-bill and backlog strength exceed the note’s bull/base emphasis, supporting a positive reaction, but the lack of a clean EPS beat tempers the upside.

Quarterly organic revenue and EPS beat, and—most importantly—full-year organic growth guidance was raised to 8–11% (well above the note’s maintained 2–6% base case). Underlying margins were roughly stable (21% down only on acquisition dilution and tough comp), while pull-forward demand helped; FCF was a modest disappointment but not large enough versus the stronger growth outlook.

No pre-release note or consensus was provided, so relative surprise vs expectations is unknown. On the call, growth and orders/backlog look strong (revenue milestone, $130M+ orders, record backlog), but non-GAAP EPS declined year over year and gross margin was pressured by purchase accounting and Brazil labor, suggesting near-term margin headwinds—supporting a roughly neutral-to-mildly positive reaction.

The quarter does not clearly beat consensus expectations on EPS, and FY2026 guidance is reaffirmed. Key disappointment vs the pre-release setup: management guided the remaining 2H APT uptick to the lower end of the prior range (implying less spread benefit), and spreads narrowed faster since June. Partially offsets: implementation of annualized operating income increases and O&M guidance were updated, but the underlying message points to margin headwinds/timing risk into FY27.

Headline underlying execution was strong (record adjusted EBITDAX/net income; power GWh and spark spread improved), but guidance worsened versus what the note flagged as the key risk: power strategic capital was raised materially to $400–$475M and BKV will likely require more capital without a signed PPA. Production guidance rose slightly, and PPA timing was reiterated, leaving investors focused on the higher capex/binary counterparty risk.

Reported Q2 EPS isn’t clearly above what the note framed as the main risk (the contracting narrative), but the company raised FY26 adj. operating EPS guidance and provided concrete contracting progress: ~920 MW of new long-term nuclear deals and ~30% contracted clean baseload. Underlying power/reliability metrics were also strong (93% capacity factor; refueling outages better than industry), so the guidance beat plus tangible contract momentum should drive a mildly positive reaction despite already-expected fundamentals.

Headline EPS rose largely due to ~$125M insurance EBITDA recognized in Q2 (already a key wildcard in the pre-release note). Underlying operating costs improved (met cash cost guidance cut and HCV/thermal cost near the cost-curve), but PRB sales volumes fell sharply and HCV thermal full-year cost guidance was raised due to inflation, which dampens the cost-normalization narrative. Net effect points to a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction versus the market’s guidance-cost focus.

Q2 delivered clear revenue outperformance and a guidance raise (FY revenue to $805–820M), beating the note’s “soft bar” concern. However, the key margin risk (forgivable-loan/amortization narrative) was not explicitly resolved on the call summary provided, and DSO rose to 113 days—so EPS was only effectively inline vs the small-consensus bar.

Q2 and margins beat the note’s “management pre-framed” setup (revenue 32% Y/Y; adj. EBITDA and gross margin expansion). Guidance was also raised (FY net sales and adj. EBITDA midpoints above the note’s midpoint), and demand commentary supports better mix/organic traction; no meaningful incremental negatives were highlighted despite FX headwinds.

Q2 headline EPS and margin beat with strong orders/book-to-bill and a large FCF beat, but revenue is slightly below consensus and—critically—FY EPS guidance is raised only modestly (to $15.10–$15.40 vs consensus largely spanning ~$14.90–15.30). Given the stock’s rich pre-print positioning and that management already pre-flagged a second-half/rich margin profile, the net outcome skews to roughly median/neutral reaction despite quality beats.

No pre-release note or consensus figures were provided, but management delivered clearly strong Q2 operating performance (22% sales growth, 13% adjusted EPS growth, ~150 bps organic EBITDA margin expansion) and raised full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $4.22-$4.42 alongside record SAT backlog and ongoing international growth/capacity expansion.

The note already framed Q2 as a structurally weak/war-quarter driven by fewer and lower-fee Gulf races, and management reiterated that calendar variance is the driver (e.g., season revenue recognition step-down) rather than underlying demand. With no clear guidance raise/cut in the facts provided, the upside comes mainly from qualitative MotoGP momentum and hospitality sell-through—offsetting limited quantitative upside visibility, keeping reaction near-neutral-to-slightly positive.

Reported results were strong on operating metrics (Q3 adj. EBITDA and NAS margin/day) but EPS/ headline were distorted by the Utica Square gain and select items, while the pre-release note already expected results to be near the guidance midpoint. The key swing is the raised full-year NAS rig and Q4 NAS direct margin guidance, but some Saudi reactivation lag (two rigs excluded from Q4) tempers the upside versus the bull case.

HWM delivered a clear Q2 beat (revenue/EPS all above the top end of guidance) and, most importantly, raised full-year revenue/EBITDA/EPS and provided a strong Q3 guide. With the stock already priced for near-perfection, the reaction is positive but likely not outsized beyond a normal beat-and-raise profile.

EPS/AOI ex-Closed Block beat (Enact $143M contribution), and capital-return guidance to Enact for FY26 ($445–485M) plus raised buyback ($225–250M) were constructive. Offsetting negatives were meaningful: CareScout revenue/matches are below what the preview implied for Q2 pace, and the Closed Block loss widened with management warning FY full-year A/E losses could exceed expectations—undercutting the re-rating thesis that depends on containing LTC tail risk.

No pre-release note or reported revenue/EPS numbers were provided, so surprise vs consensus can’t be quantified. On the qualitative fundamentals, management highlighted underwriting improvement ex-cat and substantial cash-flow funding capacity, which should be net supportive; however, reported group combined ratio deterioration (111.6%) from catastrophe and prior-year development is a clear negative headline item.

Reported Q2 operating growth and labor/margin metrics broadly matched the note’s base expectations, but management still raised FY2026 guidance—incrementally supportive versus the derived consensus. The key offset is the guidance cut to net provider tax benefits (~$10M vs prior ~$21M, with retroactive Florida Medicaid impact), which tempers the quality of the raise; overall reaction should be modestly positive given the rest of the operating momentum and MA pilot data.

IBP beat on revenue and adjusted EPS versus a bearish-consensus setup, helped by commercial strength and large distribution/other growth, but adjusted gross margin fell (33.3% vs 34.2%) and management flagged potential Q3 margin drag from spray-foam pass-through timing lag and moderating heavy commercial growth vs tough 2H comps. Guidance (FY gross margin range) was effectively reaffirmed/unchanged per the note, so the stock reaction skews modestly positive rather than outsized.

Underlying EBITDA growth remained strong even after excluding cyber-event insurance, and the company raised FY26 adj. EBITDA growth to 22%–28% (vs the note’s expectation that reaffirmation would be most likely; this is a clear guidance upgrade). Digital mix and cash-cost deleveraging drove margin expansion; subscriber base was roughly consistent with the note’s trough baseline rather than a fresh breakdown.

Q3 operating performance was solid (record-adjusted EBITDA; expanding margin; Americas strength), but the key overhang from the pre-note—FCF reconciliation and a trimmed/pro-cyclical FY outlook—remains: full-year adjusted EBITDA was moved to the low end on inflation/macro uncertainty, with Europe still soft. Call suggests the beat was more about timing/conversion than a clearly improved durability story, putting the reaction near-median.

Q2 revenue and EPS both beat consensus, but the bigger swing factor from the pre-release note—FY26 EPS “generally in line with FY25” being arithmetically hard—was largely defanged by management explicitly framing remaining EPS impact as limited OMARS charges and reaffirming the same FY26 revenue range with an expected ~flat EPS vs 2023. At the same time, demand was described as flat and margin was only set to normalize to mid-13%, keeping upside capped versus a true growth/upgrade setup.

Reported net revenue slightly exceeds the $1.98B consensus, but the key “carry the cost / none of the benefit” story (TEGNA integration constraints) is already the market’s baseline. Political pacing came in ahead (political $147M, targets raised; ahead of the note’s ~$120–150M base range), while nonpolitical softness still matches the expected down mid-single-digits guide, keeping the overall reaction near-median.

Revenue landed essentially in-line with the guided range, but adjusted EBITDA missed the original Q2 guide due to ongoing coiled-tubing margin compression. Q3 EBITDA was guided flat to modestly down and the coiled tubing units have maintenance downtime extending toward year-end, making the outcome weaker than the note’s base-case conversion expectation despite completion-tools strength.

On the surface PRI delivered a strong EPS and ISP-led growth profile (record AUM/net inflows), but the release added meaningful new downside to the key distribution/agent metric (sales force outlook cut to flat-to-down 2%; issued policies still declining) while margins/claims ratio worsened and taxes benefited EPS via a tax equity item (non-operating). With the stock near highs and guidance now more cautious on the sales force, the market is likely to treat this as a negative despite the EPS beat.

Headline revenues/EPS are mixed, but the pre-release note’s core debate was Specialty durability in peak storm season. Q2 Specialty combined ratio printed 98% with explicit reserve/assumption charges, and management now frames low-90s combined ratio as the new “reflective” level (vs mid/high-80s historically), which is worse than the note’s base/bull path. Buyback/dividends were supportive, but underlying profitability and the implied earnings power step-down dominate, leading to a negative reaction despite revenue growth.

The call delivered record Q2 free cash flow ($751M, $0.88/share) and raised full-year oil production guidance to 199,000 bbl/d while lowering the CapEx midpoint. This is better than what the note’s base case implied (FCF reset + H2 flexibility) and does not show the key feared issue (worsening gas drag/Waha or a weaker liquidity outlook). However, headline EPS/revenue beat sizing can’t be scored because the release facts provided don’t include reported revenue/EPS vs the note’s consensus.

Q2 headline revenue and adj. EPS beat the pre-release range, but the release signals margin pressure is worsening: FY26 guide is maintained while gross profit and adjusted EBITDA are expected to land at the lower end due to interchange cost pressure and buyer-funded payables booked on a gross basis. Leverage improved to 3.8x, which offsets some downside, but the guided margin/EBITDA lower-end outcome likely limits upside versus what was hoped for in the base case.

While oil production/momentum and FY oil volume guidance were raised (supportive for the long-run growth story and above what the note modeled), free cash flow sharply deteriorated due to much higher CapEx and leverage increased. With key near-term delivery (Targa) pushed to early Q4 and temporary shut-ins from midstream constraints, the outcome looks mixed versus a note that already expected hedge/gas noise and possible EPS softness—so the net reaction skews negative.

Revenue and adjusted EPS beat the stale consensus, and—more importantly—2H production guidance was raised (435–440 MBoe/d) while capex guidance was reaffirmed and synergy execution is nearly complete (95% of $375M run-rate). With net debt falling toward low-1x and buybacks delivered, the print is better than the note’s base case; downside priced via skew is likely offset.

ORA delivered a sizable Q2 revenue beat and raised FY26 guidance (reaffirmed growth profile rather than a trim), which is directionally better than the note’s base/bear setup for a guidance-update quarter. However, management explicitly guided H2 Energy Storage merchant margin normalization and confirmed Product/backlog deterioration, limiting upside vs the already-drawn bear risk; overall expectation is modestly positive for the print-plus-raise.

Q2 delivered a large adjusted EPS shortfall versus consensus largely driven by weaker gross margin and higher opex, while management also cut FY adjusted EPS and EBITDA and pushed ERP optimization/normal ops back (now 1H’27 for North America; EMEA beyond 2026). Orders/backlog were stronger, but the margin/profitability and timeline deterioration dominate near-term sentiment.

Q1 came in materially worse on both segments (tobacco op income collapse; ingredients swing to a loss) and management explicitly framed weakness as timing tied to oversupply, with uncommitted inventory only expected to drift toward the 20% target as the season progresses. Even though dark air-cured write-downs are not expected to repeat, the core inventory/timing problem looks worse than the already-thin $0.25/EPS anchor, supporting a negative near-term reaction.

Q1 showed a strong top-line and margin beat versus the note’s base case (including 35.8% margin up 230 bps). However, management explicitly pre-guided sequential Q2 EBITDA margin compression greater than normal (~300 bps typical) from resin headwinds, and FY27 guidance was maintained while the Street was already at the midpoint—limiting upside. Options imply a modest ~8.6% move with slight downside skew, consistent with a near-median reaction.

Headline profitability/cash flow beat (FCF +50% seq to $31M; adj. EBITDA $54M) and Q2 LOE ($72M) came in below the $71–79M guide midpoint, easing the key cost-discipline worry from the preview. Q3 guidance also looks incrementally better (34.7k boe/d avg reported with Q3 guide >35k), supporting a modestly positive repricing despite an already oil-driven setup.

Q2 beat on revenue and profitability versus a consensus that called for modest improvement (+$0.03 EPS). However, management indicated cost of services is expected to increase sequentially in Q3 and characterized pipeline growth into Q3 as only modest amid choppy rates, which tempers enthusiasm; the stock was already run up and the note flagged sequential gross-margin risk.

Q3 delivered strong beats on the real scorecards (GMV +10% to $453M, adj. EBITDA +30% to $22M, adj. EPS $0.45). However, the setup mattered: shares were priced for continued execution and the pre-release note expected broadly in-line outcomes with a tight focus on Q4. Q4 guidance also came in at the low end only modestly above expectations (adj. EPS $0.41–$0.50), so the print is more likely a modest positive than a re-rate catalyst.

Reported EPS and revenue both came in below the pre-release base case, despite strong record volumes and positive narrative. Realized royalty production and produced-water were very strong (supports underlying), but the weaker-than-modeled headline economics (implied realized pricing/other lines vs expectations) and the absence of quantified Kilby terms keep the market from rewarding fully; guidance was maintained.

Headline EPS modestly beat the ~$1.88 mean and, more importantly, management raised the cost-savings run-rate to ~$500M and lifted Permian oil production guidance while cutting lease operating expense. The pre-release note framed Q2 as largely de-risked and focused the market on H2/FCF and Egypt—those appear broadly held (Egypt FCF impact minimal; cost/LOE and debt paydown supportive), limiting upside beyond relief on a stock not priced for perfection after the earlier run-up.

Revenue and visit/rate trends exceeded the preview’s organic-quality checks (record revenue/visit, 33.5 avg daily visits, and $5.6M affiliation contribution). However, adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat vs expectations of ~+4–6% and adj. EPS fell to $0.75 vs $0.85 consensus, with margin pressure from self-insured costs and clinician hiring. Guidance was reaffirmed in line, but the key “Q2 EBITDA must show the H2 ramp” test failed, which should cap upside on a stock that was already positioned for credibility.

Revenue was essentially in line with the pre-release setup, while adjusted EBITDA ($49.7M) clears the note’s key ~$49M catalyst. However, management reiterated full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance and the stock already benefited from a tower-sale narrative; the underlying 2H outlook still appears muted by the guided $1M/period EBITDA drag and conservative capital allocation framing, supporting only a modestly positive reaction.

The release was a severe headline EPS miss driven by a one-time hedge loss tied to the failed Two Harbors deal, but the key stock-moving items (preferred coupon disclosed at 10% and large warrant package) still resolve uncertainty in a way that remains unattractive for common holders. Despite operating gain-margin strength, the capital-structure shock (dividend suspension + new preferred coupon) dominates and likely adds downside/volatility after an already large pre-drop.

Headline Q2 adjusted EPS of $0.54 beat the $0.40–$0.41 consensus (~+32%), but the key yardstick was whether FY26 guidance would be narrowed/lowered (bear trigger). Management reaffirmed $4.25–$4.45 and reiterated optimism on data-center negotiations (definitive agreements expected in Q3 2026) with no stated derailment from Crusoe’s exit. Despite the beat, expected reaction is only modest because the quarter-to-quarter surprise is largely secondary to merger/data-center catalysts and guidance held steady (base-case).

Revenue and total adjusted EBITDA beat the pre-release setup, but the key thesis margin line is only partially validated: stimulation margin was 9% (below the ~11–12% watch), proppant profitability remained weak (5% margin). Guidance was maintained (CapEx/cost program) while liquidity/FCF remains pressured (FCF -$8M; liquidity tight), tempering upside versus the note’s bear-case framework.

Headline revenue/FCF were strong, but the call emphasized acquisition/PPA noncash charges that inflated CAS and confirmed constrained realized-price assumptions (gold $4,000/oz, silver $60/oz) with second-half weighting while ramp timing for New Afton was pushed to early Q4. For a stock already set up for uncertainty, the key unresolved risk (margin/guide durability amid silver weakness) didn’t clearly improve versus what the note flagged.

Reported Q2 cash flow and shareholder returns beat, and oil volumes met/cleared the high end while FY oil volume guidance was maintained. However, the release raised full-year LOE (cost inflation) and guided LOE up even as the strip has weakened—reducing confidence that the FY FCF $1.4B @ $80 deck is fully protected—so the beat is only modestly supportive given the market’s ‘guide risk’ framing going in.

Despite a bullish mid-cycle EBITDA/FCF raise, the reported Q2 EPS ($4.73) was well below the ~$5.63–$5.71 consensus/whisper framed in the note, and fixed-cost pressures were noted. Guidance lift appears to be more about longer-term mid-cycle than replacing the near-term forward curve concerns highlighted pre-release; the delayed Yazoo City restart (now 1H27) is a fresh negative versus the note’s FY26 production watch item.

Headline adjusted EPS of $1.39 beats the ~$1.26 consensus bar, but the key margin narrative broke: management guided to modest second-half compression after an exceptional 17.8% Q2 margin, citing front-loaded recruiting/acquisitions. With the stock already up strongly into the print and refi/orders softness implied by guidance, the directional guide/margin deceleration outweighs the beat.

Revenue and adj. EPS beat consensus meaningfully, helped by strong performance chemicals and record FCF/OCF. However, the release still confirms the key overhang from the note—CMC remains weak (down to $8M) and coal tar/raw material pressure persists—while FY adj.
