EBITDA guidance is only reiterated (upper end effectively trimmed vs prior positioning), leading to a roughly neutral-to-slightly positive reaction.

Quarter beat on both revenue (+29% YoY to $71.3M) and adjusted EPS ($0.49, +22% vs $0.40 expectation), with a record backlog ($557M) and strong space/defense order momentum (2.3x space book-to-bill; $61.8M defense orders). Guidance was reaffirmed (no upside/trim), and gross margin is 25% vs 26.5% last year but improved sequentially and still supports the maintained FY27 EBITDA range—so the market reaction is moderately positive rather than a rerating.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat/strengthened (record revenue; margin 89% with rising FCF), and power/digital LOI momentum was reiterated. However, FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed (no raise/narrowing from the already raised range), which is a key requirement in the pre-release setup for a larger upside reaction.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so beats/misses can’t be quantified. However, the company raised full-year 2026 stand-alone production growth guidance (from 5% to 6%) and reported record production and strong operating margins, partially offset by a very low reinvestment rate (D&C at 34% of EBITDAX) that suggests slower growth capital intensity and higher reliance on the acquisition/financing plan.

LOAR delivered a clear Q2 beat (sales and adjusted EPS) and—more importantly—raised 2026 guidance to the upper end/above the prior range, with margin expansion to a record 40.5% and stronger commercialization/aftermarket signals. This counters the note’s core risk that only an reaffirm or small raise would be insufficient for a stock priced for sustained beat-and-raise.

EPS and operating performance beat expectations, with a significantly improved P&C combined ratio and higher P&C core earnings. However, the print also includes a weaker full-year net investment income guide and cut in catastrophe assumptions where management explicitly flags no continuation into 2H, partially offsetting the raise. Net effect is positive but not a huge upside because the stock was already well positioned into the release and guidance is only modestly above the high end of what the note modeled.

Headline Q2 sales were slightly above the pre-release $136.6M but the gross margin spike was largely driven by a large IEPA tariff refund, so underlying profitability signal is weaker. The key takeaway is guidance: full-year net sales was maintained while adjusted profitability/EBITDA/net income guidance was raised; however, management also flagged potential Hagerstown startup disruption and higher distribution expense, and Dolly Parton growth is only modest—keeping the H2 bridge credibility risk elevated versus what the market was already watching.

Cheniere delivered the big market item—an additional FY26 guidance raise with both EBITDA and DCF stepping up to levels above the note’s base case and implying a more durable ~$8B+ run-rate. Underlying Q2 operating metrics looked better (adj. EBITDA, DCF, exports/shipments), partially offset by less friendly macro/flows (Strait of Hormuz disruption and Europe inventory tightness), but not enough to derail the forward contract/optimization narrative already emphasized in the note.

No pre-release note or consensus provided, so surprise is hard to quantify. While the company raised full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance, the call emphasized that margin expansion was largely driven by IEEPA tariff refunds and one-time tax benefits; underlying gross margin was only ~30 bps higher YoY, and Q4 is guided to margin decline in WMS due to backlog normalization and a residential slowdown—limiting upside for the stock.

The quarter’s key operating read-through is broadly supportive (same-store fuel volumes held up; controllables supply margin improved; loyalty strength; conservative but non-negative back-half all-in fuel margin guide ~$/gal 0.35 with upside). However, the pre-release note flags the central risk—fuel supply inventory revaluation and guidance that may not close the FY gap vs Street—and the release does not provide clear upside to offset that. With the stock already strong and option-implied absolute move modest (~6.9%), the setup points to a neutral-to-slightly negative reaction rather than a positive rerating.

The market setup heavily centered on gas-realization uncertainty and whether the Hugh Brinson/ET uplift would land in Q2. Management reported near-record Q2 free cash flow, a debt-paydown step, outperformance to the top end of production guidance, raised full-year oil growth guidance (4–7%), and reduced capex—collectively a better-than-base outcome versus the note’s base/bear tensions. While the quarter also included a non-recurring marketing gain, the key operating narrative (higher volumes, improved forward oil/growth/capex, early pipeline benefits) points to a supportive though not blowout reaction.

Q4 delivered a clear adj. EPS beat (record $9.27). More importantly, FY27 adjusted EPS guidance of $34.75 at the midpoint is above the $34.03 anchored consensus in the pre-note, alongside continued margin expansion and strong orders/backlog—although much of the narrative around Filtration/Aerospace was already anticipated, limiting upside.

Q2 underlying adjusted EBITDA came in at a record $1.603B versus a ~$1.42–1.47B (derived ~$1.45B) bar, and management moved FY26 EBITDA toward the top of the $5.7–$5.9B range. Upside is supported by record Permian volumes and downstream throughput; while marketing outperformance was assumed to fade in H2, the quarter still exceeded the market’s key “marketing-normalized” risk.

Q2 revenue came in slightly above the note’s base case and margins (via LOE guide) were not worse, while leverage improved faster due to the equity-funded revolver paydown and 2H oil volume guidance was modestly raised. However, the note flagged the key swing factor (oil hedge settlement/FCF reconciliation) as a likely bear driver; the company also raised full-year capex materially, partially conflicting with the note’s debt-paydown/discipline emphasis, and natural gas differentials remain pressured—limiting upside in spite of headline beats.

Q3 distributable earnings ($0.48) and adjusted EBITDA ($19.7M) met company guidance, with recurring service revenues slightly above the ~$44M expectation (reported $45.5M) and incentive-fee pace upgraded to >$40M for CY26. However, recurring service revenue is guided flat (~$45M) next quarter as Greenwich fee tailwinds roll off, and EBITDA margin remains in the low-40s amid an OPI-related impairment, limiting upside versus a largely pre-framed/“mechanical” quarter.

For LBRDK itself, the pre-release note argued the earnings print was largely non-informative and that trading should be driven by the CPUC Aug 13 / DOJ HSR Sept 15 process and the CHTR tape. On the call, fundamentals were mixed-to-soft (OIBDA -11%, FCF down, margin down), but the dividend and Quintillion synergy/accretion framework reduce downside—so the net reaction is near-median.

Headline storage and moving revenue were roughly in line, and disposal losses improved. However, EBITDA margin fell ~1.5% (expense/cost pressure and freight headwinds), fleet depreciation increased in Q1 (though the post-April run-rate suggests the prior headwinds are easing), and EPS materially missed the (already unreliable) pre-release range—while same-store occupancy declined further. Given the stock was priced for the depreciation inflection, this is more of a confirmation-but-not-a-beat setup versus what the note required.

Q2 EPS is essentially in-line with the note’s conservative consensus expectations, but results and capital returns beat (production above the top of guidance; buybacks doubled to $2B) with FY/FCF messaging reaffirmed (FCF breakeven to low-$30s WTI by 2029). Importantly, the feared second production/guidance cut did not materialize—Q3 guidance assumes Qatar ramp—so the release is more a relief-and-strong execution story than a downside surprise.

LEGH delivered a clear beat on both revenue and EPS versus the pre-release consensus (and shipped meaningfully into the workforce housing contract), but the key re-rating driver was already largely assumed in the note (base/bull scenarios centered on unit deliveries and margins holding). No guidance raise/cadence shock was provided, and the tax-rate normalization toward 21% in 2H is a known offset; therefore reaction is modestly positive rather than a major upside.

DXP delivered a clear upside print: revenue and adjusted EBITDA margin (12.2%, record) came in materially above the $543M / ~11.4% setups, and EPS rose to $1.76 vs $1.59 consensus. With the stock already up ~15% off the late-July low and trading at a higher-than-peer multiple, some of the upside was likely expected, but the margin expansion plus strong FCF inflection supports a meaningfully positive next-day move.

Revenue was effectively pre-disclosed (range capped) so the print is not a new information shock. Adjusted EPS of $2.56 is in the expected DD&A/tax mechanics, while liquidity/deleveraging and buybacks were largely aligned with the note’s bull/base setup; portfolio/copper strength and slightly better cash/FCF are the main incremental positives.

Strong top-line and profitability growth (revenue +36% YoY; adj. EPS +33%) alongside improved same-store margins and higher full-year guidance. Offsetting factors include integration/lumpiness from newly acquired low-occupancy senior living communities and negative revenue-per-episode pressure in home health driven by CMS wage indexes/seasonality. Without the pre-release consensus, the magnitude of beat vs expectations is uncertain.

EPS beat consensus ($1.16 vs ~$1.01) and management confirmed no FY26 guidance change (reaffirmed $4.80–$5.30). Underlying quarter strength came from a clearer-than-feared Oncor catch-up ($~50M in Q1 related benefit plus $138M Texas y/y), but the call introduced a delay risk to Texas batch-zero visibility (capex timing pushed toward later in 2027), which offsets some of the positive impulse. Market reaction expected slightly positive given guidance is held and the stock was not positioned for perfection per the note.

No pre-release note/consensus provided, but the release showed strong growth and a large margin expansion alongside a guidance raise to 2026 revenue, organic growth, and EBITDA margin. Offset somewhat by management’s commentary that Q4 organic growth will be flattish on tough comps, tempering the forward trajectory.

Headline EPS and free cash flow materially beat the pre-release EPS range, and midstream/marketing handily exceeded the guide (plus an increase to segment guidance). Crucially, management also offered meaningful incremental cash-flow/midstream upside and reiterated the overall capital-deleveraging framework without a guidance reset, limiting downside despite permissive oil-price dynamics already priced in.

Underlying profitability improved (gross margin + YoY to 40.6% and operating income +21%) and RaiseWell enrolled 270k head—both are key positives vs the note’s setup. However, EPS declined due to non-operating/non-cash digital-asset mark and missing prior-year dividend, muting the headline impact; with guidance not provided, the net setup is modestly positive.

EPS beat is clear ($1.09 vs $0.93 consensus), supported by higher consumption and a better water supply mix, but management explicitly warned those favorable conditions may reverse later in 2026 and the stock was already positioned for a modest/limited upside. Guidance was effectively maintained (ASUS FY2026 contribution still $0.63–$0.67).

Revenue and margins came in clearly above the note’s $214–$217M revenue expectations (record $224.5M; gross margin +160 bps; adj. EBITDA margin 17.1%), and RPO/book-to-bill were stronger. However, EPS growth appears materially lifted by a one-time compensation clawback, and management also guided that H2 growth moderates to low-to-mid single digits—conflicting with the note’s base/bull emphasis that destocking could already be fading. With the stock priced near highs into the print, the net setup is still more likely to disappoint than rally.

Results were better than the note’s base/bear mainly on operating leverage (adj. EBITDA positive; operating income swing), and 45Z supported the quarter. However, the note emphasized the balance-sheet/going-concern and refinancing binary; reported cash was only ~$1M with no refinancing update, creating incremental dilution/going-concern anxiety. Additional negatives came from the low-yield near-term 45Z dairy valuation (relying on a future DOE correction) and debt paydown dependency on future credit/catch-up.

Headline EPS ($0.10) beat the note’s $0.08 base-case, but the note already expected a penny-level outcome and flagged guidance language as the primary driver; management reaffirmed FY26 EPS $0.93–$1.00 (no raise/narrow). Underlying mix showed some segment softness (pipeline earnings down), while Bakken/data-center positives were mostly about pipeline progress already in the narrative. Net: modestly positive but largely anticipated.

Q2 delivered a near-inline revenue print but returned to non-GAAP profitability better than the guided loss (helped by tax benefits/subsidies). The key market risk—Q3 and the gross-margin/2H ramp math—did not get clearly improved: Q3 revenue guide ($255–290M) is broadly consistent with the note’s base, while capex + dilution under an ATM raises financing overhang; 100G softness and the sharp Q3 EPS range also limit upside. Net: modestly positive but largely priced given the pre-release melt-up and call-skew/options move.

No consensus/research note was provided and the release content is largely operational (samples/MOU/partnerships) with no reported revenue/EPS benchmarks. Cash runway extended via ATM proceeds is a positive, but losses worsened and R&D/stock-comp accelerated—likely keeping sentiment muted to slightly negative-to-neutral absent clearer commercial traction.

Q2 results beat the guide/consensus (revenue above top-end; ACV+royalties record $99.5M above expectations) and full-year revenue guidance was raised. However, non-GAAP operating loss is pressured by unexpected payroll tax costs, and royalties were slightly down sequentially, limiting how “clean” the margin beat is.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat the low-bar setup and AMDS PMA-related acceleration language met expectations, but EBITDA margin declined ~90 bps on higher R&D, and FCF was materially negative due to post-acquisition costs/bonuses—offsetting the headline beat. Guidance was reiterated and back-half conservatism was explicitly maintained, keeping reaction near median despite the upside.

EPS and EBITDA came in ahead of expectations, and management raised FY SaaS and total revenue guidance plus lifted FY adj. EBITDA at the midpoint—key items the note flagged as the real test (hardware flow-through + FY EBITDA absorption). Demand/retention stayed solid and margins expanded. Upside is somewhat capped because the stock had already run and part of the backdrop was widely anticipated (tariff pass-through optics).

Q2 headline P&L was broadly in line with what the note expected, with margin down YoY from higher depreciation/colocation and Delivery continuing as the drag. The main potential upside surprise was CIS strength (39% YoY) with management emphasizing GPU capacity fully sold out into Q4; the main offset was confirmation of still-heavy capex/cost pressure (CapEx ~40% FY26; Q3 step-up), leaving the market focused on whether the FY26 H2 acceleration and RPO math remain credible rather than a large upgrade to the outlook.

Despite a strong top-line and cash return/sustained production growth, reported results lag the note’s expected oil/EPS profile: revenue is below the ~$58.7–$59.0M consensus range and adjusted EPS ($0.57) is materially under the ~$0.75 commodity-implied expectation. With the quarter widely expected to be supported by the prior oil windfall and the market already priced that dynamic, the net is a small negative/near-neutral reaction rather than a selloff.

Revenue in Q2 ($3M) and H1 ($5M) aligned with the note’s bear/base framing around the CSL wind-down rather than delivering a meaningful upside to the vulnerable H2 ramp. Guidance emphasis shifted toward the Q4’26 Phase 3 go/no-go decision (instead of earlier Phase 2 timing), and the CSL termination is a fresh negative versus the note’s “runway” assumptions, driving a likely risk-off reaction.

Q2 revenue and EPS largely track what the note framed as a modest beat/base-case setup; gross margin improved and power-liposuction momentum (expanded clearance + initial June shipments, >95% attach expectation) supports demand. Offsetting factors: operating cash burn increased and OEM revenue declined as expected, while FY26 guidance was reaffirmed (not meaningfully raised) into a stock that the note already flagged as priced for a sizable uplift after the run-up.

Despite a strong “largest-quarter” headline for Ibsrela+Xphozah, Q2 total revenue fell short of the $123.7M consensus build. More importantly, management cut FY26 Ibsrela guidance to $350–$370M (below what the pre-release note framed as the credibility threshold for keeping the back-half ramp on track), and pulled $750M long-term Xphozah guidance—together pointing to a weaker growth trajectory and margin/opex pressure.

Q2 cleared the already-high bar on both revenue and EPS, but the pre-release note framed beats as likely and the stock was priced with meaningful upside already reflected. The raise/stronger-than-expected quality (unit-volume emphasis, components margins ~sustained) offsets the ECS contract charge, and Q3 guidance still implies sequential earnings decline—limiting upside.

Q2 revenue and non-GAAP results beat the note’s bar, and management raised FY26 ARR guidance to a growth-midpoint consistent with the expected 26% constant-currency outcome. The key risk—margin/back-end credibility—looks better than feared given 16.3% non-GAAP margin vs guided ~15.8% and accelerating net new ARR, though retention remains below the 115% target (an expected overhang).

The quarter missed both the consensus revenue and especially the transaction-driven EPS (asset-sale/engine timing risk played out). Underlying margin deteriorated sharply (gross margin down to 22.9%) and EBITDA collapsed, while liquidity tightened versus a scenario the note already flagged as high-risk—despite some positives in leasing growth and TechOps ramp.

Q2 revenue/loan growth landed in-range (pre-released), but the call delivered the key risk: management confirmed it will not reach EBITDA break-even by September and gave Q3 guidance implying a sequential revenue decline and another sizable EBITDA loss. Even with higher cost cuts and more HELOC mix, the combination of missed break-even timing + weaker next-quarter trajectory drives a downside reaction versus what the market feared in the note (and especially given prior headline narrative risk).

Revenue and near-term profitability tracked expectations, and FY26 adjusted EBITDA guidance was reaffirmed. The only incremental positive is RNG upstream getting closer to breakeven with a stronger cash position, but the biggest potential swing factor (45Z GREET) was explicitly delayed to Q4 and framed as potentially dilutive to getting to the high end of the FY range—keeping the reaction modestly positive rather than a rerating.

Q1 revenue and adjusted EBITDA were essentially in-line with the pre-release underwriting (revenue at the top of the guide, EBITDA within $0–1M). The call did show some positive underlying signals (retention/LTV improving and Bark Air strong), but normalized gross margin was flat and DTC orders still declined ~28% YoY, with only the expected reliance on 2H/holiday ramp. Q2 guide also remains consistent (reaffirm full-year), so there’s no clear catalyst for a large re-rate.

Q2 headline was stronger than the note (revenue near top-of-range and non-GAAP op income topping the guide), but the key issue—the Q3 revenue guide—came in below the ~$33.9M derived consensus bar and the margin guide implies a drop (~12% vs ~18% context). While Autopilot progress was tangible (paying contracts, lender activation, pull-through/cycle-time gains), management also flagged weaker macro and churn/seasonality (marketing step-up), leading to an overall negative setup versus what the market had recently been discounting.

The company raised FY26 revenue/VOXZOGO/EPS guidance and delivered strong Q2 growth (~20% Y/Y) alongside materially higher-than-expected margin optics (36.4%). Key new information exceeded the note’s base case: quantified low competitor switching (~10% / <100 switches) and first quantified synergy run-rate ($220M by 2028) with an accretion timeline (EPS benefit starting 2027).

Headline GAAP EPS was dominated by a BTC mark-to-market, which the note framed as mechanical; underlying profitability was still weak but the release largely matched the market’s expectations for a light revenue quarter. The main new incremental upside was more concrete financing/disintermediation language (no project equity raise planned, long-lead items prepaid) supporting the lease narrative, but Q3 gross margin fell as power prices rose, limiting the upside.

Headline margins/EBITDA improved sharply versus a pessimistic setup, but the company cut FY26 revenue guidance materially (to $83–90M) from $105–115M, directly violating the note’s core H2 bridge expectations. Cash burn improved, yet service/product mix and the lowered top-line outlook likely dominate for next-day reaction.

CRVS is pre-revenue, so the release is mostly about operating updates. Headline cash/investment funding is broadly supportive vs the note’s base case, but the key incremental downside was pushing the PTCL interim futility analysis to Q1’27 (worse than prior expectation). Overall, with EPS/revenue effectively non-informative and no clear AD-enrollment disappointment (early-2027 completion still, Q3’27 topline), the net reaction is slightly negative-to-neutral.

Q3 revenue landed within the $68–72M guidance range and adjusted EBITDA beat the $8–12M band, with connected services up 20% and margin mix favorable—better than the note’s base/bear skew. However, Q4 guidance ($61–65M, adj. EBITDA $1–5M) still reflects the expected fixed-license absence and implies a weak EBITDA trough consistent with the note, limiting upside. The main additional positive is the FY26 FCF raise to $76–82M, partially offset by variable license decline and mix headwinds.

Revenue and margin improved, but the balance-sheet risk is worse than the note’s base case: total cash/risk runway was $5.9M vs the note’s focus on unrestricted cash $3.5–4.0M with sensitivity to any ATM use and cash < $3.0M. Guidance was essentially maintained (operating cash flow break-even in H2 2026 reiterated). Underlying operating loss/EBITDA improved, but the combination of thin cash runway language and ongoing Germany/Middle East weakness keeps the reaction modestly negative versus expectations.

Q2 sales and EBITDA broadly match the pre-release framing, but underlying profitability is still negative and the key credibility test deteriorates: gross margin is boosted by a tariff-refund tailwind and Q3 guide implies a further EBITDA decline (-$2.4M). Liquidity/covenant relief is a net positive yet it mainly removes tail risk rather than delivering a clear step-up in the ramp, keeping reaction negative vs what was already feared.

MYQORZO delivered a strong launch quarter (1,500 patients by end-Q2; >80% paid dispensed) and MYQORZO product revenue materially exceeded the note’s implied product threshold, but EPS missed and, more importantly, FY26 OpEx guidance was raised—confirming higher spend for the (still-uncertain) 2027 nHCM launch—on a stock priced for perfection after a huge run. Acacia trial progress was positive but broadly consistent with expectations, limiting upside.

Q2 and AI mix beat the already-low-bar setup, and FY/Q3 revenue guidance was raised (FY midpoint to $1.266B; Q3 midpoint $319M) with AI growth guidance lifted to ≥60%. The main offset is margin contraction (gross 61%, adj. EBITDA 22%) despite management attributing it to temporary professional services expansion, which caps upside.

Q2 revenue and gross margin beat/track expectations, but management cut FY2026 revenue to $58–60M (materially below the $65.28M consensus) and explicitly cited weaker second-half execution from high territory-manager turnover and negative implant growth in churned regions. Medicare Advantage prior-auth approval remains below 30% for the largest payer (despite a 60% consolidated rate), reinforcing the reimbursement execution risk and driving a negative skew vs the note’s base/bull setup.

On the quarter, results were better than the pre-release concerns, but the key EBITDA/margin upside was largely driven by a $25m tariff-related credit and the monetization of IEEPA claims—factors the note flagged as optionality. The meaningful surprise is the raised FY26 adj. EBITDA guide (to $100–$110m), but the company also reiterated flat-to-up-3% sales, limiting upside beyond profitability. Overall reaction is mildly positive.

AVLAYAH Q2 net product revenue ($3.6M) beat the ~$2.15M consensus base, and launch demand/disclosure was more constructive than the note’s mid-case, while Q2 OpEx was roughly stable. Guidance for Q3 net product revenue ($10–12M) implies strong sequential growth and is a positive relative to the launch-ramp concerns embedded in the preview; the main remaining overhang (DNL593 timing) was already flagged as a risk in the note, limiting downside from that area.

Revenue was essentially in line and sequentially flat as expected, but EPS and adjusted EBITDA losses improved meaningfully versus the pre-release yardstick. However, cash remains a key overhang (up to ~$10M at 6/30 vs the note’s $7.5M cash comfort threshold) with no explicit confirmation of 'no ATM' funding language, keeping the reaction near neutral-to-mildly positive.

Operating momentum (American Place best quarter ever, Chamonix near break-even) broadly matches the pre-release base, but the refinancing remains unsigned/“expected to close in Q3,” and rising star had an outage without insurance recovery—so the core overhang wasn’t resolved. With positioning already de-risked on solvency concerns, the net is neutral-to-slightly positive.

Q2 EPS ($1.34) beat consensus ($1.12) and EBITDA/gross margins expanded sharply, supporting a favorable read-through. Full-year EPS guidance was raised to $4.95-$5.05, above both the prior guide and the note’s base-case raise skepticism, while revenue guidance was reaffirmed (so the main disappointment vs the note is limited). The watch item was Enabling Technologies; it fell more than expected despite commentary on rental/rate model transition.

Revenue landed near the top of the wide range, and Q2 margin expanded (12.7% vs 9.7% in Q1) with a cost-savings program on track. However, the key puts/asks in the preview were the credibility of an H2 EBITDA margin step-up and limiting inflation risk; management disclosed nearly $20M of cost inflation above plan and an implied full-year margin cut to ~12.4%–13.3% (vs prior framework), which undermines the “hockey stick” needed for the FY guide. Despite a narrower/tighter EBITDA range and higher sales guide, the margin compression/inflation news is likely a net negative versus what was already feared.

Revenue is broadly in line with the pre-release setup (Q2 structurally weak/optical). The key delta is guidance: management more than doubles FY26 non-GAAP Adj. EBITDA outlook to >$60M, consistent with the note’s “$55–65M” win zone, but not beyond it enough to drive a top-quartile reaction. Offsetting that, the large Lake Preston impairment is headline-negative (even if mainly non-cash) and highlights remaining execution/timeline risk in project transitions.

Underlying profitability beat (Q2 gross profit +18%, gross margin 22.8%) and residents/scripts held up, but the setup already anticipated a modest revenue softness with margin resilience and an EBITDA/guidance outcome around reiteration-to-bump. The guidance raise is directionally supportive, yet the magnitude vs the note’s “third consecutive raise” expectation and the continued low/low-single-digit 2H reported revenue decline keep the reaction near neutral-to-slightly positive.

Q2 revenue ($3.9M) and gross margin (50.7%) broadly fit the preview’s base scenario and full-year revenue guidance ($20–22M) was reiterated, reducing guidance-driven downside risk. Management added supportive demand proof points (12 systems; first national IDN placement expanding; Contrast PMR enrollment ~75%), which modestly improves the H2 quality versus what the note implied as the main swing factor, supporting a near-median positive tape reaction.

Q2 and margin/EPS materially beat consensus, and—critically—management raised FY2026 guidance materially above the already-promising pre-release setup. With partner royalty read-throughs largely pre-positioned, the upside reaction hinges on the magnitude of the raise and stronger-than-expected royalty/product ramp, which should support a clearly positive next-day move despite already-bullish positioning.

Q2 revenue came in slightly below consensus while EPS beat was largely tax/margin/interest and share-count driven. More importantly, in-quarter book-to-bill (0.85) and backlog slip tied to slower federal awards add downside to the already back-half-loaded FY ramp, while management reaffirmed guidance without narrowing the range after a stock run-up.

ICUI delivered a bigger-than-expected Q2 (EPS and EBITDA well above consensus) and, more importantly, raised full-year adj. EPS and EBITDA while also lifting FY gross margin guidance. Despite some narrative caution that pump installations pulled forward (pressuring later-year growth), the guidance raise and margin improvement drive a clearly positive reaction versus the note’s base-case of a flat/reaffirm with limited upside.

Q2 revenue and (implied) profitability exceeded expectations, and—most importantly—FY26 revenue and adj. EBITDA margin were raised. The setup was partially priced for reimbursement/LCD relief and guidance reaffirm risk, but the stronger-than-expected Q2 margin profile plus raised EBITDA targets should drive a modest-to-positive reaction. Negative: the Baxter/Welch Allyn settlement cash outflow is a slight overhang versus a more neutral “no news” expectation.

Headline P&L/EPS look materially better than expectations largely due to non-recurring Australian R&D rebate recognition (an items-to-items swing consistent with the note), but the call also pushed the Ebstracell regulatory timeline out to end of Q3/early Q4 2026 (still not a clear “submitted/validated” catalyst) while reaffirming cash into Q2’27 and outlining ATM funding into 2027. Overall: modestly positive from improved cash runway clarity, offset by the absence of the key near-term filing confirmation that the note’s bull case depended on.

Underlying profitability and restaurant margin beat expectations, but demand quality weakened (traffic down) and the Q3 comp guide implies deceleration despite the full-year raise. With the stock already in a momentum/multiple narrative and guidance action largely aligning with a “likely raise” setup, the net reaction is mildly negative/neutral.

Revenue materially beat the derived Q2 range and programmatic/core growth stayed strong. However, gross margin was boosted by a tariff refund that was largely related to prior periods, while underlying margin remains pressured and operating cash flow turned negative—offsetting the headline profitability surge. Overall reaction is modestly positive given already-low expectations and weak positioning into the print.

Underlying financials are not particularly supportive (revenues lower vs the already-lumpy expectations; opex higher). The key swing factor is the cash/runway: cash supports ~Q3 2028 funding versus the note’s ~Q2 2028 base case, a modest positive that likely offsets limited downside from the cash-funded burn and does not introduce a new OpRegen-controlled-trial timepoint.

The quarter delivered higher-than-expected revenue ($1.5M vs ~$1.0M consensus in the pre-note) and, more importantly, management raised FY26 gross margin guidance to 40–45% from 35–40%. While the FY revenue range was reiterated (still H2-loaded), the combination of margin expansion and improved demand/activity metrics shifts the setup toward the note’s bull/base-leaning outcomes rather than the bear case.

EPS ($0.47 diluted) landed essentially in line with the pre-release consensus, but management flagged a strategic shift to hold more SBA 7(a) loans that will reduce gain-on-sale and pressure net interest income, and it will re-evaluate/redo prior Q4 guidance. With the stock near recent highs and Q2 framed as a “don’t break the story” quarter, this shift/read-through to back-half earnings quality is the key downside driver versus what was expected.

Q3 EPS is largely flattered by the ~$2M business interruption insurance recovery (a known item in the note), while underlying profitability deteriorated: gross margin fell 60 bps and adjusted EBITDA declined. Most importantly, the FY26 guidance was tightened slightly lower on comp growth (1.5%-2.0% vs 1.5%-2.5%), implying a weaker demand/traffic trajectory versus what the note framed as a key comp/traffic-driven inflection; net effect should weigh on the stock despite a small headline EPS stability.

Revenue beat was modest versus the already-low $186–202M band, and non-GAAP operating income was above the midpoint; however, management guided to higher customer-acquisition spend with a clear multi-quarter NGOI headwind (and SMB still fell), which fights any upside from the beat. Q3 growth guidance also looks supportive, but FX/funding/tax mechanics and the record FCF are partially non-recurring, limiting enthusiasm.

Q2 delivered a clear beat vs the note’s ~$695–715M hurdle (reported ~$753M) with strong gross margin (~65%) and a much stronger-than-feared Signatera unit trajectory (283k, +34k sequential). FY26 revenue guidance was raised to $2.85–$2.91B at the midpoint, beating the note’s base/raise expectations; no underlying margin/opex deterioration was indicated, though management tempered Q3 sequential growth expectations. Net effect: positive upside reaction, but moderated because the stock already had a strong run-up and the note framed a high bar.

Revenue came in well above consensus and gross margin expanded, while FY26 revenue guidance was reaffirmed in line with expectations. The HCA refresh was a first-of-its-kind $40M agreement (partly de-risking the feared 2H ramp), but overall guidance was not raised—so the reaction is modestly positive rather than a rerating shock.

Q2 materially beat (including gross/operating margin) and—critically vs the note—the Q3 revenue guide moved well above the ~$350M bar (implying FY bridge confirmation). The raise is accompanied by strong backlog visibility and sharply upgraded advanced packaging growth, leaving limited downside and supporting a strong positive next-day reaction.

Underlying Q2 revenue and EPS came in well above the note’s base/consensus setup, and the FY26 cash guidance improved. However, management explicitly said milestone revenue is front-end loaded with weaker second-half revenue, which matches the note’s risk of H2 deceleration; guidance is raised but reads partially as de-risking after a strong Q1 rather than a clear upside beat to the bull case.

Q2 headline results beat consensus and, more importantly, full-year net product revenue and net income were raised versus the note. However, the stock is priced for an alisertib re-rating with lumpy H2/royalty risk, and management trimmed royalty guidance and flagged potential China royalty rate reductions—limiting upside.

PAR delivered a meaningful profitability beat (Adj. EBITDA $14.3M vs the $9.5–11.5M guide range and ~$10.5M midpoint in the note) alongside raised FY26 revenue/EBITDA guidance. While ARR is strong and management points to faster 2H growth, hardware margins are expected to normalize after tariff/supply-chain pressure and the hardware margin drag plus normalization language caps the upside reaction.

On the core P&L, PRDO delivered roughly in line with the pre-release yardstick (revenue ~in line; adj. EPS exactly at the $0.80 top-of-range bar). The main incremental item was the tax resolution lifting the quarter, but underlying operating income quality at CTU was pressured by higher legal fees and enrollments were weak/uneven, with management calling out potential CTU second-half softening—together supporting a neutral-to-slightly-negative reaction rather than a re-rating.

The key operational update was meaningfully better than the pre-release risk case: enrollment is now expected to complete by early October 2026 (three months ahead) despite protocol amendments. The company also strengthened cash (major ATM proceeds). However, GAAP/non-GAAP losses widened and ongoing burn guidance remains heavy, limiting upside beyond a modest-to-constructive reaction given the stock was already near the highs and the consensus earnings numbers were low-information.

Revenue and gross margin improved, and management reaffirmed the $150–180M FY26 range. However, the note flagged the key gate (gross margin path and the H2 delivery schedule) and warned the Q2 set-up could be noisy; with no reported EPS beat magnitude and still elevated opex/inventory build, the print is more supportive than decisive versus the market’s base case.

The release largely confirms the pre-existing bear setup around Gauzy disruption: royalties declined and the company took reserves/going-concern language on receivables. While management added potentially constructive contingencies (Klim licensing and aircraft program wins), the core underlying margin trajectory looks worse and cash/runway risks remain, making any positive offset limited versus the delisting/financing overhang emphasized in the note.

RCEL delivered an upside revenue surprise ($21.7M vs ~$20.25M expected) and, more importantly, raised FY26 revenue guidance to $86–89M. Liquidity improved materially (net cash use ~$3.2M; cash+marketables ~$11.1M) and management added a cash breakeven/C4 shift plan plus increased debt flexibility—together more than offset that EPS remains weak and is directionally worse than modeled.

Q2 delivered upside mix (11% revenue growth, adj. EBITDA up 38% to 25% margin and FCF up 47%) and—critically—Q3 revenue guide $75–77M midpoint clears the note’s ~$75M bar, supporting the 2H reacceleration thesis. With the stock already run up and guidance action largely in-line (carried narrative/commitment), the setup is a modest beat-and-raise, not a blowout.

Underlying operating adjusted EBITDA was strong (best core quarter in ~3 years) and liquidity/maturity coverage looks well supported versus the note’s solvency focus. Offsetting negatives: trading gains were weaker than the note’s modeled carry/valuation strength and Targus remained loss-making.

Q2 largely matched the setup (adj. revenue near the guide midpoint; adj. EPS $0.16). The key surprise is the Q3 guide: management guided adjusted revenue to $2.5–$2.7B vs the note’s base/bear framework centered higher ($2.7–2.9B), effectively signaling sequential contraction despite rate pressure—more negative than expected. Margin expansion is a partial offset (28% vs 26% in Q1), but the demand/volume narrative broke bearish with the softer Q3 midpoint.

Revenue and gross margin beat and management raised FY26 revenue guidance, but the stock also reported a materially wider-than-expected net loss (SG&A ramp) with only mixed clarity on the H2 phasing given Europe/tender delays. Overall reaction is near-median for this high-risk CGM name: positives are partially expected in the setup, while loss widening offsets the guidance raise.

Q4 topped consensus on revenue/EPS with continued margin strength, but guidance is partially offset by first-time forward guide featuring an Astral field safety-driven FY2027 revenue headwind (~130bp) and EPS drag, limiting the rerating. Mask growth (10–12%) supports the GLP-1 narrative, but the device declines in Americas/Rest-of-World likely keep investors cautious.

While cash/runway increased and Phase 3 RESCUE site enrollment is underway (~80 sites), the key overhang in the note was IND/initial Phase 3 initiation by mid-2026 and year-end 2026 3-month data. Management disclosed the year-end three-month complete response timing may slip to first-half 2027 due to manufacturing/GMP execution delays, which is a catalyst slip for an options/biotech story. The quarter’s EPS line is less relevant given the research note’s framing and lack of reliable consensus reconciliation.

The quarter came in better than the pre-release modeled Q2 (~$23M revenue, EPS ~$0.07) with ~$38M product revenue and ~$0.17 EPS. However, the key overhang from the note—no new U.S. oral TPOXX contract yet and continued slowness commentary—remains intact, so the surprise is largely about timing/scale of deliveries rather than de-risking the FY27 contract vacuum.

Revenue landed below the lower end of the guided range and below the pre-release consensus, with delivery systems/consumables still weakening. However, underlying profitability (adj. EBITDA) beat the guided range and FY EBITDA was raised, plus gross margin expanded sharply; the guidance raise is partially offset by a still-concerning second-half EBITDA deceleration and the continued solvency/stock-price overhang (Oct 2026 maturity and reverse-split approval). Net reaction is mildly negative/neutral given the multiple moving pieces vs the note’s key watchitems.

Underlying quarter looks better than the note’s base: stronger-than-feared US comps (+6.6%) and expanding adjusted EBITDA margin (16.6%) plus Canada margin expansion. However, management only raised the low end of FY net sales guidance and the stock had already run materially into the print, so the reaction is positive but not outsized. Q3 EBITDA is guided modestly below Q2 (timing/pre-opening), which limits upside.

Q2 itself was largely de-risked by the prior pre-announcement (high end) so the quarter does not meaningfully surprise. The key incremental item is guidance: management raised FY26 non-GAAP profitability/ EPS and guided to ~17% exit margin, but the Q3 guide implies deceleration and moderation/continued pressure in CRPO and sub-30K cohort before stabilizing—limiting upside.

Q2 revenue was essentially in-line but margins and adjusted EBITDA improved materially (underlying margin up), while management reaffirmed FY revenue and the harder FY EBITDA range with only modest Q3 phasing detail. However, the quarter still showed a widened net loss and management reiterated the inventory/build and back-half-weighted GTA VI/CoD timing—key risks already highlighted in the pre-release note—so upside is likely limited versus the setup.

Revenue landed around the high end of the note’s implied range (note expected ~$9.3M; reported $11.4M), but the key yardstick—FY2026 guidance—was reiterated at $54–57M versus a base case of a cut/narrowing. Offsetting that, operating performance deteriorated (adjusted EBITDA loss widened; S&M scaled up to ~100% of revenue) which is consistent with the note’s concern that the H2 ramp may still be fragile. Net: modestly positive but not a decisive beat for a guidance-driven, high-doubt story.

Revenue and margin came in very much in line with the pre-release base case, and FY guidance was reaffirmed. The upside is stronger gross margin and Mobi volume scaling; the downside is formulary coverage at ~45% (below the >50% “bull” checklist) and the operating margin remains negative (adj. EBITDA margin still loss-making). Net: modestly positive but not a re-rating event.

Key operational catalysts landed cleanly vs the note’s highest-worry items: OCEAN-1 Phase 3 IPF initiation and LAKE RCC Phase 2b initiation both in Q2, plus runway reiterated into 2030 and no guidance change. The only likely upside surprise is confirmation of both trial initiations (reducing bear-case slippage risk), while the ILD FDA meeting timing remains within the expected window and no financial upside/downside was provided.

Headline revenue and adjusted EBITDA materially exceeded the note’s base-case (notably DBMG growth and margin expansion). Offsetting negatives were that Life Sciences/R2 remained weak and liquidity/capital-structure items still dominate, though no new DBMG-sale-process failure was indicated; overall this should be a modest positive reaction versus a market backdrop focused on balance-sheet catalysts.

Revenue came in below consensus and underlying gross margin (~27% ex tariff) declined further, matching the note’s bear arithmetic. EPS looks inline versus expectations on an underlying basis, and the FY guidance was reaffirmed, but the quarter’s profitability still depended on a one-time tariff recovery, limiting upside.

Operating momentum looked solid (US Y-CANTH net revenue and units beat the note’s base assumptions), and the credit facility is a meaningful non-dilutive runway extender. However, EPS/GAAP losses were materially worse than expected (milestone-free quarter impact) and the note’s bear case leaned on dilution/going-concern risk—while reduced, the headline earnings quality still disappoints. Overall reaction skews negative versus what the stock was likely positioned for (runway overhang not fully “solving” earnings/loss optics).

Revenue largely matches the pre-announced trough/base case (Atera pause still intact) and guidance remains broadly consistent with the note. Gross margin improved (headline aided by tariff refunds), but spatial instrument demand continues to look weak—so the beat is not strong enough to overcome a priced-for-premium setup; net reaction is modestly positive/near-median.

Revenue rebounded to $25.1M versus the pre-release window ($22.9M–$27.8M), so the headline looks largely expected/possibly slightly favorable. The key incremental positive is the narrowing adjusted loss alongside management reiterating the H2 self-sustaining narrative, supported by disclosed non-dilutive funding that reduces dilution risk; VS-7375 updates were not a primary earnings-surprise driver in the note.

Headline Q2 revenue landed only slightly above the in-guide “beat” bar implied by the note, while margins and efficiency improved (and FCF was positive in 1H). However, management guided FY revenue down to $273–275M (below consensus and below the note’s raise trigger), which likely outweighs the operating-income upgrade and AI engagement positives.

Q2 consolidated adjusted EBITDA ($21.3M) and FCF ($20.2M) were strong, but the key under-watch item was expected to be around ~$21M EBITDA with $90–100M FY guidance reaffirmed; management did not raise the FY EBITDA guide despite beating internal plans. With the stock positioned for a guide raise after a run-up, the lack of a raise plus mixed gross-profit dynamics limits upside reaction.

With no formal consensus/guidance, the main ‘beat/miss bar’ is the absolute AUM/flow outcome. Revenues and GAAP/Economic EPS are roughly inline to the note’s model, but AUM ended at $17.0B versus the note’s $19.8B base expectation, driven by large institutional outflows—an unanticipated and thesis-negative development. The ETF/platform progress and private co-invest commitments are positives, but they do not offset the magnitude/direction of outflows, especially in institutional value mandates.

Reported revenue beat consensus modestly, helped by favorable FX and a planned inventory reduction. However, underlying EPS fell absent tariff refunds ($0.17 benefit) and management maintained FY guidance while pointing to a sequential revenue decline in Q3 and another EPS dip vs Q2 (excluding the refund), which undermines the H2 “proof” implied by the setup; the key negative was more about the quality/timing of earnings power than the headline beat.

Underlying trends (ex-transition revenue growth, gross margin expansion) and 2026 financial framing largely matched the pre-release base case. The key tension is that FY26 revenue guides to the low end of the preview’s “raise needed” setup and Q2/Q3 EPS/mix looks less like an acceleration story; additionally, the company tempered expectations for Progyny Select’s 2027 contribution, reducing upside beyond what was hoped.

Q2 revenue/GBV/nights came in better than the note’s base path and management raised FY growth and the EBITDA margin floor. Despite Q3 revenue guidance also beating the ~4.55–4.65B consensus range, the implied EPS upside appears limited (EPS/tax benefit complexity) and Q3 EBITDA margin is guided to decline slightly—tempering enthusiasm for an outsized move.

EPS ($5.60) beat the $5.04 consensus and was higher than the note’s $5.25-base expectation, while the Q2 loss/combined ratios stayed within stated targets. The guidance framework (cession cut translating to large quarterly savings; Q3 ceded premiums ~$96M) was supportive, but Exzeo distribution timing was not reported, limiting the upside-to-perfection re-rate. Buyback completion and improved coverage add modest positive carry.

Q2 revenue was roughly in-line vs consensus, but results deteriorated on margins (EBITDA margin 33% vs ~37% expected/earlier trend) and, more importantly, FY26 guidance was cut meaningfully (revenue and especially adj. EBITDA) versus what the note considered fragile. Same-store comps also came in worse than the note’s critical -3% to -5% target, reinforcing that the H2 bridge is breaking and the strategic review offers no near-term resolution.

Q2 beats on revenue/EPS versus the note, but much of the EBITDA/margin lift is from non-recurring labor-disruption true-ups/reserve reversals; core margin is described as not repeating in Q3. While Q3 revenue guide is slightly above the May consensus band, the guide embeds limited strike revenue and the call adds new negatives (Kaiser in competitive RFP; international nurse growth lowered). Net: upside surprise is partially priced/guarded; reaction tilted negative on trajectory and guidance quality for the “core return to growth” thesis.

Revenue is roughly in line with the Street, and adjusted EPS beat the adjusted consensus. The key swing factor is margin expansion plus buybacks, but the note already framed BAQSIMI price/rebate drag and gross-margin risk—so the reaction should be modest rather than explosive; IMS and ongoing glucagon decline are not fully resolved versus the bear case.

Q2 results were roughly in-line on revenue and on adj. EBITDA versus the model range, with expanding margins and stronger material-handling backlog/bookings. The key scoring issue is guidance: management narrowed the FY26 adj. EBITDA range and cut the upper end, which prevents a clear upside re-rating despite improving demand signals and reaffirmed FCF.

Q2 beat on revenue and EPS (tariff-refund helped headline, but pro forma still beat) plus a full-year revenue and EPS raise. However, the pre-run setup (stock up ~19% into print) and the guidance mix—Q3 revenue guide that does not resolve the H2 ‘decline’ concern, plus ongoing negative product margin expectations—should cap the upside reaction versus a perfect beat-and-raise story.

Q2 headline revenue/EPS were not large enough upside given the pre-print framing, and adjusted EBITDA declined (margin pressure) versus the prior year. Most importantly, management reiterated FY26 revenue and EBITDA (no raise) despite the record fire-season setup in the note—consistent with the note’s base/bear asymmetry, which should pressure the stock on the guidance catalyst.

Headline revenue and EPS beat the note’s working consensus, aided by a small Mercury contingent-consideration adjustment; however, fair-value changes deteriorated (worse-than-prior-year drag), net charge-offs rose and management guided delinquency/charge-offs to rise next quarter. Also, acquisition costs are above plan (mail) and ROE is expected to revert toward ~20% rather than sustain the upside—driving a negative risk/reward despite the beat.

Q2 landed above guidance on revenue and at the high end for EBITDA, but margin still compressed (~200 bps) and the company guided Q3 revenue deceleration (and dealer spending remains cautious). The main offset is a more favorable FY margin outlook (compression only 50–150 bps vs the prior 1.5–2.5 pts), which likely prevents a downside reaction given the note’s focus on margin trajectory.

GTV, revenue, ads, and adjusted EBITDA all landed at/above the high bar in the pre-release note, but key margin optics worsened (GAAP gross profit % of GTV down) as publisher payments scaled. The bigger driver is the Q3 guidance philosophy change plus the widened ranges—sentiment is mixed rather than a clean upside beat, keeping the reaction near neutral-to-slightly positive.

The quarter broadly matches the pre-announced revenue/subscriber setup, but the key unreleased item (Adj. EBITDA/margin) underwhelmed: 49.7% margin and $173.5M EBITDA vs the note’s ~50.8%/($175–179M) expectations, implying worse cost takeout vs what the market penciled. Guidance/MBI financing was not updated and management declined questions—leaving balance-sheet uncertainty unresolved, which is a negative for a stock that already ran into the print and is priced as a capital-structure option.

Q2 revenue and Corporate crossed $60M with accelerating growth (a real fundamental positive vs the note’s risk case), while adjusted EBITDA was essentially flat and EPS was not clearly a beat versus the note’s ~$1.49 expectation. Guidance was reaffirmed (midpoint effectively still “no raise”), and margin guidance toward the lower end as hiring ramps limits upside—so the stock likely reacts modestly to moderately as the quarter is good but the key catalyst (a raise) did not arrive.

Q2 headline and profitability beat the thin consensus (adj. EPS $2.46 vs $2.35) while capacity reached full utilization and both Mt. Holly and Grundartangi restarts came ahead/near schedule. Most importantly, Q3 adj. EBITDA guide ($325–345M) clears the note’s base-case range and signals the H2 pricing/support the bear case worried about; the action is largely guided by fundamentals rather than a clear one-off. With implied options already pricing a ~9.5% move and downside skew, the setup points to a modestly positive print.

Q2 revenue is broadly inline with the low-end “credibility test” framing, and the major gross-margin and EBITDA upside is largely driven by the one-time IEEPA tariff refund and legal-expense adjustments (underlying profitability/segment trends are mixed: Adventure remains weak). Guidance action is a sharp FY EBITDA raise, but Q3 guide stays modest (sales $66–68M; adj. EBITDA ~$3M), limiting upside versus the market’s base case and raising “beat-and-stall” risk.

Underlying operating strength broadly held up even after removing tariff benefits (adjusted EBITDA above the top of guide; components GM still expanded despite revenue decline), and management raised FY2026 guidance with revenue and EBITDA midpoints implying real second-half strength. However, the headline GM beat is heavily driven by a large tariff-refund one-time item and CORSAIR PRO/AI contribution is largely delayed to late 2027+, limiting upside magnitude versus the already-high expectations and positioning.

Headlines are worse than the note assumed: Q2 revenue was only $1.4M vs an $11–13M expectation driven by Regeneron recognition timing, and opex rose with no offsetting operational upside. Milestones leaned toward late-2026/1H27 execution and cash runway was intact, but the quarter’s revenue/earnings mechanics look weaker than modeled, which is the key near-term read-through for the market.

Revenue of $49.0M beat the (already-stale/low) $48.21M consensus, but the bigger surprise versus the note’s downside risk was achieving positive adjusted EBITDA (+$0.4M) and improving FCF/operating cash. Guidance was reaffirmed, which is not a raise but aligns with the note’s base case of “nudge,” so overall the setup is positive but not a blowout.

Q1 revenue and adj. EBITDA beat the top end, and FY27 revenue guidance was raised (slightly) vs the note’s expectation of reaffirm/cut risk. However, FY27 EBITDA margin was lowered and Q2 implies ~flat YoY growth with “minimal AI revenue” in the quarter, plus gross margin continues to deteriorate—limiting upside on valuation-priced-for-growth expectations.

Q2 revenue and operating margin beat expectations, and paying users (+96K to 18.9M) were a key positive versus the note’s risk that a second quarter of user decline would invalidate Q1. Guidance was raised (opex margin +50bp; FCF +$15M; revenue guide raised modestly), and there was no evident undercutting deceleration beyond continued FX tailwinds and ongoing compute-driven gross pressure.

Q3 showed a clear EPS upside (>$2.12 consensus proxy) alongside record backlog and a higher book-to-bill, but the key mix/margin narrative was mixed because Utility Solutions EBIT margin fell on NRG weakness. FY26 EPS guidance was raised to $8.30–$8.40, which is modestly above the note’s ~$8.19 consensus, supporting a modestly positive print/reaction rather than a breakout.

Revenue and FY guidance were largely in line with the note, with another positive adjusted EBITDA and improved cash flow. However, the key underlying demand metrics (actives/orders) fell sharply year-over-year, gross margin declined (partly one-time) and CFO departure adds overhang—keeping the reaction slightly negative/neutral rather than a rerate.

Headline beat is modest on revenue but FCF guidance is raised sharply ($12–14M vs prior $6–9M). However, the stock was already priced for a validated inflection after a ~73% run; management also flagged Classic churn offset timing as unclear and Q2 new-platform growth was not yet forecasting-clear. Net: positive guidance/margin/FCF support, but the unproven timing and lack of clear revenue reacceleration pressure reaction.

GRND delivered a clear Q2 revenue beat and raised FY2026 guidance (revenue and adj. EBITDA), but the call also flagged growth deceleration in Q3/Q4 and an adjusted EBITDA margin around 42% (below the note’s ~43% expectation), limiting upside. With the stock already near the $18 take-private ceiling, the market likely treats this as a modestly positive guide-supported outcome rather than a major re-rating.

Headline Q2 growth and EPS beat, and FY26 revenue growth was raised to ~20%, which is above the Street’s ~14–16% framing. However, the note emphasized that the market is mainly trading the H2 deceleration and tariff step-up; while guidance is better, reported gross margin and EBITDA expansion are driven heavily by IEEPA tariff refunds (one-off), which tempers confidence in underlying sustainability. The release also introduced operational friction (Jordan supplier withhold release order), partially offsetting the upside.

GEN delivered stronger-than-expected Q1 growth and—most importantly—raised FY27 revenue and non-GAAP EPS guidance above an already pinned consensus midpoint. Mix did not deteriorate (Cyber Safety margin stayed ~61%, blended op margin stable), and the Trust/Engine momentum supports the new guide, driving a likely positive tape reaction.

Good Times turned positive (+0.6% SSS) and margins/Adj. EBITDA beat versus the setup; revenue came in roughly in line with the note’s ~$35.4M base. Offsetting items: Bad Daddy’s comps were still down (–2.3%) and there was no sign of the broader turnaround/bear-case reversal beyond Good Times.

Q2 revenue/adj. EBITDA landed at the high end, but the key market focus (FY26 like-for-like framing and the margin/profit trajectory) deteriorated: FY26 guidance was cut and Q3 guide stepped down sharply to revenue ~$55–56M with adj. EBITDA breakeven to $0.5M. Management also reaffirmed continued DOS→Ignite churn with only $22M of $52M at-risk ARR expected to be retained, and guided FY gross margin to fall below 50%. Debt-free is a real positive, but largely offsets rather than drives an upside rerating given the underlying 2H/exit decline.

Q2 headlines largely met the note’s bar (revenue modestly above the guidance midpoint; non-GAAP EPS in the expected ($0.05) range), so little incremental upside from the print. The key overhang remains the pre-release checklist: Q3 guide ($67–73M, midpoint $70M) is still below the ~$75M implied by FY consensus in the note, limiting re-rating despite constructive commentary on iND880/radar—net reaction close to median/fade.

Q2 revenue is roughly in-line with the pre-release expectation, with improving gross margin. However, management lowered FY26 revenue guidance to $355–361M (midpoint below the prior consensus range in the note), and reiterated the pressure from distributor inventory management—this is exactly the key ‘H2 hockey stick’ risk the note flagged. The raised FY adjusted EBITDA helps, but it doesn’t offset the lowered top-line path.

Headline revenue and profitability metrics beat, and Q2 comps (-2.8%) land inside the expected “slightly negative” zone. However, the cut to new clinic openings (22–26 vs prior 30–35) points to a weaker unit-growth trajectory, while the FY guide is reiterated—so the market focuses on the change in forward operating momentum, not just the maintained ranges.

Q2 delivered a clear beat on revenue (+7%) and especially EPS (~95%) with a strong 49% adjusted gross margin and improved concentration. However, FY26 guidance was reiterated at “40% or more” (not raised) and management cautioned sequential revenue risk from project mix, keeping the reaction mixed-positive versus the already bullish pre-print setup.

Headline gross margin and EPS benefited heavily from a one-time IEEPA tariff refund, so the underlying business was roughly in line with expectations. More importantly, Q3 guidance explicitly signals normalization (gross margin 35–37%, adjusted EBITDA 9–11%), which is a disappointment for a stock priced for the refund-driven recovery—putting emphasis on deceleration versus the narrative.

Q2 revenue ($202k) cleared the low consensus bar, and management added incremental positive proof-of-concept/customer wins. However, the key market focus—2H cash consumption and any quantified bridge to FY26—is not meaningfully improved (cash-use guidance reaffirmed with heavier 2H burn), while operating expenses rose and losses widened on the quarter, keeping the dilution/ATM and heavy 2H funding overhang in play.

Q2 revenue and products/gross margin beat the note, and JLWS timing commentary is a positive. However, Q3 revenue guidance (midpoint $68M) is below the note’s $80–86M placeholder and EBITDA guidance implies lower volumes/margin absorption (products GM sequentially down to 41.2% and guided lower), which is the key positioning risk for a stock already priced for perfection after a large run-up.

Financials were a mechanical BTC-driven loss with a worse revenue number, largely matching the note’s bear/base framework (so not a strong incremental shock). The key incremental support was the disclosed AI/HPC lease confidence/demand and the non-dilutive Long Ridge funding, but it was offset by another large underlying EPS/revenue miss versus what the note expected and by no clear step-up in contracted AI MW beyond what was already anticipated.

While Q3 revenue/EPS beat the already guidance-pinned consensus, the quality is mixed: Fraud & Identity SaaS was inflated by a one-time EMEA regulatory surge and Check verification growth was largely timing-driven with expectations that verification stays range-bound. Despite a guidance raise, underlying normalization risk (F&I high-teens/low-20s SaaS, Check run-rate range-bound) tempers upside versus the note’s bull/bear setup.

Headline revenue/consolidated adjusted EBITDA supported by higher PPA income than implied, while the key underlying operating momentum (NdPr sales/EBITDA improvement and implied margin expansion) aligns with the note’s base case rather than the bear. Q3 pricing/PPA setup appears broadly in line, and no incremental negative guidance shows up, limiting upside beyond a modest positive reaction.

The pre-release note flagged the Q3 guide and the rides growth rate (~259M) as the swing factor. While the release commentary confirms bookings+rider quality/mix improvements and driver economics, the provided facts do not include the consensus-critical reported rides figure (262M mentioned is above the ~259M watch level, but we can’t verify revenue/EPS or explicit Q3 guidance vs the note), limiting certainty; overall signals skew positive (premium mix, linked rides higher-value, Waymo on track).

Despite a record Q2 sales quarter and higher gross margin, management cut FY26 sales and especially EBITDA guidance, citing FX and a China slowdown (China -20%). With the pre-release note already flagging H2 deceleration risk and guide sensitivity, the explicit downward revision is incremental bad news and dominates the quarter.

Q2 results beat the (soft) consensus anchor and, more importantly, management raised FY26 adjusted EBITDA to $33–35M while keeping the revenue range intact. Incremental positives (no COVID GMP in-quarter, very strong gross margin expansion, continued customer additions) support the raise; the main offset is that non-COVID GMP/ModTill order timing still pushes out (GMP-grade ModTill orders into 2027), limiting upside narrative for further multiple expansion.

EPS beat was largely helped by one-time accounting/portfolio actions (including held-for-sale and fair-value treatment beginning Q3), while the call did not clearly raise the core FY26 EPS range that was the key debate in the pre-release note. Underlying credit looks a bit better (charge-offs/delinquencies improving) but management’s stance on the CECL/opex framework appears more credibility-sensitive than a clean guidance beat, keeping the reaction near median.

NET delivered a clear upside vs the pre-release yardstick on the two key acceleration metrics (revenue and DBNR), and also showed customer adds/paying customer growth that support the agentic monetization narrative. However, guidance implies some deceleration (36% growth in Q2 to ~31% in Q3) and margins/FCF show underlying pressure, limiting upside reaction versus a perfection-level beat-and-raise.

Q2 revenue and EPS materially beat expectations, driven by an all-time-high enterprise non-GAAP gross margin and improved enterprise contribution margin. However, the key risk—memory-driven 2H headwind—was not reduced; Q3 revenue guide ($165–175M) and non-GAAP op margin (–3% to 0%) remain consistent with the note’s base case, with Consumer margin still pressured.

Q2 revenue and EBITDA landed roughly where the note expected for a tough quarter (EBITDA beat on narrowing loss), but the key yardstick failed: management cut FY26 revenue guidance to $168–175M and cash to $30–32M, with Q3 EBITDA still negative. With delisting/ratio risk and the market focused on solvency/member inflection, the guidance reset is a meaningful negative versus the note’s base/bull thresholds.

Revenue and shipments cleared the high-end of the prior guide narrative, but the key trade—Q3 revenue guide—lands only modestly above the pre-release framework while upside flexibility is constrained by backlog. Normalized gross margin in the high-30s (due to a refund-driven headline GM) tempers the quality of the beat, likely leading to a muted-to-slightly positive reaction rather than a strong rerating.

Headlines look mixed versus the note’s expectation: revenue is roughly consistent with the “likely operationally similar” setup, but Ironton volume dipped q/q due to a planned turnaround (slightly negative) while management delivered an operational throughput milestone and reiterated improving branded utilization/cash-breakeven framing (positive). The only clear guidance improvement is the raised full-year project spend capex guidance, which helps the growth narrative but is not a pure earnings lever; margins/Adj. EBITDA remain deeply negative and widened vs prior year.

Q2 revenue/underlying sequential volume showed some recovery (net product revenue +18% QoQ; advanced wound care units +30%), but FY2026 guidance was sharply cut to $179–215M versus prior already-down trend ($270–310M) due to a slower-than-expected recovery, and cash fell to $46.8M with a wider EBITDA loss and ATM/dilution risk. The guide reset drives a negative reaction despite localized QoQ improvements.

Revenue and EPS beat consensus, and the FY revenue growth guide was reaffirmed at 20%. However, gross margin fell to 73% (below the 76%/77% backdrop the setup assumed would be supported), which offsets the upside from backlog growth and new high-value system contracts; net effect is a modest relief/rerating rather than a big re-rate.

Underlying profitability beat expectations: adjusted EBITDA was +$1.8M vs the note’s +$1.5M base, and management delivered margin expansion and continued sequential improvement (highest since Q3’23). Revenue came in modestly above the note, while guidance remained limited to reaffirming FCF-positive 2026, so reaction likely skews modestly positive rather than a breakout.

Collections were slightly above the company’s expectations and revenue surged largely due to a larger-than-modeled European ERC write-up; purchases stayed within the ongoing $1–1.3B target range and leverage declined toward mid-2x. Guidance was maintained, so the main upside is the stronger revenue/EPS optics versus an already “modestly unfavorable” setup in the note rather than a clear new operational inflection.

Revenue and EBITDA margin beat modestly/cleanly, but the key swing factor was the H2 bridge: management withdrew FCF guidance and sharply lowered FY26 revenue, EBITDA, and EPS. Demand tone deteriorated via the China inventory drawdown and a below-seasonal respiratory second-half assumption, which was the bear risk in the note.

Headline revenue beat the company’s prior “flat sequentially” expectation and gross margin improved materially (420 bps sequentially), but EPS comparability is muddied by the prior-year one-time tax benefit and management declined to provide formal FY guidance. With the note already flagging a headline-meets/underlying-margin-sensitive setup and no clear new bear-proofing, the net reaction is neutral-to-modestly positive despite the EPS outperformance.

Q4 revenue (+43% YoY) and, more importantly, adjusted EBITDA margin (11.1% vs expectations of a 10.6–11.6% step-up with the ~40M midpoint bar) came in at the high end, beating the market’s guide/margin thesis. Guidance for FY27 was also reaffirmed as strong-double-digit with continued EBITDA margin expansion (10.3%, +160 bps) and Q1 2027 supports the ramp, which should drive a positive reaction versus a note that emphasized the margin ramp as the key risk.

REAL delivered a clear upside quarter (revenue and especially Adj. EBITDA/margin) and—critically—raised FY26 GMV, revenue, and EBITDA, with Athena progress and a strengthening flywheel. This directly counters the pre-release “guide is the trade” bear trigger after TDUP’s H2 cut, so the reaction should be meaningfully positive despite the stock’s beaten-down state.

Headline results were roughly in line with the pre-release expectations ($5.1M revenue; non-GAAP EPS -$0.05), and the key binary items (C-DAC recognized in Q4 2026; elevated 2026 CapEx; CHIPS LOI not definitive with potential dilution) did not meaningfully improve vs the note’s base/bear framing. Gross margin improved (a positive), but cash declined and operating loss/burn widened with no clear upgrade to the fragile FY26 H2 bridge.

Q2 revenue/EPS beat consensus while adjusted EBITDA margin held at 32.1% (in line with the pre-guided ‘flat-to-down’ hurdle). The key incremental item is a guidance raise (revenue/EBITDA/FCF/EPS) driven by commodity prices rather than volume, plus underlying margin expansion expectations (60–70 bps H2/HY2 with Q3 flat). With the stock not priced for perfection and no major demand miss vs the note’s framework, reaction is modestly positive rather than strongly bullish.

Revenue came in modestly above consensus, and Q3 gross margin was guided flat-to-slightly up, but gross profit dollars missed the note’s key $11.0M+ check (gross margin fell to 16.3% vs 18.5% a year ago) and liquidity remains tight (only ~$1M cash). The expected deleveraging supports the stock, but the margin/mix softness offsets it, leading to a roughly median reaction.

The major surprise was a sharp FY26 revenue guidance cut to $9–10M (from ~$26M) tied to removal of the expected Uber ramp; this resets the core bull case the note said the market already underwrote. Q2 revenue was only modestly sequential, with gross margin still deeply negative, so the headline improvement is outweighed by the bearish guide and Uber non-renewal risk.

Underlying demand (GMV +37.9%) and engagement metrics beat the already-constructive seasonal setup in the note, while credit/risk stays within the guided provision band (2.5–3% FY). Guidance was raised to revenue growth +35% and adj. EPS $5.25 (above the note’s $5.10 bar), which should offset valuation overhang; marketing is flagged as a one-time test as expected.

Q2 cleared the key Engine Services credibility tests (record 14.4% margin; LEAP/CFM56 profitability) and raised FY revenue/EBITDA/EPS. However, the release also flagged CRS margin compression to 26.3% and military delays, which partly offsets the headline strength—so the reaction is only modestly positive versus a stock already positioned for H2 recovery in the pre-note.

Q2 revenue was roughly in line and early sequential comps stabilized briefly, but underlying demand weakened (SSS –6.2%) and margins/EBITDA deteriorated sharply. The key swing is the full-year guide cut (comp, restaurant margin, and especially adjusted EBITDA) that re-anchors growth to a much worse outcome than consensus expected, despite the stock being positioned for a trough.

Q2 was essentially in line on revenue ($17.8M vs $18.0M guide midpoint and $17.9M consensus) but non-GAAP operating profit was achieved and positive ($0.635M vs near-breakeven expectation). However, Q3 revenue guidance implies downside to the feared inflection (midpoint ~$17M vs the note’s expectation of ~$19M+ to sustain the FY26 run-rate), tempering the upside.

The note already expected a largely mechanical optics-heavy quarter with ~-$20M digital-asset/receivable MTM losses and cash pressure; reported revenue was higher than the pre-release model while the net loss is dominated by non-cash digital losses that were largely in-scope. However, cash remained very low ($3.1M vs $5M modeled) and the quarter confirmed further Bluefin-related losses, both negative for the key runway/accumulation narrative; no clear offsetting, explicitly better-than-feared guidance was provided in the facts.

Reported EPS of $0.48 missed consensus ($0.51–0.52), though fee-related earnings beat (FRE $106M; 39% FRE margin vs implied ~38–39% base case). The key upside was a record $2.8B of Private Wealth subscriptions and best-ever 12-month period, partially offset by disclosed next-quarter managed account expirations and public-market volatility expectations from SPRING lockups/performance realization timing. Net reaction is modestly positive given the flow/asset-quality surprises vs a headline EPS disappointment and no clear guidance action provided.

Q4 revenue and cloud growth beat the note’s pre-announced guidance optics, but the bigger question—FY27 growth/financial trajectory—did not clearly improve versus what was already expected. Subscription ARR deceleration and DX acquisition headwind (plus GAAP margin weakness) temper the upside, so reaction is mildly negative/near-median despite better cloud execution.

Headline EPS and revenue beat were largely driven by the $6.9M Dedeaux JV land sale, which the pre-release note already flagged as the key variable—so the beat is not much of a surprise. However, liquidity still declined to ~$79M (worse than the note’s base calibration), and management’s water/capital narrative doesn’t fully offset the cash-burn risk; net reaction is modestly positive rather than strong.

Q2 revenue and EPS materially missed a setup that already assumed little cushion (and Q3 guide was the key). The Q3 revenue guide of at least $650M implies a sharp Y/Y decline and EBITDA that is far below what was required in the note’s base/bull cases. Although international/EMEA-APAC growth and CTV strength are positives, the demand tone and margin contraction plus leadership/guidance reset risk drive a downside-biased reaction.

Revenue was ~in-line with the pre-announced/“stale” consensus that looked ~3% too high, and guidance for FY26 adj. EBITDA ($95–$100M) was reiterated. However, underlying profitability softened (Q2 adj. EBITDA margin 13% vs 14.4% last year) and I&A consulting bookings were weaker, increasing doubts about achieving a stronger H2 implied ramp versus what the guide requires.

Q2 headline results beat consensus and Twilio raised FY organic and non-GAAP op income/FCF guidance. However, gross margin declined due to carrier pass-through pressure, and management guided Q3 organic (11–12%) with explicit caution that prior 5%+ beats likely won’t persist—reducing the upside vs an already-strongly-expected setup for this stock.

Revenue and comps landed around the note’s base, but EPS missed the note’s $1.90 whisper/upper consensus mix and restaurant margin fell to 16.4% (below the note’s ~16.5–16.3 base/bull band). Commodity inflation guidance was cut to ~5% (good), but margin compression plus mild Q4 same-store headwinds (holiday/calendar) likely drives a negative tape given the stock’s priced-for-perfection setup.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA beat the pre-release expectations, and PAL declined less than feared. However, adjusted EBITDA still fell y/y and Q3 guidance caps upside with only $70–75M (pressuring the FY sustainability debate), while buybacks were paused and RR&O remained weak—so the market reaction is modest/near-median.

Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA landed near the high end of guide, but the key market lever—FY adjusted EBITDA—was raised (midpoint above the pre-release bull/base framing), supporting continued cost/run-rate credibility. Underlying medical cost trend is slightly better than the 5.2% assumption and Prospect synergies track high end; no meaningful downside was disclosed beyond minor CMS billing anomaly effects.

Q2 delivered well ahead of the note’s consensus bar (net revenue and adjusted EPS beats) and—more importantly—management raised full-year FY26 guidance across net revenue, adj. EBITDA, and adj. EPS. The margin expansion (28.2% adj. EBITDA margin) also supports the H2 ramp narrative, reducing the key execution/timing risk despite slightly lower gross margin from mix.

Top-line and adjusted EPS/EBITDA beat the pre-release framing, but the market’s core watchpoint (EBITDA margin and the implied H2 back-half bridge) moved the wrong way: margin fell to 37.2% despite the revenue strength. Guidance was raised (revenue/EBITDA) and management kept Q3/Q4 margin expansion targets, tempering the downside, but the margin deterioration offsets the revenue beat for next-day reaction.

Headline Q2 revenue and EPS beat consensus, and the company lifted the full-year revenue midpoint (floor raised).
