However, the most important forward signal—shipments vs. revenue—slightly deteriorated (0.96x vs 1.04x in Q1) and the guidance raise looks largely like flowing through the Q2 beat with the ceiling unchanged, plus management flagged component supply/longer lead times for 2H. Net: modestly positive but not a “beat-and-raise” blowout given what was already expected and the forward constraints.

Q2 adjusted EPS ($1.75) was roughly inline vs the note’s $1.77 adjusted consensus, but underlying tone was negative (Japan benefit ratio 64%—above the note’s ~$61.7 setup and below the implied full-year guide range) while the company also cut/softened the U.S. net earned premium growth outlook. Guidance action is only partially positive (Japan benefit ratio guided to the high end of 60–63% rather than mid), which isn’t enough to offset margin pressure in a stock already priced for stability/option-implied modest moves.

Q2 headline growth/EBITDA were strong, and early gout rep productivity indicators were better than implied. However, the key credibility item in the note—Cortrophin phasing/guide—was a downside guide action (full-year Cortrophin Gel revenue cut) while gross margin also declined, and Q3 EBITDA was guided to decline sequentially. That undercuts the H2 ramp confidence that drove the bullish setup, so reaction is likely negative despite a decent quarter.

Because the deal was signed pre-print, consensus anchor/dispersion is the yardstick but the earnings metrics were effectively secondary to completion risk. The company also withdrew guidance as expected for the transaction. Underlying fundamentals showed margin compression (gross and S&I), and the cash/FCF profile remains weak, which is directionally negative, but not surprising given the note’s framing—hence a modestly positive, neutral-to-slightly-constructive reaction driven by confirmatory operating results rather than new upside.

Q2 delivered upside vs the pre-set sequential bar (revenue above the implied flat guidance) and, more importantly, management raised FY revenue and adj. EBITDA guidance plus lifted levered FCF guidance. With ACV bookings already >2025 and pipeline expansion, the report is better than what the note’s base/bear asymmetry was guarding against (especially FCF/liquidity).

Q3 revenue and EPS came in above the (loosely held) consensus, and full-year adj. operating margin and adj. EPS were raised. However, underlying profitability remained weak (margin down sharply Y/Y), U.S. revenue fell ~25% Y/Y with mix/timing caveats, and the Q4 implied revenue (~$270M) is slightly below Street expectations—so the raise looks more like partial offset than a clear operational turn.

Headline results were better than the pre-release base-case: revenue came in above the $250–255M framework and adjusted EBITDA losses narrowed versus expectations. Cash increased to $105M at quarter-end (and $121M by July), which helps address the primary balance-sheet concern, supporting a mildly positive reaction despite ongoing six-month EBITDA cash-burn pressure.

Despite Q2 adjusted EBITDA landing at the high end and positive free cash flow, revenue/billings declined and the update still left unresolved H2 acceleration proof. Importantly, Q3 guide calls for negative FCF, reinforcing the steep ramp risk highlighted in the note; the maintained FY revenue/EBITDA ranges were largely expected, so the incremental positives (organic channel recovery, AI content/SEO, July mid-single-digit growth) only partially offset the top-line weakness.

Headline EPS beat is driven by a one-time IEPA tariff refund, but underlying gross margin strength and a record backlog add genuine upside. Revenue is roughly in line with the note’s base-case, while communication systems growth and backlog momentum after quarter-end support the long thesis.

Headline Q2 sales beat and full-year sales guidance was raised, but the EPS beat is heavily driven by a one-time $15.6M tariff refund and underlying gross margin strength is not sustained (Q3 GM ~40.8% vs prior expectations and full-year GM ~40.6%, with Q4 seasonality/timing concerns). The demand/backlog datapoints are solid, yet the guidance/margin trajectory is less favorable for a stock already near highs, keeping the reaction muted-to-negative.

Q1 net bookings came in modestly above the top of guided range (~$1.39B vs $1.32–$1.37B) with RCS declining only ~1% (better than the ~3% decline guided). However, management maintained FY27 bookings ($8.0–$8.2B) and reiterated the unchanged GTA VI date (expected). The notable downside is Q2 guidance ($1.62–$1.67B) implying deceleration, plus a weaker cost/margin picture from the $43M impairment.

Q2 revenue beat consensus ($45.4M vs ~$44.0M) with high-single-digit case growth and rising adoption (LAPApalsty users using new bunion systems to ~40% from 35%). However, gross margin slipped to 78.5% and the EPS metric wasn’t provided in the facts. The key item is a small FY26 revenue guide raise to $204–$212M (low end slightly higher, effectively a mild improvement vs the prior range), alongside better FY26 adjusted EBITDA loss guidance (to -$3 to -$5M), which supports a modestly positive reaction rather than a rerating given the still-delicate H2/Q4 math.

EPS of $2.00 beat the $1.92–$1.95 implied bogey, and underwriting margin improved (AYCR 88.1%, +30 bps). However, management also flagged ongoing soft/inadequate pricing (intl and energy down) and retention cut in Lexington, which limits any upside beyond a modest positive reaction; guidance was not meaningfully changed vs what was expected in the note.

Quarterly EPS landed roughly in the expected band, but management delivered the key Pathway detail (commitments, ownership structure) and upgraded the 2024–28 capital trajectory while reaffirming 2028 EPS. The main offset is the modest Q2 EPS growth (1% YoY) due to dilution and the deferred 2027–2031 guidance, keeping upside more mixed for the next few quarters.

Headline Q2 EBITDA ($115M) was below the publish-consensus but management delivered the key ‘whisper’ bar and—most importantly—maintained FY26 revenue and EBITDA ($700–900M). Demand/handle and CAC improved and Predictions spend appears already embedded, offsetting the quarter’s outcome-noise/overhang; downside risk was more about a guide cut than the quarter.

Q3 revenue came slightly light vs the note’s consensus, though EPS beat. The key negative surprise is that FY26 revenue guidance was cut again (to $216–221M), and FY27 growth was lowered to mid-single digits, reinforcing the bear case of a second guidance revision and weaker visibility—despite some margin improvement in Q3 and an unchanged-ish EBITDA trend.

Headline GAAP loss improved versus last year and adjusted loss was slightly better, but this largely fits the note’s base case. Key however: leverage and PREPA gross par trends were favorable (capital improving), yet the PREPA settlement overhang remains (rejection / lower recoveries), and underlying drivers are still heavily legal/holdco-capital dependent. Net: modestly positive at most, not a clear re-rate.

Q2 EPS and revenue handily beat the note’s ~$0.70/$3.90B expectations, and new awards/backlog surged (supporting a positive demand narrative). However, the key credibility item—back-half EBITDA ramp—was weakened by revised FY adjusted EBITDA guidance (to $500–$525M vs the note’s ~$525–$560M context), and segment profitability was partly noisy/charge-driven (Urban FX/subcontractor losses) while 2H margins were guided to diminish.

EPS (diluted $1.05) beat the $0.95 consensus, helped by favorable prior-year reserve development, but management reaffirmed full-year EPS $2.20–$2.90 versus expectations for a likely upward narrowing at this 52-week-high setup. Underlying loss ratio worsened (43.1% vs 38.7%), and management flagged a softening competitive market with moderation in NY growth into 2H, both weighing on the stock despite strong growth and improved reported combined ratio.

RPID beat revenue and delivered a record 15% gross margin with stronger recurring/consumables, and it raised validation guidance to at least 27 (better than the note’s base). However, net loss widened and cash fell to ~$20M with financing dependence (Trinity + warrants), keeping downside risk alive even with expected lower H2 burn.

Revenue/EPS were effectively expected to remain de minimis and loss-heavy for a pre-revenue developer. The key actionable surprise was the raised FY2026 operating cash use and capex guidance (accelerated Aurora-INL spending) which is directionally positive for execution, but the stock also carried the recent “sell-the-news” Groves criticality narrative and the call did not provide a binding PPA or near-term revenue-date beyond early-2027 isotope timing—so overall reaction is likely muted-to-mixed rather than a clear beat/raise rally.

Quarterly adj. EPS and operating income beat guidance, but the print is heavily driven by a large IEEPA tariff-refund benefit. The bigger issue versus expectations is the guidance downgrade for FY27 revenue (mid-single-digit decline) alongside a sharp deterioration in traffic/demand (esp. NA/APAC), plus a marketing-spend reset, which likely outweighs the headline margin beat for the next-day reaction.

Q2 reflected weaker demand (traffic down and check gains not offset), with adjusted EPS $0.18 missing consensus. Most importantly, management withdrew full-year 2026 outlook—worse than the note’s base case of reaffirm/narrowing—while also signaling continued traffic headwinds and margin pressure from commodity/labor inflation, driving a likely negative repricing.

Headline read-through is meaningfully better than the note’s base (recovery narrative intact): adjusted EBITDA with tax attributes is $175M and management guided a stronger SAF ramp/ongoing deleveraging. While Montana Renewables EBITDA was weak near the note’s concern (offline), guidance suggests accelerating cash/EBITDA power in H2/H3. With the stock already up strongly YTD, reaction is positive but not explosive.

P&L numbers were largely in line on revenue and roughly aligned on underlying margin, while adjusted EPS beat was primarily driven by aggressive buybacks rather than better operating demand. Guidance (low-to-mid single-digit revenue decline with modest margin improvement in Q3, slightly down EBITDA margin in Q4) fits the pre-release setup, limiting upside.

Headline EPS/revenue surprise can’t be cleanly scored (not provided in the facts). The key scoreboard (Adj. EBITDA) came in near the note’s ~$80–85M expectation band but with underlying Q2 YoY decline; management reaffirmed full-year EBITDA ($245–$265M) and raised the full-year retail fuel margin outlook to $0.455–$0.475, partially offset by commentary that 2H implies lower YoY EBITDA due to consumer and fuel-price uncertainty.

Q2 revenue beat consensus with sales volumes above the guidance midpoint, but adjusted EPS was effectively inline (headline supported by non-cash/unrealized hedge gains). Guidance was largely maintained (capex unchanged) with Q3 production up and NRI sales in line with the pre-release framing; the meaningful push/pull was delivery vs the expected hedge/timing risks, leading to a near-median reaction.

Q2 beat on both revenue and adjusted EPS with clear margin expansion (23.3% vs expected ~21.4%); visits and RPV were also better than the note’s base/bear sensitivities. The key incremental positive is the full-year guidance raise (EBITDA/FCF) above consensus, not just a reaffirmation. With the stock not described as deeply beaten down and the note calling a beat-and-raise only in the bull case, reaction is positive but not “perfect.”

MATW cut full-year adjusted EBITDA guidance to $158–162M (below the note’s ≥$180M bar), with industrial technology still loss-making and memorialization margin pressured by input costs. While Propelis EBITDA exit timing remains favorable (sale process within 12 months), the credibility hit from the guide cut should drive a negative reaction.

Quarterly operational/cash flow momentum (record gas volumes, improved realized prices, FCF $159m) supports the base-case framing from the note, and full-year adjusted EBITDA/FCF and sustaining capital were effectively reiterated rather than meaningfully raised. With the pre-disclosed quarter and wide EPS consensus dispersion largely tied to hedge mark-to-market, the main upside is execution and buyback/FCF coverage, but no clear guidance beat limits the upside reaction.

Headline Q3 EPS ($0.05) missed consensus, but more importantly the FY26 EPS range was narrowed to $1.29–$1.32 versus the note’s top-end $1.31–$1.37 expectation; the incremental annual rate-case settlement (3.85M vs 4.3M sought) and the higher refi interest burden also keep the FY27 risk elevated. While margin support is coming from interim rate increases, the call’s key swing item (LNG recovery timeline/cost quantification) remains adverse versus what the market was bracketing.

Q3 revenue growth and Home & Garden were stronger than expected, but the quality of EPS is poor: underlying adjusted EPS excluding tariff refunds fell sharply (0.89 ex-refunds vs prior-year), and management signaled Q4 headwinds (GPC tough comps; H&G elevated retailer inventories and late-season weather). Guidance for FY26 EBITDA was raised (excluding tariff refunds), but with risky underlying EPS/margin signals and a weaker Q4 setup, the net reaction is negative.

The pre-release note expected POST to largely defend FY26 with a key Q3 determinant (foodservice run-rate / PCB stabilization). While management offered a normalized foodservice run-rate step-down that supports mean reversion, FY2027 framing is only “roughly flat” EBITDA and highlights continued pressure factors (refrigerated retail headwinds and pricing lag vs inflation), which is a negative implication for the growth path the market wants—despite the stock being near washed-out levels.

Despite a raised transformation cost-savings run-rate target, the quarter missed on underlying momentum (local distribution down sharply on blackout impact; Networks profit collapsed) and EPS was dragged down by a very large noncash goodwill/intangible impairment plus deterioration in leverage (to 4.9x). Political outlook and net distribution revenue guidance are still constructive, but the combination of weak segment profits, higher restructuring costs, and leverage adds downside pressure versus what the note expected.

Q2 revenue was essentially in-line, but EPS and profitability missed sharply (EBITDA down to $32M). While the company confirmed 45Q/FCF-related items and ammonia volume growth, the key incremental negatives versus the note were (1) Q2/underlying margin softness (lower EBITDA), (2) weaker spring plant-nutrient volume, and (3) explicit guidance for a larger-than-historical Q3 plant-nutrient earnings headwind—reinforcing the bear-case path despite no major guide cut.

North America and U.S./Nugget trends were solid (record Q2 revenue and adjusted EBITDA; expanding U.S. margins), and debt metrics improved (net leverage 6.5x; CapEx down). However, Poland was a clear underperformance versus the note’s base thesis (Rosa closure/startup losses and ~normalized $8M vs prior peak), with no disclosed Poland sale/LOI—limiting upside and keeping reaction close to median.

Revenue and EBITDA level beat consensus, and landfill volumes/pricing were strong, but adjusted EBITDA margin fell (fuel + Resource Solutions) and the key de-risking guidance point for the base business (FY adjusted EBITDA) was reaffirmed while full-year revenue was lifted mainly via fuel recovery fees. With the market focused on an EBITDA guide raise/volume validation, the reaffirmation and margin compression likely drive a muted-to-negative reaction.

Q3 results were significantly worse than the pre-release base case (revenue and EPS both materially missed) with Smart Water the main drag. Although the company highlighted a ~$10.8M Navy award and claimed PRM contract value is unchanged (timing delay only), management also pushed PRM revenue recognition into the later window (Q3–Q4 FY27), reinforcing the cash/margin-burn overhang flagged in the note. Net: downside reaction consistent with a “burn + margin/cash path” disappointment rather than an operational inflection.

Q2 revenue landed essentially in line with the two-point consensus, while adjusted EPS and (headline) adjusted EBITDA/FCF improved versus expectations. Guidance was reaffirmed (no change vs the note), but management flagged elevated CapEx from ClearPath stabilizer investment that could weigh on credibility of the upper-end FCF ramp—limiting upside.

Q2 revenue and orders beat expectations, and management raised FY26 net sales/EBITDA/FCF. However, the tariff-refund benefit (explicitly $12M in Q2 and ~$16M in FY EBITDA) means some of the upside is not purely underlying, which limits the magnitude of the positive reaction versus a pre-release setup that worried about the H2 tariff/margin bridge.

Underlying results deteriorated sharply: operating EBITDA swung to -$21M versus the note’s expectation of modestly positive/slightly recovering EBITDA and liquidity relief. Liquidity fell to ~$192M (below the note’s relief threshold) and management disclosed going-concern plus likely Q4 leverage-ratio breach, reinforcing the balance-sheet bear case; fiber costs stayed elevated into Q3, confirming the key suspected negative.

Underlying profitability appears supported by favorable economic claims and stronger-than-planned investment income, but the quarter also leaned on material one-time/other items, and—most importantly—deployment remains below the previously discussed ~$1.5B annual pace (only $158M this quarter). With the stock near 52-week highs and consensus already set, the primary setup is more ‘less-bad than bear’ than a durability catalyst.

Fiber/Array build metrics and guidance were meaningfully better than the note’s key “fiber address bogey,” including a large 50k raise to fiber addresses and improved address delivery; Array also raised guidance and confirmed monetization progress. Offsetting negatives were a telecom revenue guide cut and higher consolidated CapEx (implying margin/FCF pressure), plus no Q2 buybacks. Net: constructive but not a “blowout,” given the under-the-hood telecom revenue softness and cash burn despite better units.

Q2 adjusted EBITDA of $1.767B beat the note’s $1.76–$1.79B “base” expectation only marginally/inline-to-slight-beat, but guidance was a full reaffirm at $6.8B–$7.6B and, crucially, management said the 2027 midpoint is trending toward the lower end on weaker ERCOT forward curves—an explicit narrative risk that the market was already primed to trade. Add the lack of upgrades (2027 not raised) and the reaffirm framing, and reaction skews muted-to-negative despite strong segment momentum.

Underlying Q3 showed solid top-line growth, but EBITDA margin came in below the note’s ~17.0% bar (16.3% vs ~17.0%), which matters for the FY bridge. The company still raised FY26 revenue and EBITDA ranges and delivered record backlog with high contract coverage, offsetting the margin concern; given the stock had already sold off meaningfully, the net reaction is mildly positive rather than a rerating surge.

Revenue and EPS landed essentially where the (thin/dispersion) consensus expected (~$217M, ~$4.75), with no formal guidance. The key improvement was cost relief from contract renegotiation (pay-on-collected) and the new federal IDR rule, plus stronger visits (+9.6%) and solid cash/EBITDA—offset by continued dependence on IDR mechanics, so the reaction is modestly positive rather than a re-rate.

The print showed a strong underlying EBITDA/margin step-up (Q2 adj. EBITDA $60M; NA margin 15% vs. 10%) and management reaffirmed a constructive 2H price/mix benefit ($75–85M) versus the note’s base case. However, the new tariffs worsened the previously expected footprint/tariff import tailwind ($20M eliminated) and guided North America volumes down in 2H due to Riverdale losses and a longer Eastover outage—two negatives not fully anticipated as upside offsets. Overall: modestly positive reaction given the operational improvement, offset by softer volume/outlook risk.

Despite a modest GAAP EPS improvement, adjusted EBITDAX and guidance credibility deteriorated versus what the note feared: LOE ran even higher (Q2 $10.27/BOE; up to $8.25-$9.25) and production was below the implied base case. The Q3/Q4 gas-swing narrative is helpful, but the further LOE guidance raise is a key negative for the capital-efficiency pivot, likely driving a down-to-middling reaction.

Reported revenue and adjusted EBITDA/EPS came in stronger than the pre-print setup, and management raised full-year 2026 guidance (EBITDA and discretionary cash flow) while also improving Compression gross margin and maintaining strong utilization. The key remaining variable—power contracted demand versus procured supply—was supported by 33M of power revenue and improved power ramp visibility (1.8 GW available by 2030, 1 GW Baker Hughes supply), limiting downside despite some lingering conversion risk.

Q2 revenue and, more importantly, adjusted EBITDA ($214M) came in above the note’s implied ~$210M and political revenue ($83M) materially exceeded the $60–70M setup. Importantly, Q3 political guidance ($165–185M) keeps the political payoff on track rather than deferring it, which should drive a modestly positive reaction despite leverage/deleveraging being slightly less than initially modeled.

Headline profitability is flattered by ~$15M tariff refunds (management says no further meaningful refunds), and underlying gross margin would have been modestly lower vs prior year despite reported expansion. Revenue growth is positive but the quarter guidance substitute (cost/tariff absorption and inventory/cash implications) skews toward a less durable recovery, with weak Camping/Watercraft cited—consistent with the base-to-bear setup in the note.

Operational momentum (RevPAR ex-Royal Palm nearly +7%, EBITDA margin up ~80 bps, adjusted FFO $0.70) appears solid versus the note’s “near-certain” setup. However, the note’s core concern was Park’s under-capture of the Miami World Cup window and a likely “cheap for a reason” narrative; while the company raised FY guidance and provided stronger group growth, there was also a stated second-half hit from non-core dispositions and no clear confirmation that the Royal Palm program will immediately erase the previously flagged earnings drag. Net: a beat-and-raise, but not a decisive narrative re-rating, leading to below-median reaction.

EPS was slightly below the $0.35 ongoing expectation ($0.33 reported), but guidance was reaffirmed at $1.90–$1.98 (midpoint $1.94) and management highlighted continued strength in PA signed/committed data center activity and new load pipeline/possible CPCN filing—supporting the already-base-case narrative despite the modest EPS miss.

Q2 delivered a modest upside to consensus on both revenue and adjusted EPS, with adjusted EBITDA margin landing slightly above the note’s fragile ~20.6% bar (20.7%). However, the key undercurrent is that after the margin-friendly Q2, guidance tightened slightly on EBITDA margin (top end cut) and aftermarket remains flat with ongoing Middle East cost pressure—limiting the upside to a muted-to-modestly positive reaction rather than a true re-rate.

Q2 delivered strong operating momentum with a clear swing to positive adjusted EBITDA and a second quarter in a row. More importantly, FY2026 guidance was raised again (revenue growth now >90% and adj. EBITDA margin >10%), exceeding the note’s main yardstick (>60% growth and FY-positive adj. EBITDA) rather than merely confirming it.

Headline net income/EPS were boosted by a large noncash Maui wildfire liability remeasurement, but underlying (core) EPS declined year over year and management highlighted structural O&M headwinds and a full-year outlook that includes a net loss from PIMs/SSMs plus the maximum fuel-cost penalty. Despite a proposed base rate increase and an improved credit trajectory (rating upgrades), the deterioration in underlying earnings and cash cost pressures likely drove a negative-to-mildly negative reaction versus what options typically price for such a release.
